questions.sample: Morning is better, because it's cooler. Do I need to book in advance?
questions.sample_ko: 시원하니까 오전이 좋아요. 미리 예약해야 하나요?

questions.q: Just sign here. Do you have everything you need, like a hat and sunscreen?
questions.q_ko: 여기에 서명만 하세요. 모자나 선크림 같은 필요한 건 다 있으세요?
questions.sample: Actually, I forgot my sunscreen at home.

questions.q: We sell some at the front desk. What else do you like to do on vacation?
questions.q_ko: 프런트에서 팔아요. 휴가 때 또 뭘 하는 걸 좋아하세요?
questions.sample: I like reading by the pool and eating fresh fruit.
questions.sample_ko: 수영장 옆에서 책 읽고 신선한 과일 먹는 걸 좋아해요.

closing: Sounds relaxing! See you at the surf lesson tomorrow morning.
closing_ko: 편안하겠네요! 내일 아침 서핑 수업에서 만나요.

title: Hiking Trail
situation_ko: 국립공원 입구에서 레인저에게 등산 코스를 물어요.

key_phrases.text: Which trail is good for beginners?
How long does it take to reach the top?

questions.q: Hi! Planning to hike today?
questions.sample: Yes, but I'm not very experienced. Which trail is good for beginners?
questions.sample_ko: 네, 그런데 경험이 많지 않아요. 초보자에게 좋은 코스는 어디예요?

questions.q: Try the Lake Loop. It's easy and has great views. How much time do you have?
questions.q_ko: 레이크 루프를 가 보세요. 쉽고 경치가 좋아요. 시간은 얼마나 있으세요?
questions.sample: About four hours. How long does it take to reach the top?

questions.q: Around two hours up. Did you bring enough water and snacks?
questions.q_ko: 올라가는 데 2시간쯤 걸려요. 물과 간식은 충분히 챙기셨어요?
questions.sample: I have one bottle. Should I bring extra water?
questions.sample_ko: 한 병 있어요. 물을 더 가져가야 할까요?

questions.q: Yes, definitely. It gets hot after noon. Are you hiking alone?
questions.q_ko: 네, 꼭이요. 정오가 지나면 더워져요. 혼자 등산하세요?
questions.sample: I'm with my coworker. We wanted to get out of the office.

questions.q: That's a great idea! Have you ever seen wild animals on a hike?
questions.q_ko: 좋은 생각이에요! 등산하다가 야생 동물을 본 적 있으세요?
questions.sample: Once I saw a deer in the mountains. It was beautiful.

closing: You might see one today! Stay on the trail and have a safe hike.
closing_ko: 오늘도 볼지 몰라요! 길을 벗어나지 말고 안전하게 다녀오세요.

title: Late Checkout Request
situation_ko: 비행기 시간 때문에 호텔에 늦은 체크아웃을 부탁해요.

key_phrases.text: My flight is in the evening.

questions.q: Good morning! Is everything OK with your room?
questions.sample: Yes, it's great. I have a question, though. Could I check out later today?
questions.sample_ko: 네, 좋아요. 그런데 질문이 있어요. 오늘 체크아웃을 늦게 해도 될까요?

questions.q: Standard checkout is at eleven. What time would you like?
questions.sample: Around three, if possible. My flight is in the evening.

questions.q: We can do two o'clock for a small fee. Would that work?
questions.sample: Two o'clock is fine. How much is the fee?

questions.q: It's twenty dollars. Is there anything else you need?
questions.sample: Yes, can you keep my luggage after I check out?
questions.sample_ko: 네, 체크아웃 후에 짐을 맡아 주실 수 있어요?

questions.q: Of course. What did you enjoy most about your stay?
questions.q_ko: 물론이죠. 머무는 동안 가장 좋았던 게 뭐예요?
questions.sample: The view from my room was amazing, and the staff were so kind.
questions.sample_ko: 방에서 보는 경치가 멋졌고 직원들도 아주 친절했어요.

closing: We're so glad. Thank you for staying with us. Safe travels home!
closing_ko: 정말 기뻐요. 저희 호텔에 묵어 주셔서 감사해요. 안전하게 귀가하세요!

title: Staying in a Hostel
situation_ko: 호스텔에서 여러 명이 쓰는 도미토리 방에 대해 이야기해요.
user_role: A backpacker staying in a hostel

key_phrases.text: I booked a bed in a dorm room.
Is there a locker for my bag?
Where can I meet other travelers?
key_phrases.ko: 다른 여행자들은 어디서 만날 수 있어요?

questions.q: Hey there! Welcome to the hostel. Do you have a booking?
questions.q_ko: 안녕하세요! 호스텔에 오신 걸 환영해요. 예약하셨어요?
questions.sample: Yes, I booked a bed in a dorm room for three nights.

questions.q: Found it. You're on the bottom bunk in room six. Is that OK?
questions.sample: That's perfect. Is there a locker for my bag?

questions.q: Yes, under your bed. Bring your own lock. Have you stayed in a hostel before?
questions.q_ko: 네, 침대 아래에 있어요. 자물쇠는 직접 가져오세요. 호스텔에 묵어 본 적 있어요?
questions.sample: Yes, a few times in Europe. I like meeting people from different countries.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 유럽에서 몇 번요. 다양한 나라 사람들을 만나는 게 좋아요.

questions.q: Me too! Are you traveling for a long time?
questions.sample: I'm traveling for a month, mostly by train.
questions.sample_ko: 한 달 동안 주로 기차로 여행해요.

questions.q: That sounds amazing. Is there anything you'd like to know about the area?
questions.q_ko: 멋지네요. 이 지역에 대해 궁금한 게 있어요?
questions.sample: Yes, where can I meet other travelers tonight?
questions.sample_ko: 네, 오늘 밤 다른 여행자들은 어디서 만날 수 있어요?

closing: We have a free pizza night in the lounge at seven. See you there!
closing_ko: 7시에 휴게실에서 무료 피자 파티가 있어요. 거기서 만나요!

title: Local Food Recommendation
situation_ko: 현지인에게 꼭 먹어 봐야 할 음식을 물어요.

questions.q: Hi! You look hungry. Are you looking for a place to eat?
questions.q_ko: 안녕하세요! 배고파 보이시네요. 식당을 찾고 계세요?
questions.sample: Yes, I want to try something local. What's the local specialty?
questions.sample_ko: 네, 현지 음식을 먹어 보고 싶어요. 이 지역 대표 음식이 뭐예요?

questions.q: You must try the fish stew. Do you like seafood?
questions.q_ko: 생선 스튜는 꼭 드셔 보세요. 해산물 좋아하세요?
questions.sample: I love seafood. Is it very spicy?

questions.q: A little, but you can ask for it mild. Do you usually eat spicy food?
questions.q_ko: 조금요, 하지만 순하게 해 달라고 할 수 있어요. 평소에 매운 음식을 드세요?
questions.sample: Yes, I'm from Korea, so I eat spicy food all the time.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 한국 사람이라 매운 음식을 늘 먹어요.

questions.q: Then you'll be fine! What's your favorite food from home?
questions.q_ko: 그럼 괜찮을 거예요! 고향 음식 중 제일 좋아하는 게 뭐예요?
questions.sample: I really like kimchi stew with rice.

questions.q: That sounds delicious. Do you want me to show you a good restaurant?
questions.sample: Yes, please. Where can I try it?
questions.sample_ko: 네, 부탁해요. 어디서 먹어 볼 수 있어요?

closing: It's just around the corner, the one with the blue door. Enjoy your meal!
closing_ko: 모퉁이만 돌면 있어요, 파란 문이 있는 곳이에요. 맛있게 드세요!

title: Delayed Flight
situation_ko: 비행기가 지연되어 공항 직원에게 상황을 물어봐요.
user_role: A passenger with a delayed flight

key_phrases.text: Can I get a meal voucher?

questions.q: Hello. How can I help you?
questions.sample: Hi, my flight to Sydney is delayed. Why is my flight delayed?
questions.sample_ko: 안녕하세요, 시드니행 비행기가 지연됐어요. 왜 지연된 건가요?

questions.q: There's a storm over the city, so planes can't take off right now. Do you have a connecting flight?
questions.q_ko: 도시 위에 폭풍이 있어서 지금은 이륙이 어려워요. 환승 비행기가 있으세요?
questions.sample: No, Sydney is my final stop. How long is the delay?
questions.sample_ko: 아니요, 시드니가 최종 목적지예요. 얼마나 지연돼요?

questions.q: We expect about three hours. How are you going to spend the time?
questions.q_ko: 약 세 시간 걸릴 것 같아요. 그 시간을 어떻게 보내실 거예요?
questions.sample: Maybe I'll read a book or get some coffee. Can I get a meal voucher?
questions.sample_ko: 책을 읽거나 커피를 마실까 해요. 식사 쿠폰을 받을 수 있나요?

questions.q: Yes, here's a voucher for fifteen dollars. Is someone waiting for you in Sydney?
questions.q_ko: 네, 15달러짜리 쿠폰이에요. 시드니에서 기다리는 사람이 있어요?
questions.sample: Yes, my friend will pick me up. I should tell her about the delay.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 친구가 마중 나올 거예요. 지연된다고 알려야 해요.

questions.q: There is free Wi-Fi in the terminal. What's the reason for your trip to Sydney?
questions.q_ko: 터미널에 무료 와이파이가 있어요. 시드니에는 무슨 일로 가세요?
questions.sample: I'm going to visit her and see the Opera House.
questions.sample_ko: 친구를 만나고 오페라 하우스를 보러 가요.

closing: What a lovely trip. Thank you for your patience, and we'll update you soon.
closing_ko: 멋진 여행이네요. 기다려 주셔서 감사하고, 곧 안내해 드릴게요.

title: Solo or Group Travel
situation_ko: 친구와 혼자 여행과 단체 여행 중 어느 쪽이 나은지 이야기해요.
user_role: A friend sharing opinions about travel styles

key_phrases.text: I prefer traveling alone because I can set my own schedule.
key_phrases.ko: 내 일정대로 움직일 수 있어서 혼자 여행하는 게 좋아요.

key_phrases.text: On the other hand, it can get lonely.

questions.q: I'm thinking about my next trip. Do you prefer traveling alone or with a group?
questions.q_ko: 다음 여행을 생각 중이야. 혼자 여행이 좋아, 단체 여행이 좋아?
questions.sample: I prefer traveling alone because I can set my own schedule and change plans freely.
questions.sample_ko: 내 일정대로 움직이고 계획도 자유롭게 바꿀 수 있어서 혼자가 좋아.

questions.q: That makes sense! Has traveling alone ever been difficult for you?
questions.q_ko: 이해돼! 혼자 여행이 힘들었던 적 있어?
questions.sample: Sometimes it can get lonely, especially at dinner, and it's harder if something goes wrong.
questions.sample_ko: 가끔 외로울 때가 있고, 특히 저녁 식사 때 그래. 문제가 생기면 더 힘들어.

questions.q: I know the feeling. What do you do to stay safe when you're alone?
questions.q_ko: 그 기분 알아. 혼자 있을 때 안전하려고 뭘 해?
questions.sample: I share my location with my family and I avoid walking alone late at night.
questions.sample_ko: 가족과 위치를 공유하고 밤늦게 혼자 걷지 않아.

questions.q: Smart. On the other hand, what are the good things about group trips?
questions.q_ko: 현명하네. 반대로 단체 여행의 좋은 점은 뭐라고 생각해?
questions.sample: You can split the costs, and it's more fun to share memories with others.
questions.sample_ko: 비용을 나눌 수 있고 추억을 함께 나누면 더 재밌어.

questions.q: True. So where would you go if you could choose, and with whom?
questions.q_ko: 맞아. 그럼 고를 수 있다면 어디에 누구와 가겠어?
questions.sample: It depends on the destination. For somewhere safe like Japan, I'd go alone, but for hiking in Nepal, I'd want a group.
questions.sample_ko: 여행지에 따라 달라. 일본처럼 안전한 곳은 혼자, 네팔 트레킹은 단체로 가고 싶어.

closing: Good point. Maybe I'll try a mix of both. Thanks for the advice!
closing_ko: 좋은 지적이야. 둘을 섞어서 해 볼까 봐. 조언 고마워!

title: Overtourism Debate
situation_ko: 유명 관광지에 사람이 너무 많이 몰리는 문제에 대해 의견을 나눠요.
user_role: A person sharing opinions on tourism

key_phrases.text: I think there are too many tourists in some places.
key_phrases.ko: 일부 장소에는 관광객이 너무 많다고 생각해요.

key_phrases.text: Local people should have a say.
One solution could be limiting daily visitors.
key_phrases.ko: 해결책 하나는 하루 방문객 수를 제한하는 거예요.

questions.q: Have you ever visited a place that felt too crowded with tourists?
questions.q_ko: 관광객이 너무 많아서 북적거린다고 느낀 곳에 가 본 적 있어요?
questions.sample: Yes, I went to a famous palace and could hardly move. I think there are too many tourists in some places.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 유명한 궁에 갔는데 움직이기도 힘들었어요. 일부 장소에는 관광객이 너무 많다고 생각해요.

questions.q: That sounds stressful. How do you think it affects the people who live there?
questions.q_ko: 스트레스였겠네요. 그곳에 사는 사람들에게는 어떤 영향이 있다고 생각하세요?
questions.sample: Prices go up, streets get noisy, and locals sometimes can't afford to live in their own neighborhoods.
questions.sample_ko: 물가가 오르고 거리가 시끄러워지고, 주민들이 자기 동네에 살기 어려워지기도 해요.

questions.q: Exactly. But tourism also brings money. Do you think the benefits are worth the problems?
questions.q_ko: 맞아요. 하지만 관광은 수입도 가져오죠. 이점이 문제보다 가치 있다고 생각하세요?
questions.sample: It brings jobs, but I think local people should have a say in how many visitors come.
questions.sample_ko: 일자리를 만들지만, 얼마나 많은 방문객이 올지에 지역 주민의 의견도 반영되어야 한다고 생각해요.

questions.q: Interesting. What solutions would you suggest?
questions.sample: One solution could be limiting daily visitors and charging a small fee to protect the area.
questions.sample_ko: 하루 방문객 수를 제한하고 지역 보호를 위해 소정의 요금을 받는 거예요.

questions.q: What can individual travelers do to be more responsible?
questions.q_ko: 개별 여행자는 더 책임 있게 하려면 무엇을 할 수 있을까요?
questions.sample: We can visit in the off-season, stay in local businesses and respect the rules.
questions.sample_ko: 비수기에 방문하고, 지역 업체를 이용하고, 규칙을 지킬 수 있어요.

closing: Those are great ideas. Travel should be good for both visitors and locals.
closing_ko: 훌륭한 생각이에요. 여행은 방문객과 주민 모두에게 좋아야 해요.

title: Budget or Luxury
situation_ko: 여행에서 돈을 아낄지 쓸지에 대해 의견을 나눠요.
user_role: A traveler with strong opinions on spending

key_phrases.text: I'd rather spend money on experiences.
A cheap hotel is fine as long as it's clean.
It's worth paying extra for comfort.
key_phrases.ko: 편안함을 위해 더 내는 건 가치가 있어요.

questions.q: When you travel, do you try to save money or spend freely?
questions.q_ko: 여행할 때 돈을 아끼려고 해, 아니면 자유롭게 써?
questions.sample: I try to save on hotels, but I'd rather spend money on experiences like tours and good food.
questions.sample_ko: 호텔은 아끼지만 투어나 맛있는 음식 같은 경험에는 돈을 쓰는 편이 좋아.

questions.q: Interesting! What kind of hotel do you usually choose?
questions.sample: A cheap hotel is fine as long as it's clean and in a safe area, because I'm hardly ever in the room.
questions.sample_ko: 깨끗하고 안전한 지역이면 싼 호텔도 괜찮아. 방에 거의 없으니까.

questions.q: Fair enough. Have you ever tried a luxury hotel? Was it worth it?
questions.q_ko: 그렇구나. 고급 호텔에 묵어 본 적 있어? 그만한 가치가 있었어?
questions.sample: Once, for my birthday. It was lovely, but I felt it was too expensive for just a bed.
questions.sample_ko: 한 번, 생일 때. 좋았지만 잠자리치고는 너무 비싸다고 느꼈어.

questions.q: Would you ever pay more for comfort, like a direct flight?
questions.q_ko: 직항처럼 편안함을 위해 돈을 더 낸 적 있어?
questions.sample: Yes, on long trips it's worth paying extra for comfort, because being exhausted ruins the first days.
questions.sample_ko: 응, 장거리 여행에서는 편안함을 위해 더 내는 게 가치 있어. 지치면 첫날들을 망치니까.

questions.q: What's one money-saving tip you'd give other travelers?
questions.q_ko: 다른 여행자들에게 해 줄 절약 팁 하나만 알려 줄래?
questions.sample: Eat where locals eat, not near the tourist spots. It's cheaper and usually tastier.
questions.sample_ko: 관광지 근처가 아니라 현지인이 가는 곳에서 먹어. 더 싸고 보통 더 맛있어.

closing: Great tips, thanks! I'll try eating like a local on my next trip.
closing_ko: 좋은 팁이야, 고마워! 다음 여행에서는 현지인처럼 먹어 볼게.

title: Culture Shock
situation_ko: 외국에서 겪은 낯선 문화와 놀랐던 경험을 이야기해요.
user_role: A traveler who experienced culture shock

key_phrases.text: What surprised me most was the way people greet each other.
key_phrases.ko: 가장 놀랐던 건 사람들이 인사하는 방식이었어요.

key_phrases.text: At first I felt uncomfortable, but I got used to it.

questions.q: Have you ever experienced culture shock when traveling abroad?
questions.q_ko: 해외여행에서 문화 충격을 받은 적 있어요?
questions.sample: Yes, in France. What surprised me most was the way people greet each other with kisses on the cheek.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 프랑스에서요. 가장 놀랐던 건 사람들이 뺨에 키스하며 인사하는 방식이었어요.

questions.q: That would be surprising! How did you react?
questions.sample: I froze at first and didn't know what to do, which was a bit embarrassing.
questions.sample_ko: 처음엔 굳어서 어떻게 해야 할지 몰라 조금 창피했어요.

questions.q: Did you get used to it after a while?
questions.sample: Yes, by the end of the week I did it naturally. At first I felt uncomfortable, but I got used to it.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 주말쯤엔 자연스럽게 했어요. 처음엔 불편했지만 익숙해졌어요.

questions.q: Were there any customs from your own country that surprised the locals?
questions.q_ko: 당신 나라의 관습 중 현지인들이 놀란 것도 있었어요?
questions.sample: They were surprised that we take our shoes off at home and share food from the middle of the table.
questions.sample_ko: 집에서 신발을 벗고 식탁 가운데 음식을 함께 나눠 먹는다는 걸 신기해했어요.

questions.q: What did that experience teach you about traveling?
questions.q_ko: 그 경험이 여행에 대해 뭘 가르쳐 줬나요?
questions.sample: It made me think differently. I learned that no culture is strange, just different, and being open-minded makes travel better.
questions.sample_ko: 다르게 생각하게 됐어요. 이상한 문화는 없고 다를 뿐이며, 열린 마음이 여행을 더 좋게 만든다는 걸 배웠어요.

closing: What a thoughtful answer. Open-mindedness really does make travel richer.
closing_ko: 생각이 깊은 답이네요. 열린 마음은 정말 여행을 더 풍성하게 해 줘요.

title: Travel Insurance
situation_ko: 여행자 보험이 꼭 필요한지 보험 상담원과 이야기해요.

key_phrases.text: I'm not sure it's necessary for a short trip.
I'd rather be safe than sorry.
key_phrases.ko: 나중에 후회하느니 미리 대비하는 게 낫죠.

questions.q: Hello! Are you thinking about getting travel insurance for an upcoming trip?
questions.q_ko: 안녕하세요! 곧 있을 여행을 위해 여행자 보험을 생각 중이세요?
questions.sample: Yes, I'm going to Thailand next month, but I'm not sure it's necessary for a short trip.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 다음 달에 태국에 가는데 짧은 여행에 꼭 필요한지 모르겠어요.

questions.q: Good question. What worries you most about the trip?
questions.q_ko: 좋은 질문이에요. 여행에서 가장 걱정되는 게 뭐예요?
questions.sample: Getting sick or losing my bag. Hospitals abroad can be expensive.
questions.sample_ko: 아프거나 가방을 잃어버리는 거요. 해외 병원비는 비쌀 수 있잖아요.

questions.q: That's exactly what insurance covers. Will you do any adventure activities?
questions.q_ko: 바로 그걸 보험이 보장해요. 모험 활동을 하실 건가요?
questions.sample: I want to try scuba diving, so I need to know what exactly it covers.
questions.sample_ko: 스쿠버 다이빙을 해 보고 싶어서 정확히 무엇을 보장하는지 알아야 해요.

questions.q: Some plans exclude diving, so we'd add an extra option. Have you had a bad travel experience before?
questions.q_ko: 어떤 플랜은 다이빙을 제외하니 옵션을 추가해야 해요. 안 좋은 여행 경험이 있으세요?
questions.sample: Yes, my flight was canceled once and I had to pay for a hotel myself.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 한번은 비행기가 취소돼서 호텔비를 직접 냈어요.

questions.q: Then how do you feel about insurance now?
questions.q_ko: 그럼 이제 보험에 대해 어떻게 생각하세요?
questions.sample: I think it's worth it. I'd rather be safe than sorry.
questions.sample_ko: 가치 있는 것 같아요. 나중에 후회하느니 미리 대비하는 게 낫죠.

closing: Wise choice. I'll prepare a plan that includes diving. Have a safe trip!
closing_ko: 현명한 선택이에요. 다이빙이 포함된 플랜을 준비할게요. 안전한 여행 되세요!

title: Dream Trip Around the World
situation_ko: 세계 일주를 한다면 어디를 어떻게 갈지 상상하며 이야기해요.
user_role: A dreamer planning a world trip

key_phrases.text: If I had a year, I'd visit every continent.
key_phrases.ko: 일 년이 있다면 모든 대륙을 가 볼 거예요.

key_phrases.text: I'd start with Europe, then move on to Asia.
What I'd miss most is my family.

questions.q: Imagine you could travel around the world for a year. Where would you go first?
questions.q_ko: 일 년 동안 세계 일주를 할 수 있다고 상상해 봐요. 어디부터 가겠어요?
questions.sample: If I had a year, I'd visit every continent. I'd start with Europe, because it's easy to travel by train.
questions.sample_ko: 일 년이 있다면 모든 대륙을 가 볼 거예요. 기차로 다니기 쉬운 유럽부터 시작할 거예요.

questions.q: Nice plan! Which place are you most excited about?
questions.sample: Patagonia in South America. I've always wanted to see those mountains and glaciers.
questions.sample_ko: 남미의 파타고니아요. 늘 그 산과 빙하를 보고 싶었어요.

questions.q: Wow! How would you pay for such a long trip?
questions.q_ko: 와! 그렇게 긴 여행 비용은 어떻게 마련하겠어요?
questions.sample: I'd save for two years and maybe work part-time in some places along the way.
questions.sample_ko: 2년 동안 저축하고, 가는 길에 일부 지역에서 아르바이트도 할 것 같아요.

questions.q: Would you travel alone or take someone with you?
questions.q_ko: 혼자 가겠어요, 아니면 누군가와 함께 가겠어요?
questions.sample: I'd love to go with my best friend, but I wouldn't mind meeting new people as I go.
questions.sample_ko: 가장 친한 친구와 가고 싶지만 가면서 새로운 사람들을 만나는 것도 좋아요.

questions.q: Last question: what would you miss most from home?
questions.q_ko: 마지막 질문이에요. 집에서 가장 그리울 것 같은 건 뭐예요?
questions.sample: What I'd miss most is my family and my mom's cooking.
questions.sample_ko: 제일 그리운 건 가족과 엄마가 해 주시는 음식일 거예요.

closing: What an adventure that would be! I hope your dream comes true someday.
closing_ko: 정말 멋진 모험이겠어요! 언젠가 꿈이 이루어지길 바라요.

title: Package Tour or Independent
situation_ko: 패키지 여행과 자유 여행의 장단점을 비교해 이야기해요.
ai_role: A travel agent chatting about options

key_phrases.text: A package tour is less stressful.
I like having the freedom to explore.
The downside is that it can be rushed.
key_phrases.ko: 단점은 일정이 빡빡할 수 있다는 거예요.

questions.q: Are you more of a package tour person or an independent traveler?
questions.q_ko: 패키지 여행 쪽이세요, 자유 여행 쪽이세요?
questions.sample: I'm an independent traveler. I like having the freedom to explore at my own pace.
questions.sample_ko: 자유 여행 쪽이에요. 제 속도로 자유롭게 돌아다니는 게 좋아요.

questions.q: I see! But isn't it stressful to plan everything yourself?
questions.q_ko: 그렇군요! 하지만 모든 걸 직접 계획하는 건 스트레스 아닌가요?
questions.sample: It can be, especially booking transport. That's why a package tour is less stressful for some people.
questions.sample_ko: 그럴 수 있어요, 특히 교통편 예약이요. 그래서 어떤 사람들에겐 패키지가 스트레스가 적죠.

questions.q: Have you ever joined a package tour?
questions.q_ko: 패키지 여행에 참여해 본 적 있어요?
questions.sample: Once, with my parents in Europe. The downside is that it can be rushed, and we only had ten minutes at each place.
questions.sample_ko: 한 번 부모님과 유럽에서요. 단점은 일정이 빡빡할 수 있다는 거고, 장소마다 10분밖에 없었어요.

questions.q: What would you say are the advantages for older travelers?
questions.q_ko: 나이 드신 여행자들에게는 어떤 장점이 있을까요?
questions.sample: They don't have to worry about language or directions, and a guide explains the history.
questions.sample_ko: 언어나 길 걱정을 안 해도 되고 가이드가 역사를 설명해 줘요.

questions.q: So which would you recommend to a first-time traveler abroad?
questions.q_ko: 그럼 해외여행이 처음인 사람에게는 어느 쪽을 추천하겠어요?
questions.sample: I'd recommend a short package tour first. After gaining confidence, they can try traveling independently.
questions.sample_ko: 먼저 짧은 패키지를 추천해요. 자신감이 생기면 자유 여행에 도전할 수 있어요.

closing: That's a balanced view. Both can be great depending on the traveler!
closing_ko: 균형 잡힌 시각이네요. 여행자에 따라 둘 다 훌륭할 수 있어요!

title: Travel and the Environment
situation_ko: 비행기 여행이 환경에 미치는 영향과 친환경 여행에 대해 이야기해요.
user_role: A traveler sharing views on eco-friendly travel

key_phrases.text: Flying produces a lot of carbon.
I try to take the train when possible.
Small changes can make a difference.
key_phrases.ko: 작은 변화도 차이를 만들 수 있어요.

questions.q: Do you ever worry about how your travel affects the environment?
questions.q_ko: 여행이 환경에 미치는 영향을 걱정한 적 있어?
questions.sample: Yes, I do. Flying produces a lot of carbon, so I sometimes feel guilty about long trips.
questions.sample_ko: 응. 비행은 탄소를 많이 배출해서 장거리 여행엔 가끔 죄책감이 들어.

questions.q: I feel the same. What do you do to reduce your impact?
questions.q_ko: 나도 그래. 영향을 줄이려고 뭘 해?
questions.sample: I try to take the train when possible, and I bring my own water bottle and bag.
questions.sample_ko: 가능하면 기차를 타고, 물병과 가방은 내 것을 가져가.

questions.q: Do you think hotels and tour companies should do more?
questions.q_ko: 호텔이나 여행사가 더 노력해야 한다고 생각해?
questions.sample: Definitely. They could reduce plastic, save water, and support local communities instead of only making profits.
questions.sample_ko: 당연하지. 플라스틱과 물 사용을 줄이고 이익만 추구하지 않고 지역 사회를 지원할 수 있어.

questions.q: Would you pay more for a greener option, like an eco-friendly hotel?
questions.q_ko: 친환경 호텔 같은 더 환경적인 선택에 돈을 더 낼 수 있어?
questions.sample: Yes, if the difference is reasonable. I think people are willing to pay for something they believe in.
questions.sample_ko: 차이가 합리적이라면 응. 사람들은 믿는 것에는 돈을 낼 의향이 있다고 생각해.

questions.q: Do you think one person's choices really matter?
questions.q_ko: 한 사람의 선택이 정말 중요하다고 생각해?
questions.sample: I do. Small changes can make a difference when many people do them.
questions.sample_ko: 응. 많은 사람이 하면 작은 변화도 차이를 만들 수 있어.

closing: I agree. Every little step helps. Thanks for sharing your thoughts!
closing_ko: 나도 동감이야. 작은 걸음도 도움이 돼. 생각을 나눠 줘서 고마워!

title: Working Remotely Abroad
situation_ko: 해외에서 일하며 여행하는 디지털 노마드 생활에 대해 의견을 나눠요.
user_role: A person considering remote work abroad

key_phrases.text: I'd love to work from a beach town.
The biggest challenge would be the time difference.
It might be hard to separate work from vacation.
key_phrases.ko: 일과 휴가를 구분하기 어려울 수 있어요.

questions.q: Would you ever work remotely from another country for a few months?
questions.q_ko: 몇 달 동안 다른 나라에서 원격으로 일해 볼 의향이 있어요?
questions.sample: Yes, I'd love to work from a beach town in Portugal if my company allowed it.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 회사가 허락한다면 포르투갈의 해변 마을에서 일하고 싶어요.

questions.q: Sounds dreamy! What do you think the biggest challenge would be?
questions.sample: The biggest challenge would be the time difference, because my team is in Korea.
questions.sample_ko: 팀이 한국에 있어서 가장 큰 어려움은 시차일 거예요.

questions.q: True. What about staying focused when there's so much to see?
questions.q_ko: 맞아요. 볼 게 많은데 집중하는 건 어떨까요?
questions.sample: It might be hard to separate work from vacation, so I'd need a strict daily routine.
questions.sample_ko: 일과 휴가를 구분하기 어려울 수 있어서 엄격한 일과가 필요할 거예요.

questions.q: What would you miss about working in an office?
questions.q_ko: 사무실에서 일하는 것 중 뭐가 그리울까요?
questions.sample: I'd miss chatting with my coworkers and having lunch together.
questions.sample_ko: 동료들과 수다 떨고 같이 점심 먹는 게 그리울 것 같아요.

questions.q: Do you think more people will live this way in the future?
questions.q_ko: 앞으로 더 많은 사람이 이렇게 살 거라고 생각해요?
questions.sample: I think so, because technology makes it easier, but not everyone can afford to do it.
questions.sample_ko: 기술이 쉽게 해 주니 그럴 거라 생각하지만 모두가 감당할 수 있는 건 아니에요.

closing: Interesting! It might be the future of work. Thanks for your thoughts!
closing_ko: 흥미롭네요! 미래의 근무 방식일지도 몰라요. 의견 고마워요!

title: A Language Barrier Story
situation_ko: 언어가 통하지 않아 겪은 일을 이야기해요.
ai_role: A friend who loves funny travel stories

key_phrases.text: We couldn't understand each other at all.
In the end, we used gestures.
It taught me to be more patient.

questions.q: Have you ever been in a situation where you couldn't communicate in a foreign country?
questions.q_ko: 외국에서 의사소통이 안 된 적 있어요?
questions.sample: Yes, in a small town in Italy. I tried to order food, but we couldn't understand each other at all.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 이탈리아의 작은 마을에서요. 음식을 주문하려는데 서로 전혀 이해하지 못했어요.

questions.q: Oh no! How did you solve the problem?
questions.sample: In the end, we used gestures and pictures on my phone, and we both started laughing.
questions.sample_ko: 결국 몸짓과 휴대폰 사진을 썼고 둘 다 웃기 시작했어요.

questions.q: Haha, what did you end up eating?
questions.sample: Something I didn't order, a big plate of mushrooms, but it was actually delicious.
questions.sample_ko: 주문하지 않은 거요, 커다란 버섯 접시였는데 사실 맛있었어요.

questions.q: Did that experience change how you prepare for trips?
questions.q_ko: 그 경험으로 여행 준비 방식이 바뀌었어요?
questions.sample: Yes, now I download a translation app and learn a few basic phrases before I go.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 이제 가기 전에 번역 앱을 받고 기본 표현 몇 개를 배워요.

questions.q: What did it teach you in the end?
questions.sample: It taught me to be more patient, and that kindness doesn't need a common language.
questions.sample_ko: 더 인내심을 갖게 됐고, 친절에는 공통 언어가 필요 없다는 걸 배웠어요.

closing: What a great story! A smile really is a universal language.
closing_ko: 정말 멋진 이야기예요! 미소는 정말 만국 공통어예요.

title: A Travel Disaster
situation_ko: 여행 중 일이 꼬였던 경험을 이야기해요.
user_role: A traveler recalling a bad trip

key_phrases.text: Everything went wrong from the start.
I learned to always have a backup plan.
key_phrases.ko: 항상 대안을 마련해 둬야 한다는 걸 배웠어요.

questions.q: Have you ever had a trip where everything went wrong?
questions.q_ko: 모든 게 잘못된 여행을 해 본 적 있어요?
questions.sample: Yes, a trip to Vietnam. Everything went wrong from the start. Our flight was late and our luggage was lost.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 베트남 여행이요. 처음부터 모든 게 잘못됐어요. 비행기가 늦고 짐도 잃어버렸어요.

questions.q: That sounds awful. What happened next?
questions.sample: Then it rained for three days, and I got food poisoning on the fourth.
questions.sample_ko: 그다음엔 사흘 동안 비가 왔고 나흘째에는 식중독에 걸렸어요.

questions.q: Oh dear. How did you deal with it all?
questions.sample: I tried to stay positive and rested in the hotel while my friend found a local doctor.
questions.sample_ko: 긍정적으로 지내려 했고 친구가 현지 병원을 알아보는 동안 호텔에서 쉬었어요.

questions.q: Do you ever laugh about it now?
questions.sample: Looking back, it's funny now. We still joke about it every time we meet.
questions.sample_ko: 돌아보면 지금은 웃겨요. 만날 때마다 아직도 농담해요.

questions.q: What did you learn from it?
questions.sample: I learned to always have a backup plan, and to buy travel insurance.
questions.sample_ko: 항상 대안을 마련해 두고 여행자 보험을 들어야 한다는 걸 배웠어요.

closing: Thanks for sharing. Sometimes the worst trips make the best stories!
closing_ko: 이야기해 줘서 고마워요. 최악의 여행이 최고의 이야기가 되기도 해요!

title: Souvenirs or Experiences
situation_ko: 여행에서 기념품을 사는 게 좋은지 경험을 남기는 게 좋은지 이야기해요.
ai_role: A friend interested in travel habits

key_phrases.text: Something handmade means more to me.

questions.q: Do you usually buy souvenirs when you travel?
questions.q_ko: 여행 갈 때 보통 기념품을 사?
questions.sample: Not really. I don't buy many souvenirs, because they just take up space at home.
questions.sample_ko: 별로. 기념품은 많이 안 사. 집에서 자리만 차지하거든.

questions.q: I see. So how do you remember your trips?
questions.sample: Photos are enough for me, and I write a short diary every night.
questions.sample_ko: 나는 사진이면 충분하고 매일 밤 짧게 일기를 써.

questions.q: That's nice. Is there anything you'd make an exception for?
questions.sample: Something handmade means more to me, like a small ceramic cup from a local artist.
questions.sample_ko: 수제품은 더 의미 있어. 현지 작가가 만든 작은 도자기 컵 같은 거.

questions.q: Do you buy gifts for family and friends?
questions.sample: Yes, usually local snacks or tea, because people can share them and nothing is wasted.
questions.sample_ko: 응, 보통 현지 과자나 차를 사. 나눠 먹을 수 있고 버려지는 게 없어서.

questions.q: Do you think souvenirs are worth the money?
questions.q_ko: 기념품이 돈 쓸 가치가 있다고 생각해?
questions.sample: Only if you really love them. Otherwise I'd rather spend on a good meal or a tour.
questions.sample_ko: 정말 마음에 들 때만. 아니면 맛있는 식사나 투어에 쓰는 게 낫지.

closing: I like that mindset. Memories really are the best souvenirs.
closing_ko: 그 생각 마음에 들어. 추억이야말로 최고의 기념품이야.

title: Staying Safe While Traveling
situation_ko: 해외에서 안전을 지키는 방법에 대해 조언을 주고받아요.
user_role: A traveler giving and getting advice

key_phrases.text: I always keep copies of my passport.
You should avoid carrying too much cash.
key_phrases.ko: 현금을 너무 많이 들고 다니면 안 돼요.

questions.q: Safety is important when traveling. What do you do to protect yourself?
questions.q_ko: 여행에서는 안전이 중요해요. 스스로를 지키려고 뭘 하세요?
questions.sample: I always keep copies of my passport, and I save important numbers on my phone.
questions.sample_ko: 여권 사본을 항상 챙기고 중요한 번호는 휴대폰에 저장해요.

questions.q: Smart! How do you protect your money and belongings?
questions.sample: You should avoid carrying too much cash. I use a card and keep a small bag in front of me in crowds.
questions.sample_ko: 현금을 너무 많이 들고 다니면 안 돼요. 카드를 쓰고 붐비는 곳에서는 작은 가방을 앞에 둬요.

questions.q: Have you ever had something stolen or almost stolen?
questions.q_ko: 뭔가 도난당했거나 도난당할 뻔한 적 있어요?
questions.sample: Once, someone tried to open my backpack on a crowded train, but I noticed in time.
questions.sample_ko: 한번은 붐비는 기차에서 누가 제 배낭을 열려고 했는데 제때 알아챘어요.

questions.q: Good thing you noticed! How do you decide if a place feels unsafe?
questions.q_ko: 알아챘다니 다행이네요! 어떤 곳이 위험한지 어떻게 판단해요?
questions.sample: I trust my instincts. If a street is empty or people stare at me, I leave quickly.
questions.sample_ko: 직감을 믿어요. 길이 텅 비었거나 사람들이 쳐다보면 재빨리 떠나요.

questions.q: What's the best safety tip you'd give a first-time traveler?
questions.q_ko: 처음 여행하는 사람에게 해 줄 최고의 안전 팁은 뭐예요?
questions.sample: Tell someone your plans, and always check the news about the place before you go.
questions.sample_ko: 계획을 누군가에게 알리고, 가기 전에 그곳의 소식을 꼭 확인하세요.

closing: Excellent advice. A little preparation makes a trip much more relaxing.
closing_ko: 훌륭한 조언이에요. 약간의 준비가 여행을 훨씬 편안하게 해 줘요.

title: Why We Travel
situation_ko: 사람들이 왜 여행을 하는지, 여행이 삶에 어떤 의미인지 이야기해요.

key_phrases.text: Travel helps me see things from a new perspective.
key_phrases.ko: 여행은 새로운 시각으로 보게 해 줘요.

key_phrases.text: It's a way to escape my daily routine.

questions.q: Why do you think people love to travel?
questions.sample: I think it's a way to escape the daily routine and to discover something new.
questions.sample_ko: 일상에서 벗어나 새로운 것을 발견하는 방법이라고 생각해요.

questions.q: That's true. What does travel give you personally?
questions.sample: Travel helps me see things from a new perspective, and I come back feeling refreshed.
questions.sample_ko: 여행은 새로운 시각으로 보게 해 주고, 돌아오면 기분이 새로워져요.

questions.q: Has a trip ever changed your life or your way of thinking?
questions.q_ko: 여행이 삶이나 생각을 바꾼 적 있나요?
questions.sample: Yes, volunteering in Cambodia made me more grateful for what I have.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 캄보디아에서 봉사 활동을 하면서 가진 것에 더 감사하게 됐어요.

questions.q: Do you think you can learn as much from a vacation at home?
questions.q_ko: 집 근처에서 보내는 휴가로도 그만큼 배울 수 있다고 생각해요?
questions.sample: Maybe, if you look with curious eyes. But being far away makes you notice more differences.
questions.sample_ko: 호기심을 가지고 본다면 그럴 수도 있어요. 하지만 멀리 가면 더 많은 차이를 알아채게 돼요.

questions.q: Where would you like to travel next, and why?
questions.q_ko: 다음엔 어디로 여행하고 싶고, 그 이유는 뭐예요?
questions.sample: I'd like to go to Iceland to see the northern lights, because I've wanted to since I was a child.
questions.sample_ko: 어릴 때부터 오로라를 보고 싶어서 아이슬란드에 가고 싶어요.

closing: That sounds magical. Thank you for such a thoughtful conversation!
closing_ko: 마법 같겠어요. 깊이 있는 대화 고마워요!

title: Travel Tips for Beginners
situation_ko: 해외여행이 처음인 친구에게 유용한 팁을 알려 줘요.

key_phrases.text: The most important thing is to pack light.
key_phrases.ko: 가장 중요한 건 짐을 가볍게 싸는 거예요.

key_phrases.text: I'd recommend arriving at the airport early.
Don't worry too much; most people are helpful.

questions.q: I'm going abroad for the first time next month and I'm nervous. Any advice on packing?
questions.q_ko: 다음 달에 처음 해외에 가는데 긴장돼요. 짐 싸는 조언 있어요?
questions.sample: The most important thing is to pack light, because you'll carry your bag everywhere.
questions.sample_ko: 가장 중요한 건 짐을 가볍게 싸는 거예요. 어디든 직접 들고 다닐 테니까요.

questions.q: Good point. What about the airport? I'm worried about getting lost.
questions.q_ko: 맞는 말이에요. 공항은요? 길을 잃을까 봐 걱정돼요.
questions.sample: I'd recommend arriving at the airport early and following the signs. Staff are always happy to help.
questions.sample_ko: 공항에 일찍 도착해서 표지판을 따라가길 추천해요. 직원들이 항상 도와줄 거예요.

questions.q: OK. And how should I handle money in a different country?
questions.q_ko: 알겠어요. 다른 나라에서는 돈을 어떻게 다뤄야 해요?
questions.sample: Bring a card without foreign fees and a little cash for emergencies.
questions.sample_ko: 해외 수수료가 없는 카드와 비상용 소액 현금을 챙기세요.

questions.q: What if I don't understand the language?
questions.sample: Use a translation app and learn simple greetings. Don't worry too much; most people are helpful.
questions.sample_ko: 번역 앱을 쓰고 간단한 인사말을 배워 두세요. 너무 걱정 마세요, 대부분 친절해요.

questions.q: Last thing: what's the one thing I shouldn't forget to do?
questions.q_ko: 마지막이에요. 꼭 잊지 말아야 할 한 가지는 뭐예요?
questions.sample: Enjoy it! Take photos, try new food, and don't plan every minute.
questions.sample_ko: 즐기는 거예요! 사진도 찍고 새로운 음식도 먹고, 모든 시간을 계획하지 마세요.

closing: Thank you so much! I feel much more confident now. See you after my trip!
closing_ko: 정말 고마워요! 이제 훨씬 자신 있어요. 여행 다녀와서 봐요!

title: Ordering Coffee
situation_ko: 카페에서 점원에게 커피를 주문해요.
ai_role: A friendly barista at a cafe

key_phrases.text: Can I have a latte, please?

questions.q: Hi! What would you like to drink?
questions.sample: Can I have a latte, please?

questions.q: Sure! Hot or iced?
questions.q_ko: 네! 따뜻한 걸로 드릴까요, 차가운 걸로 드릴까요?
questions.sample: Iced, please.

questions.q: Great. What size would you like?
questions.sample: Medium, please.

questions.q: Would you like anything to eat with that?
questions.sample: Yes, a small cookie.

questions.q: Okay! For here or to go?
questions.q_ko: 알겠습니다! 여기서 드실 건가요, 가져가실 건가요?
questions.sample: To go, please.

closing: Thank you! Your drink will be ready in a minute. Enjoy!
closing_ko: 감사합니다! 음료는 곧 나와요. 맛있게 드세요!

title: Fast Food Order
situation_ko: 패스트푸드점 카운터에서 햄버거 세트를 주문해요.

questions.q: Welcome! What can I get for you?
questions.sample: I'd like a cheeseburger meal.

questions.q: Okay! What side would you like, fries or salad?
questions.q_ko: 네! 사이드는 감자튀김과 샐러드 중 뭐로 하실래요?
questions.sample: Fries, please.

questions.q: And what drink would you like?
questions.sample: A cola, please.

questions.q: Any changes to the burger, like no pickles?
questions.q_ko: 햄버거에서 빼고 싶은 게 있나요? 피클 같은 거요.
questions.sample: No onions, please.

questions.q: Got it. Will you pay by cash or card?
questions.sample: By card, please.

closing: Thanks! Please wait here. Your number will be called soon.
closing_ko: 감사합니다! 여기서 기다려 주세요. 곧 번호를 불러 드릴게요.

title: Favorite Food
situation_ko: 새 친구와 좋아하는 음식에 대해 이야기해요.

questions.q: What is your favorite food?
questions.sample: I love pizza.

questions.q: Nice! How often do you eat it?
questions.sample: I eat it every week.

questions.q: Do you eat it at home or at a restaurant?
questions.sample: Usually at home.

questions.q: Who do you eat it with?
questions.sample: With my family.

questions.q: Is there any food you don't like?
questions.sample: I don't like fish.

closing: Food is great, isn't it? Thanks for sharing!
closing_ko: 음식은 정말 좋죠? 얘기해 줘서 고마워요!

title: Asking for the Menu
situation_ko: 식당에 들어가 자리에 앉고 메뉴를 부탁해요.

questions.q: Hello! How many people are in your group?
questions.sample: A table for two, please.

questions.q: Okay. Do you want a table by the window?
questions.sample: Yes, that sounds nice.

questions.q: Here you are. Do you need anything?
questions.sample: Can I see the menu?

questions.q: Of course! What would you like to drink first?
questions.q_ko: 물론이죠! 먼저 마실 것은 뭘로 드릴까요?
questions.sample: Water, please.

questions.q: Do you need a few more minutes to decide?
questions.sample: Yes, a few minutes, please.

closing: No problem. Take your time. I'll come back soon.
closing_ko: 괜찮아요. 천천히 보세요. 곧 다시 올게요.

title: Breakfast Talk
situation_ko: 동료와 아침에 뭘 먹었는지 이야기해요.
user_role: A coworker chatting in the morning

questions.q: Good morning! Did you have breakfast today?
questions.sample: Yes, I had toast and eggs.

questions.q: Sounds good! Do you eat breakfast every day?
questions.sample: Not every day. Sometimes I skip it.

questions.q: What do you usually drink in the morning?
questions.sample: I drink coffee every morning.

questions.q: Do you cook breakfast or buy it?
questions.q_ko: 아침을 직접 만들어요, 아니면 사 먹어요?
questions.sample: I make it at home.

questions.q: What time do you usually eat?
questions.sample: Around seven thirty.

closing: Nice! A good breakfast gives you energy for the day.
closing_ko: 좋아요! 든든한 아침은 하루의 에너지가 돼요.

title: At the Grocery Store
situation_ko: 마트에서 직원에게 물건이 어디 있는지 물어봐요.

questions.q: Hi! Can I help you find something?
questions.sample: Yes, where is the milk?

questions.q: It's in aisle three. Do you need anything else?
questions.q_ko: 3번 통로에 있어요. 다른 건 필요 없으세요?
questions.sample: I need some apples.

questions.q: The apples are over there. How many do you want?
questions.q_ko: 사과는 저쪽에 있어요. 몇 개 필요하세요?
questions.sample: Five, please.

questions.q: Do you want a bag?
questions.sample: No, I have my own bag.

questions.q: What are you going to make today?
questions.sample: Maybe a salad.

closing: Sounds yummy! Have a nice day.
closing_ko: 맛있겠네요! 좋은 하루 보내세요.

title: Ordering Pizza by Phone
situation_ko: 전화로 피자를 주문하고 배달을 부탁해요.
ai_role: A pizza shop worker on the phone

key_phrases.text: Please deliver it to my home.

questions.q: Hello, Tony's Pizza. What would you like?
questions.sample: I want a large pizza.

questions.q: What kind of pizza? We have pepperoni and cheese.
questions.q_ko: 어떤 피자로 하시겠어요? 페퍼로니와 치즈가 있어요.
questions.sample: Pepperoni, please.

questions.q: Would you like a drink with it?
questions.sample: Yes, two colas.

questions.q: Okay. What is your address?
questions.sample: It's 25 Green Street.

questions.q: Got it. Do you have any other questions?
questions.sample: How long will it take?

closing: About thirty minutes. Thank you for calling!
closing_ko: 약 30분 걸려요. 전화 주셔서 감사합니다!

title: Do You Like Spicy Food?
situation_ko: 외국인 친구가 한국 음식에 대해 물어봐요.

questions.q: Hi! Do you like spicy food?
questions.sample: Yes, I like spicy food.

questions.q: Cool! What is a good Korean food for me?
questions.q_ko: 멋지네요! 저에게 어떤 한국 음식이 좋을까요?
questions.sample: Try bulgogi. It's sweet.

questions.q: Is kimchi spicy?
questions.sample: Yes, it's a little spicy.

questions.q: What do you eat with kimchi?
questions.sample: We eat it with rice.

questions.q: Can you use chopsticks well?
questions.sample: Yes, I use them every day.

closing: I can't wait to try Korean food. Thank you!
closing_ko: 한국 음식을 빨리 먹어 보고 싶어요. 고마워요!

title: Paying the Bill
situation_ko: 식사를 마치고 계산서를 부탁하고 계산해요.

questions.q: Was everything okay with your meal?
questions.sample: Yes, it was delicious.

questions.q: I'm glad! Would you like dessert?
questions.sample: No, thank you. The check, please.

questions.q: Sure. Do you want to pay together?
questions.sample: No, can we pay separately?

questions.q: Of course. How would you like to pay?
questions.sample: With a credit card.

questions.q: Do you need a receipt?
questions.sample: Yes, please.

closing: Thank you so much! Please come again.
closing_ko: 정말 감사합니다! 또 오세요.

title: Buying Bread
situation_ko: 빵집에서 빵을 고르고 사요.

questions.q: Good morning! What would you like today?
questions.sample: I'd like two croissants.

questions.q: Sure! Anything else?
questions.sample: Yes, one loaf of bread.

questions.q: Do you want it sliced?
questions.sample: Yes, please.

questions.q: Would you like a coffee too?
questions.sample: No, thank you.

questions.q: Are these for breakfast?
questions.sample: Yes, for tomorrow's breakfast.

closing: That's eight dollars. Thank you, enjoy your bread!
closing_ko: 8달러예요. 감사합니다, 빵 맛있게 드세요!

title: Making Tea at Home
situation_ko: 집에 온 손님에게 마실 것을 대접해요.

questions.q: Thank you for inviting me. Your home is nice!
questions.sample: Thank you! Please sit down.

questions.q: Thanks. Can I have something to drink?
questions.sample: Sure. Would you like some tea?

questions.q: Yes, please. What kinds of tea do you have?
questions.sample: I have green tea and black tea.

questions.q: Green tea sounds good. Can I have some sugar?
questions.q_ko: 녹차가 좋겠어요. 설탕 좀 주실 수 있어요?
questions.sample: Sure, here you are.

questions.q: Do you have any snacks too?
questions.sample: Yes, I have some cookies.

closing: Mmm, this is lovely. Thank you for your kindness!
closing_ko: 음, 정말 좋네요. 친절하게 대해 줘서 고마워요!

title: Lunch Plans
situation_ko: 동료와 점심에 뭘 먹을지 정해요.

questions.q: It's almost noon. Are you hungry?
questions.sample: Yes, I'm very hungry.

questions.q: Me too! What do you want for lunch?
questions.sample: Let's eat noodles.

questions.q: Good idea. Should we walk or take the bus?
questions.sample: Let's walk. It's close.

questions.q: How much do you usually spend on lunch?
questions.sample: About ten dollars.

questions.q: Do you want to have coffee after lunch?
questions.sample: Yes, sounds good!

closing: Great! Let's go. I'm so excited to eat.
closing_ko: 좋아요! 가요. 먹을 생각에 신나요.

title: At the Food Truck
situation_ko: 푸드트럭에서 타코를 주문해요.

questions.q: Hey there! What can I get you?
questions.sample: Two tacos, please.

questions.q: Chicken or beef?
questions.sample: Chicken, please.

questions.q: Do you want hot sauce on it?
questions.sample: Just a little. Not too spicy.

questions.q: Would you like a drink?
questions.sample: Yes, a bottle of water.

questions.q: Are you eating here or taking it with you?
questions.sample: I'll eat on that bench.

closing: Here you go. Enjoy your tacos!
closing_ko: 여기 있어요. 타코 맛있게 드세요!

title: Cooking Rice
situation_ko: 룸메이트에게 간단한 요리를 어떻게 하는지 알려줘요.
ai_role: A new roommate who cannot cook

questions.q: Hi! Can you cook rice? I don't know how.
questions.q_ko: 안녕! 밥 지을 줄 알아요? 저는 몰라요.
questions.sample: Yes, it's easy. First, wash the rice.

questions.q: Okay! How much water do I need?
questions.sample: Add the same amount of water as rice.

questions.q: Got it. Do I use a pot or a rice cooker?
questions.sample: A rice cooker is easier.

questions.q: How long does it take?
questions.sample: About twenty minutes.

questions.q: What should I eat with the rice?
questions.sample: Eggs and kimchi are good.

closing: Thank you for teaching me! I'll try it tonight.
closing_ko: 가르쳐 줘서 고마워요! 오늘 밤에 해 볼게요.

title: Ice Cream Shop
situation_ko: 아이스크림 가게에서 맛을 골라요.

questions.q: Hi! Which flavor would you like?
questions.sample: Can I try the strawberry?

questions.q: Sure! Here you go. Do you like it?
questions.sample: Yes, it's sweet. One scoop, please.

questions.q: Great! A cup or a cone?
questions.sample: In a cup, please.

questions.q: Do you want any toppings?
questions.sample: Yes, some nuts.

questions.q: Is the ice cream for you?
questions.sample: Yes, it's a treat for me.

closing: Enjoy your ice cream! Have a sweet day!
closing_ko: 아이스크림 맛있게 드세요! 달콤한 하루 보내세요!

title: Reserving a Table
situation_ko: 전화로 저녁 식사 자리를 예약해요.

key_phrases.text: I'd like to make a reservation.
It's for four people at seven.
Could we have a quiet table?

questions.q: Thank you for calling Rosa's Kitchen. How can I help you?
questions.q_ko: 로사스 키친에 전화 주셔서 감사합니다. 무엇을 도와드릴까요?
questions.sample: I'd like to make a reservation for this Friday.

questions.q: Sure. What time and how many people?
questions.sample: It's for four people at seven.

questions.q: Perfect. Is it for a special occasion?
questions.sample: Yes, it's my friend's birthday.

questions.q: How nice! Do you have any seating preferences?
questions.sample: Could we have a quiet table?

questions.q: No problem. May I have your name and phone number?
questions.sample: It's Minji Kim, and my number is 010-1234-5678.

closing: All set! We'll see you Friday at seven. Happy birthday to your friend!
closing_ko: 예약됐어요! 금요일 7시에 뵐게요. 친구분께 생일 축하드려요!

title: Food Allergies
situation_ko: 식당에서 알레르기가 있다고 직원에게 알려요.
user_role: A customer with a food allergy

key_phrases.text: Could you check with the kitchen?

questions.q: Are you ready to order, or do you have any questions?
questions.sample: I have a question. I'm allergic to peanuts.

questions.q: Thanks for telling me. Which dish are you thinking about?
questions.q_ko: 말씀해 주셔서 감사해요. 어떤 요리를 생각 중이세요?
questions.sample: The pad thai. Does it contain nuts?

questions.q: Yes, it has crushed peanuts on top. We can leave them off. Is that okay?
questions.q_ko: 네, 위에 으깬 땅콩이 올라가요. 빼 드릴 수 있는데 괜찮으세요?
questions.sample: Please leave them off, and could you check with the kitchen about the sauce?
questions.sample_ko: 빼 주시고, 소스도 주방에 확인해 주실래요?

questions.q: I'll do that. How serious is your allergy?
questions.sample: It's quite serious. I can get a rash and trouble breathing.
questions.sample_ko: 꽤 심해요. 두드러기가 나고 숨쉬기 힘들어질 수 있어요.

questions.q: I understand. Would you like something to drink while you wait?
questions.q_ko: 알겠습니다. 기다리는 동안 마실 것 드릴까요?
questions.sample: Just sparkling water, please.

closing: The kitchen will take extra care. Your safety is important to us.
closing_ko: 주방에서 특별히 신경 쓸게요. 손님의 안전이 가장 중요해요.

title: Wrong Order
situation_ko: 주문한 것과 다른 음식이 나와서 직원에게 말해요.
user_role: A customer who got the wrong dish

key_phrases.text: Excuse me, this isn't what I ordered.
key_phrases.ko: 저기요, 이건 제가 주문한 게 아니에요.

key_phrases.text: I can wait a few minutes.

questions.q: Here's your meal. Is everything all right?
questions.sample: Excuse me, this isn't what I ordered.
questions.sample_ko: 저기요, 이건 제가 주문한 게 아니에요.

questions.q: Oh, I'm so sorry! What did you order?
questions.sample: I ordered the chicken salad, not the pasta.

questions.q: I'll fix that right away. Are you in a hurry?
questions.sample: A little. I have a meeting at one.

questions.q: I'll ask the kitchen to hurry. Would you like a drink on the house while you wait?
questions.q_ko: 주방에 서둘러 달라고 할게요. 기다리시는 동안 음료를 서비스로 드릴까요?
questions.sample: That's kind. An iced tea, please.

questions.q: Of course. Should I keep the pasta here or take it away?
questions.sample: Please take it away.

closing: Thank you for your patience. Your salad will be here in five minutes.
closing_ko: 기다려 주셔서 감사해요. 샐러드는 5분 안에 나올 거예요.

title: Cold Soup Complaint
situation_ko: 수프가 차갑게 나와서 정중하게 불만을 말해요.

key_phrases.text: Could you heat it up, please?

questions.q: Hello, I'm the manager. Is there a problem?
questions.sample: Yes, my soup is cold.

questions.q: I'm very sorry. How long has it been on the table?
questions.q_ko: 정말 죄송합니다. 테이블에 나온 지 얼마나 됐나요?
questions.sample: About ten minutes. It came out cold.

questions.q: I see. Would you like me to heat it up, or bring a new one?
questions.q_ko: 그렇군요. 데워 드릴까요, 새로 가져다 드릴까요?
questions.sample: A new one would be better, please.

questions.q: Certainly. Is the rest of your meal okay?
questions.sample: Yes, the bread is great.

questions.q: Good to hear. Would you like more bread while you wait?
questions.q_ko: 다행이네요. 기다리는 동안 빵을 더 드릴까요?
questions.sample: Yes, that would be nice.

closing: Thank you for letting us know. The soup will be hot and fresh shortly.
closing_ko: 알려 주셔서 감사해요. 곧 따뜻한 새 수프를 가져다 드릴게요.

title: Explaining Kimbap
situation_ko: 외국인 친구에게 김밥이 무엇인지 설명해요.

key_phrases.text: It has vegetables and egg inside.

questions.q: What's that black roll in the picture? It looks interesting!
questions.q_ko: 사진 속 검은 롤은 뭐예요? 재미있어 보여요!
questions.sample: That's kimbap. It's rice rolled in seaweed.
questions.sample_ko: 김밥이에요. 김에 밥을 말아 놓은 거예요.

questions.q: Oh nice! What's inside it?
questions.q_ko: 와, 좋네요! 안에 뭐가 들어 있어요?
questions.sample: It has vegetables, egg, and ham inside.

questions.q: Is it the same as sushi?
questions.sample: Not really. Kimbap uses sesame oil, and it usually has no raw fish.
questions.sample_ko: 꼭 그렇진 않아요. 김밥은 참기름을 쓰고 보통 생선회는 안 들어가요.

questions.q: I see! When do Koreans eat it?
questions.sample: It's popular for picnics and quick lunches.

questions.q: Can you make it at home?
questions.sample: Yes, it takes time, but it's fun to make with family.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 시간은 걸리지만 가족과 같이 만들면 재미있어요.

closing: I'd love to try making it with you someday. Thanks for explaining!
closing_ko: 언젠가 같이 만들어 보고 싶어요. 설명해 줘서 고마워요!

title: Potluck Planning
situation_ko: 각자 음식을 가져오는 파티에서 무엇을 가져갈지 정해요.

questions.q: We're having a potluck on Saturday. What can you bring?
questions.q_ko: 토요일에 포트럭 파티를 해요. 뭘 가져올 수 있어요?
questions.sample: I can bring a salad.

questions.q: Perfect! What kind of salad?
questions.sample: A pasta salad with tomatoes and olives.

questions.q: Yum! Do you need to know about any allergies?
questions.q_ko: 맛있겠다! 알레르기 같은 거 알아야 해요?
questions.sample: Yes, is anyone vegetarian?

questions.q: Two people are. That's fine, right?
questions.sample: Yes, my salad has no meat.

questions.q: Great. How many people should you cook for?
questions.sample: I'll make enough for six.

closing: Wonderful! See you Saturday. This will be a feast!
closing_ko: 멋져요! 토요일에 봐요. 푸짐한 잔치가 되겠어요!

title: Meal Delivery App
situation_ko: 배달 앱 고객센터와 주문 내용을 확인해요.
ai_role: A delivery app customer service agent

key_phrases.text: I'd like to change my order.
Please leave it at the door.

questions.q: Thanks for contacting us. How can I help with your order?
questions.q_ko: 연락 주셔서 감사합니다. 주문 관련해서 무엇을 도와드릴까요?
questions.sample: I'd like to change my order.

questions.q: Sure. What would you like to change?
questions.sample: I want to add a side of fried rice.

questions.q: Okay, added. Is the delivery address still correct?
questions.q_ko: 네, 추가했어요. 배달 주소는 그대로 맞나요?
questions.sample: Yes, but please leave it at the door.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 그런데 문 앞에 놓아 주세요.

questions.q: No problem. Do you want the driver to ring the bell?
questions.sample: Yes, just once, because my baby is sleeping.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 한 번만요. 아기가 자고 있어서요.

questions.q: Understood. Is there anything else you need?
questions.sample: When will it arrive?

closing: It should arrive in about thirty minutes. Enjoy your meal!
closing_ko: 약 30분 후에 도착할 거예요. 맛있게 드세요!

title: Planning a Grocery Run
situation_ko: 가족과 함께 이번 주 장보기 목록을 정해요.
user_role: A family member helping to shop

key_phrases.text: Let's buy enough for the week.

questions.q: Let's make a shopping list. What do we need from the fridge?
questions.q_ko: 장보기 목록을 만들어요. 냉장고에서 뭐가 필요하죠?
questions.sample: We're out of eggs and milk.

questions.q: Right. What should we cook this week?
questions.sample: Maybe chicken soup and stir-fried vegetables.

questions.q: Nice! What ingredients do we need for that?
questions.sample: We need chicken, carrots, and onions.

questions.q: Do you prefer the market or the supermarket?
questions.sample: The market. It's fresher and cheaper.

questions.q: Okay. How should we divide the shopping?
questions.sample: I'll get vegetables, and you get the meat.
questions.sample_ko: 저는 채소를 살게요. 고기는 사 주세요.

closing: Perfect plan! Let's go shopping this afternoon.
closing_ko: 완벽한 계획이에요! 오늘 오후에 장 보러 가요.

title: Learning a Recipe
situation_ko: 친구에게 간단한 계란 요리 방법을 알려줘요.
ai_role: A friend who wants to learn a recipe

questions.q: Your scrambled eggs looked amazing! How do you make them?
questions.q_ko: 네가 만든 스크램블 에그 정말 근사해 보였어! 어떻게 만들어?
questions.sample: First, crack three eggs into a bowl and mix them.
questions.sample_ko: 먼저 계란 세 개를 그릇에 깨서 섞어요.

questions.q: Do you add anything to the eggs?
questions.sample: I add a little milk and some salt.

questions.q: Interesting! How hot should the pan be?
questions.sample: Cook it on low heat so it stays soft.

questions.q: How long does it take?
questions.sample: Only about three minutes.

questions.q: What do you eat it with?
questions.sample: With toast and a little ketchup.

closing: That sounds so easy. I'll try it tomorrow morning. Thank you!
closing_ko: 정말 쉽겠다. 내일 아침에 해 볼게. 고마워!

title: Vegetarian Diet
situation_ko: 채식을 하는 친구와 식단에 대해 이야기해요.
user_role: A friend curious about vegetarian food

key_phrases.text: What do you eat for protein?

questions.q: I've been vegetarian for two years. Have you ever tried it?
questions.q_ko: 저는 2년째 채식하고 있어요. 해 본 적 있어요?
questions.sample: No, I haven't, but I'm curious about it.

questions.q: Cool! What do you usually eat in a day?
questions.sample: Rice, meat, and vegetables. I eat meat a lot.
questions.sample_ko: 밥, 고기, 채소요. 고기를 많이 먹어요.

questions.q: I see. Do you think you could stop eating meat for a day?
questions.q_ko: 그렇군요. 하루 정도 고기 없이 지낼 수 있을 것 같아요?
questions.sample: Maybe. I'd like to try it once a week.
questions.sample_ko: 아마도요. 일주일에 한 번 해 보고 싶어요.

questions.q: That would be great! What vegetables do you like?
questions.sample: I like mushrooms and sweet potatoes.

questions.q: Perfect. Should I cook you a vegetarian dinner sometime?
questions.q_ko: 좋아요. 언제 채식 저녁을 만들어 줄까요?
questions.sample: Yes, please! That would be wonderful.

closing: Great! I'll make my favorite vegetable curry for you.
closing_ko: 좋아요! 제가 제일 좋아하는 채소 카레를 만들어 줄게요.

title: Ordering at a Cafe with Friends
situation_ko: 친구들과 함께 간 카페에서 디저트와 음료를 골라요.

key_phrases.text: We'd like to share a cake.

questions.q: Welcome! Are you ready to order, or do you need a minute?
questions.q_ko: 어서 오세요! 주문하시겠어요, 아니면 시간이 더 필요하세요?
questions.sample: What do you recommend?

questions.q: Our strawberry cake is very popular. Would you like to try it?
questions.q_ko: 딸기 케이크가 아주 인기예요. 드셔 보시겠어요?
questions.sample: Yes, we'd like to share one cake.

questions.q: Sure. Would you like drinks with it?
questions.sample: Two lattes and one hot chocolate.
questions.sample_ko: 라테 두 잔이랑 핫초코 한 잔이요.

questions.q: Anything you'd like to change, like less sugar or extra milk?
questions.q_ko: 당을 줄이거나 우유를 더 넣는 등 바꾸고 싶은 건 있나요?
questions.sample: Less sugar in the hot chocolate, please.

questions.q: Okay. Do you need anything else for the cake?
questions.q_ko: 알겠습니다. 케이크와 함께 필요한 게 더 있나요?
questions.sample: Could we have three forks, please?

closing: Coming right up! Enjoy your time together.
closing_ko: 곧 가져다 드릴게요! 즐거운 시간 보내세요.

title: Korean BBQ Night
situation_ko: 외국인 동료를 한국식 고깃집에 데려가 먹는 법을 알려줘요.
ai_role: A foreign coworker at a Korean BBQ restaurant

key_phrases.text: We cook it at the table.

questions.q: Wow, there's a grill in the middle of the table! How does this work?
questions.q_ko: 와, 테이블 가운데 불판이 있네요! 이건 어떻게 하는 거예요?
questions.sample: We cook the meat at the table and cut it with scissors.

questions.q: Fun! What are all these small side dishes?
questions.sample: They're banchan. You can eat as much as you want.

questions.q: Great. How do I eat the meat?
questions.sample: Wrap it in lettuce with garlic and sauce.
questions.sample_ko: 상추에 마늘이랑 쌈장이랑 같이 싸서 드세요.

questions.q: Delicious! What do Koreans usually drink with this?
questions.q_ko: 맛있어요! 한국 사람들은 이거랑 보통 뭘 마셔요?
questions.sample: Many people drink soju or beer.

questions.q: I'll try a little soju. Is there a special way to drink it?
questions.q_ko: 소주 조금 마셔 볼게요. 특별한 예절이 있나요?
questions.sample: Yes, pour for others first and use both hands.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 다른 사람에게 먼저 따라 주고 두 손으로 따라요.

closing: I love this! Thank you for teaching me Korean dining customs.
closing_ko: 정말 좋아요! 한국의 식사 예절을 알려 줘서 고마워요.

title: At the Buffet
situation_ko: 뷔페 식당에서 직원과 이용 방법을 이야기해요.

key_phrases.text: Is it all you can eat?
How much time do we have?

questions.q: Welcome to the Grand Buffet! Is this your first time here?
questions.q_ko: 그랜드 뷔페에 오신 걸 환영해요! 처음 오셨나요?
questions.sample: Yes, it is. Is it all you can eat?

questions.q: Yes, for two hours. Would you like drinks included?
questions.sample: Yes, please. What drinks do you have?

questions.q: We have soda, juice, and coffee. What are you hungry for?
questions.q_ko: 탄산음료, 주스, 커피가 있어요. 어떤 음식이 당기세요?
questions.sample: I'd like seafood and some grilled meat.

questions.q: The seafood is on the left. What's your strategy to get the most for your money?
questions.q_ko: 해산물은 왼쪽에 있어요. 본전 뽑으려면 어떤 작전이세요?
questions.sample: I'll start with small plates so I can try everything.

questions.q: Smart! Do you save room for dessert?
questions.q_ko: 현명하네요! 디저트 먹을 자리는 남겨 두세요?
questions.sample: Always! Where are the desserts?

closing: The desserts are by the window. Enjoy your meal!
closing_ko: 디저트는 창가 쪽에 있어요. 맛있게 드세요!

title: Street Food Market
situation_ko: 야시장에서 길거리 음식을 사 먹어요.
user_role: A tourist at a night market

questions.q: Come try my grilled skewers! What are you looking for?
questions.q_ko: 제 꼬치구이 드셔 보세요! 뭘 찾으세요?
questions.sample: What is this called?

questions.q: That's chicken satay with peanut sauce. Do you like peanut sauce?
questions.q_ko: 치킨 사테인데 땅콩 소스를 곁들여요. 땅콩 소스 좋아하세요?
questions.sample: Yes, I do. Is it spicy?

questions.q: It's mild. I can add chili if you want. Do you want it spicy?
questions.q_ko: 순해요. 원하시면 고추를 넣어 드려요. 맵게 해 드릴까요?
questions.sample: Just a little, please.

questions.q: How many would you like?
questions.sample: I'll take two skewers.

questions.q: Is this your first time at the night market?
questions.sample: Yes, I'm visiting for the weekend.

closing: Welcome to town! Try the mango dessert on the next corner too.
closing_ko: 이곳에 오신 걸 환영해요! 다음 모퉁이의 망고 디저트도 드셔 보세요.

title: Wine Tasting
situation_ko: 와인 가게에서 저녁 식사에 어울리는 와인을 골라요.

key_phrases.text: I'm looking for a red wine.
It's for a dinner with friends.

questions.q: Hello! What kind of wine are you looking for?
questions.sample: I'm looking for a red wine.

questions.q: Good choice! What is the occasion?
questions.sample: It's for a dinner with friends.

questions.q: Lovely. What will you be eating?
questions.sample: We're having steak and roasted vegetables.

questions.q: A bold red would be perfect. What's your budget?
questions.q_ko: 진한 레드가 딱이에요. 예산은 어느 정도세요?
questions.sample: Something not too expensive, around thirty dollars.

questions.q: I have a nice one. Do you prefer dry or sweet wine?
questions.q_ko: 좋은 게 있어요. 드라이한 와인이 좋으세요, 달콤한 와인이 좋으세요?
questions.sample: I prefer dry wine.

closing: This one is perfect. I hope your friends enjoy it!
closing_ko: 이게 딱이에요. 친구분들이 좋아하시길 바라요!

title: Splitting a Pizza
situation_ko: 친구와 함께 피자를 나눠 먹고 비용을 나눠요.

questions.q: This pizza smells great! Which topping do you like best?
questions.q_ko: 이 피자 냄새 정말 좋다! 어떤 토핑이 제일 좋아?
questions.sample: I like mushrooms and cheese the most.

questions.q: Me too! How many slices can you eat?
questions.q_ko: 나도! 몇 조각이나 먹을 수 있어?
questions.sample: Probably three. I'm really hungry.

questions.q: Ha, nice. There's one slice left. Do you want it?
questions.q_ko: 하하, 좋네. 한 조각 남았어. 먹을래?
questions.sample: Yes, I'll take the last slice.

questions.q: Okay. Should we split the bill?
questions.sample: No, it's my treat today.

questions.q: Thanks so much! What should we do next time?
questions.sample: Next time, maybe you can pick the restaurant.

closing: Deal! I'll find a good place. Thanks again for the pizza!
closing_ko: 좋아! 좋은 곳 찾아볼게. 피자 다시 한번 고마워!

title: Cooking Class
situation_ko: 요리 수업에서 강사에게 질문하며 요리를 배워요.
user_role: A student in a cooking class

key_phrases.text: How do I chop the onion?

questions.q: Welcome to the class! Have you cooked pasta before?
questions.q_ko: 수업에 오신 걸 환영해요! 파스타를 만들어 본 적 있어요?
questions.sample: A few times, but mine is never very good.
questions.sample_ko: 몇 번 해 봤는데 맛이 별로예요.

questions.q: That's okay! Let's start with the sauce. How do I chop an onion? Can you show me?
questions.q_ko: 괜찮아요! 소스부터 시작해요. 양파를 어떻게 썰죠? 보여 줄 수 있나요?
questions.sample: I cut it in half, then slice it thin.

questions.q: Good job! Now we add tomatoes. Is this enough salt?
questions.q_ko: 잘했어요! 이제 토마토를 넣어요. 소금은 이 정도면 충분할까요?
questions.sample: I think a little more would be better.

questions.q: Right! How do you know when the pasta is ready?
questions.q_ko: 맞아요! 파스타가 다 됐는지 어떻게 알죠?
questions.sample: I taste a piece. It should be soft, but not too soft.
questions.sample_ko: 한 가닥 먹어 봐요. 부드럽지만 너무 퍼지면 안 돼요.

questions.q: Exactly. Would you like to cook this at home?
questions.sample: Yes, I want to make it for my family.

closing: Wonderful work today! Take the recipe home and have fun.
closing_ko: 오늘 정말 잘하셨어요! 레시피를 가져가서 즐겁게 만들어 보세요.

title: Diet Talk
situation_ko: 건강을 위해 식단을 바꾸려는 친구와 이야기해요.
ai_role: A friend trying to eat healthier

key_phrases.text: I try to drink more water.

questions.q: I want to eat healthier. Do you have any tips?
questions.q_ko: 더 건강하게 먹고 싶어. 조언 있어?
questions.sample: Try eating more vegetables.

questions.q: Okay! What should I stop eating?
questions.sample: Maybe sweet drinks and fried food.

questions.q: That's hard! I love fried chicken. What do you eat when you want a snack?
questions.q_ko: 어렵네! 난 치킨이 너무 좋은데. 간식이 먹고 싶을 땐 뭘 먹어?
questions.sample: I eat fruit or nuts.

questions.q: Good idea. Should I skip dinner to lose weight?
questions.q_ko: 좋은 생각이야. 살 빼려면 저녁을 거를까?
questions.sample: No, don't skip meals. Just eat smaller portions.
questions.sample_ko: 아니, 끼니를 거르지 마. 양을 줄이면 돼.

questions.q: Makes sense. Will you walk with me after dinner?
questions.q_ko: 일리 있네. 저녁 먹고 나랑 같이 걸을래?
questions.sample: Sure, that sounds fun.

closing: Thanks for your help! I feel more motivated now.
closing_ko: 도와줘서 고마워! 이제 의욕이 생겨.

title: Dinner Invitation
situation_ko: 친구를 저녁 식사에 초대하고 메뉴를 정해요.
ai_role: A friend you invite for dinner

key_phrases.text: Would you like to come for dinner?
Is there anything you can't eat?

questions.q: Hi! What are you up to this weekend?
questions.sample: Not much. Would you like to come for dinner on Saturday?
questions.sample_ko: 별일 없어. 토요일에 저녁 먹으러 올래?

questions.q: I'd love to! What are you going to cook?
questions.sample: I'll cook my special dish, beef stew.
questions.sample_ko: 내 특별 요리인 소고기 스튜를 만들게.

questions.q: That sounds delicious. Should I bring something?
questions.sample: Maybe some dessert or a drink.

questions.q: Okay. I'm allergic to shrimp. Is that a problem?
questions.q_ko: 알았어. 나 새우 알레르기 있는데, 괜찮을까?
questions.sample: No problem. There's no shrimp in the stew.

questions.q: Great. What time should I come?
questions.sample: Around six thirty.

closing: Perfect! I can't wait. See you on Saturday!
closing_ko: 완벽해! 너무 기대돼. 토요일에 봐!

title: Coffee Shop Regular
situation_ko: 자주 가는 카페에서 바리스타와 가볍게 대화해요.

questions.q: Good morning! Same as usual?
questions.q_ko: 좋은 아침이에요! 늘 먹던 걸로 드릴까요?
questions.sample: The usual, please.

questions.q: Coming up! Would you like to try our new seasonal drink?
questions.q_ko: 곧 드릴게요! 새로 나온 시즌 음료 한번 드셔 보실래요?
questions.sample: What is it? I might try it tomorrow.
questions.sample_ko: 어떤 거예요? 내일 마셔 볼까 해요.

questions.q: It's a pumpkin latte. Do you like sweet drinks?
questions.sample: Sometimes, but I prefer coffee strong.
questions.sample_ko: 가끔요. 하지만 커피는 진한 게 좋아요.

questions.q: I'll make it stronger. How is work these days?
questions.q_ko: 더 진하게 해 드릴게요. 요즘 일은 어떠세요?
questions.sample: Busy, but good. Coffee helps me a lot.
questions.sample_ko: 바쁘지만 좋아요. 커피가 큰 도움이 돼요.

questions.q: Glad to hear it. Do you have plans for the weekend?
questions.sample: I'm going to relax and try a new cafe.
questions.sample_ko: 쉬면서 새로운 카페에 가 볼 거예요.

closing: Sounds lovely. Here's your coffee. Have a great day!
closing_ko: 좋네요. 커피 나왔어요. 좋은 하루 보내세요!

title: Restaurant Review
situation_ko: 최근 다녀온 식당에 대한 경험과 의견을 이야기해요.
ai_role: A friend asking about a restaurant

key_phrases.text: The service was great, but it was pricey.
I'd recommend it if you like seafood.
It lived up to the hype.

questions.q: I heard you went to that new seafood place. How was it?
questions.q_ko: 새로 생긴 해산물 식당에 갔다고 들었어요. 어땠어요?
questions.sample: It was pretty good. The service was great, but it was pricey.

questions.q: Oh, really? What did you order, and how was it?
questions.sample: I had grilled fish. It was fresh and perfectly cooked.
questions.sample_ko: 생선구이를 먹었는데 신선하고 딱 알맞게 익었어요.

questions.q: Sounds tasty! Was there anything you didn't like?
questions.q_ko: 맛있겠네요! 마음에 안 든 건 없었어요?
questions.sample: The soup was too salty for me, and the portions were small.

questions.q: I see. Would you go back, considering the price?
questions.q_ko: 그렇군요. 가격을 생각하면 다시 갈 것 같아요?
questions.sample: Probably for a special occasion, but not for a casual dinner.
questions.sample_ko: 특별한 날에는 갈 것 같지만 평범한 저녁에는 아니에요.

questions.q: That makes sense. Who would you recommend it to?
questions.sample: I'd recommend it if you like seafood and want a nice atmosphere.
questions.sample_ko: 해산물을 좋아하고 분위기 좋은 곳을 원하면 추천해요.

closing: Thanks for the honest review. I'll save it for a special day!
closing_ko: 솔직한 후기 고마워요. 특별한 날을 위해 아껴 둘게요!

title: Eating Out vs Cooking
situation_ko: 외식과 집에서 요리하는 것 중 어느 쪽이 나은지 토론해요.

key_phrases.text: I think cooking at home is healthier.
key_phrases.ko: 집에서 요리하는 게 더 건강하다고 생각해요.

key_phrases.text: On the other hand, eating out saves time.

questions.q: Do you usually cook at home or eat out?
questions.sample: It depends on my schedule, but I cook about four times a week.
questions.sample_ko: 일정에 따라 다른데, 일주일에 네 번쯤 요리해요.

questions.q: Why do you prefer that?
questions.sample: I think cooking at home is healthier and cheaper.
questions.sample_ko: 집에서 요리하는 게 더 건강하고 저렴하다고 생각해요.

questions.q: That's true. But what do you enjoy about eating out?
questions.q_ko: 맞아요. 그래도 외식의 좋은 점은 뭐라고 생각해요?
questions.sample: It saves time, and I can try dishes I can't make myself.
questions.sample_ko: 시간이 절약되고, 제가 못 만드는 요리를 먹어 볼 수 있어요.

questions.q: Good point. Do you think people eat out too much these days?
questions.q_ko: 좋은 지적이에요. 요즘 사람들이 외식을 너무 많이 한다고 생각해요?
questions.sample: I think so. Many people are too busy to cook, so they rely on delivery.
questions.sample_ko: 그런 것 같아요. 너무 바빠서 요리를 못 하고 배달에 의존하죠.

questions.q: How could people cook at home more often?
questions.q_ko: 사람들이 집에서 더 자주 요리하려면 어떻게 해야 할까요?
questions.sample: They could plan meals on weekends and prepare simple ingredients ahead.
questions.sample_ko: 주말에 식단을 짜고 간단한 재료를 미리 준비하면 돼요.

closing: Great points on both sides. Maybe a balance is best!
closing_ko: 양쪽 다 좋은 의견이에요. 균형을 맞추는 게 최선일지도 몰라요!

title: Explaining Korean Hansik
situation_ko: 한국 음식의 특징과 매력을 외국인에게 설명해요.
ai_role: A foreign visitor curious about Korean food

key_phrases.text: Korean meals usually include many side dishes.
Fermented food is a big part of our diet.
key_phrases.ko: 발효 음식은 우리 식단의 큰 부분이에요.

key_phrases.text: We share dishes at the table.

questions.q: What makes Korean food special compared to other cuisines?
questions.q_ko: 한국 음식은 다른 나라 음식과 비교해 뭐가 특별한가요?
questions.sample: Korean meals usually include many side dishes, and everything is shared.
questions.sample_ko: 한국 식사는 보통 반찬이 많고 모든 걸 함께 나눠 먹어요.

questions.q: Interesting! Why is kimchi so important?
questions.sample: Fermented food is a big part of our diet, and it's good for digestion.
questions.sample_ko: 발효 음식은 우리 식단의 큰 부분이고 소화에 좋아요.

questions.q: I see. Is Korean food healthy, in your opinion?
questions.sample: Mostly, yes, because there are many vegetables. But some dishes are high in salt.
questions.sample_ko: 대체로 그래요, 채소가 많으니까요. 하지만 짠 음식도 있어요.

questions.q: Which dish would you recommend for someone who can't eat spicy food?
questions.q_ko: 매운 걸 못 먹는 사람에게는 어떤 음식을 추천하세요?
questions.sample: I'd recommend galbitang or bulgogi because they're mild and sweet.

questions.q: Has Korean food changed in recent years?
questions.q_ko: 최근 몇 년 사이 한식이 바뀌었나요?
questions.sample: Yes, it has become more global, and young people mix traditional and modern styles.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 더 세계화되었고 젊은 사람들은 전통과 현대 스타일을 섞어요.

closing: Thank you! I'm excited to explore Korean food even more.
closing_ko: 고마워요! 한식을 더 많이 알아보는 게 기대돼요.

title: Handling a Bad Restaurant Experience
situation_ko: 식당에서 오래 기다리고 불친절한 서비스를 받아 정중하게 항의해요.

key_phrases.text: We've been waiting for over an hour.
I'd appreciate it if you could look into it.

questions.q: Hello, I heard there was a problem at your table. What happened?
questions.q_ko: 안녕하세요, 테이블에 문제가 있었다고 들었어요. 어떤 일이었나요?
questions.sample: We've been waiting for over an hour, and our food still hasn't arrived.
questions.sample_ko: 한 시간 넘게 기다렸는데 음식이 아직 안 나왔어요.

questions.q: I'm so sorry. How did the staff respond when you asked?
questions.q_ko: 정말 죄송합니다. 문의하셨을 때 직원이 어떻게 응대했나요?
questions.sample: I understand it's busy, but the server was rude and said it was not his fault.
questions.sample_ko: 바쁜 건 알지만, 직원이 불친절했고 자기 잘못이 아니라고 했어요.

questions.q: That's unacceptable. What would you like us to do?
questions.q_ko: 용납될 수 없는 일이네요. 저희가 어떻게 해 드릴까요?
questions.sample: I'd appreciate it if you could bring our food quickly and look into what went wrong.
questions.sample_ko: 음식을 빨리 가져다주시고, 무엇이 잘못됐는지 확인해 주시면 감사하겠어요.

questions.q: We'll do both. We'd also like to offer a discount. Would that be fair for you?
questions.q_ko: 두 가지 모두 해 드릴게요. 할인도 제공하고 싶은데 공정할까요?
questions.sample: That would be fair, thank you. I just want good service next time.
questions.sample_ko: 공정하네요, 고마워요. 다음엔 좋은 서비스를 받고 싶을 뿐이에요.

questions.q: Absolutely. Would you consider coming back after this experience?
questions.q_ko: 물론이죠. 이번 일 이후에도 다시 와 주실 건가요?
questions.sample: Maybe, if things improve. Your food usually tastes good.

closing: Thank you for your patience and honesty. We'll do better.
closing_ko: 참아 주시고 솔직히 말씀해 주셔서 감사합니다. 더 잘하겠습니다.

title: Fast Food Debate
situation_ko: 패스트푸드가 건강과 사회에 미치는 영향에 대해 의견을 나눠요.

key_phrases.text: In my opinion, fast food is fine in moderation.
key_phrases.ko: 제 생각에 패스트푸드는 적당히 먹으면 괜찮아요.

key_phrases.text: The main problem is that it's high in fat.
It's convenient, but not very healthy.

questions.q: How often do you eat fast food?
questions.sample: About twice a month, when I'm too busy to cook.
questions.sample_ko: 한 달에 두 번쯤, 너무 바빠서 요리할 시간이 없을 때요.

questions.q: Why do you think it's so popular?
questions.sample: It's convenient, cheap, and fast, so it fits busy lives.
questions.sample_ko: 편리하고 싸고 빨라서 바쁜 생활에 맞아요.

questions.q: True. What are the main problems with it?
questions.sample: The main problem is that it's high in fat and sugar, and portions are big.
questions.sample_ko: 지방과 당이 많고 양도 많다는 게 가장 큰 문제예요.

questions.q: Should governments limit fast food advertising to children?
questions.q_ko: 정부가 어린이 대상 패스트푸드 광고를 제한해야 할까요?
questions.sample: I think so, because children are easily influenced by ads.
questions.sample_ko: 그렇다고 생각해요. 아이들은 광고에 쉽게 영향을 받으니까요.

questions.q: So is fast food always bad in your view?
questions.sample: No, in my opinion, it's fine in moderation if you balance it with healthy meals.
questions.sample_ko: 아니요, 제 생각엔 건강한 식사와 균형을 맞춘다면 적당히 먹는 건 괜찮아요.

closing: Great discussion! Balance really seems to be the key.
closing_ko: 좋은 토론이었어요! 결국 균형이 핵심인 것 같아요.

title: Food Memories
situation_ko: 어린 시절 추억이 담긴 음식에 대해 이야기해요.

key_phrases.text: It reminds me of my grandmother.

questions.q: Is there a dish that reminds you of your childhood?
questions.sample: Yes, my grandmother's kimchi stew. I grew up eating it.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 할머니의 김치찌개요. 어릴 때부터 먹고 자랐어요.

questions.q: That sounds special! What was it like when she made it?
questions.q_ko: 특별하네요! 할머니가 만들어 주실 때는 어땠어요?
questions.sample: The whole house smelled amazing, and the family gathered around the table.
questions.sample_ko: 온 집에 좋은 냄새가 가득했고 가족이 식탁에 모였어요.

questions.q: Can you make it yourself now?
questions.sample: I try, but nothing tastes quite like hers. She used a special secret.
questions.sample_ko: 해 보지만 할머니 맛은 안 나요. 비법이 있으셨거든요.

questions.q: Why do you think food has such a strong link to memories?
questions.q_ko: 음식은 왜 기억과 그렇게 강하게 연결된다고 생각해요?
questions.sample: Because smells and tastes are tied to emotions, so they bring back moments instantly.
questions.sample_ko: 냄새와 맛이 감정과 연결되어서 그 순간을 바로 떠올리게 하니까요.

questions.q: Do you want to pass this recipe on to someone?
questions.q_ko: 이 요리법을 누군가에게 전해 주고 싶나요?
questions.sample: Yes, I'd like to teach my children someday.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 언젠가 아이들에게 가르쳐 주고 싶어요.

closing: What a beautiful tradition. Thank you for sharing your memory.
closing_ko: 아름다운 전통이네요. 추억을 나눠 줘서 고마워요.

title: Sustainable Eating
situation_ko: 환경을 생각하는 식습관에 대해 의견을 나눠요.

key_phrases.text: I try to buy local produce.
It's hard to change old habits.

questions.q: Do you think about the environment when you buy food?
questions.sample: Sometimes. I try to buy local produce when I can.
questions.sample_ko: 가끔요. 가능하면 지역 농산물을 사려고 해요.

questions.q: That's great. How do you deal with leftovers?
questions.sample: I save them for lunch the next day, so I don't waste food.
questions.sample_ko: 다음 날 점심으로 먹어서 버리지 않아요.

questions.q: Smart. Why do you think so much food gets thrown away?
questions.q_ko: 현명하네요. 왜 그렇게 많은 음식이 버려진다고 생각해요?
questions.sample: People buy too much, and restaurants prepare large portions.
questions.sample_ko: 사람들이 너무 많이 사고 식당도 양을 많이 준비하니까요.

questions.q: Would you eat less meat to help the planet?
questions.q_ko: 지구를 위해 고기를 덜 먹을 수 있나요?
questions.sample: I could try, but it's hard to change old habits. Maybe a meat-free day each week.
questions.sample_ko: 노력은 해 볼 수 있지만 오래된 습관을 바꾸기는 어려워요. 일주일에 하루 정도는 가능하겠어요.

questions.q: Do you think companies and governments should do more?
questions.q_ko: 기업과 정부가 더 노력해야 한다고 생각해요?
questions.sample: Yes, they should make healthy, sustainable food cheaper and easier to find.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 건강하고 지속 가능한 음식을 더 싸고 구하기 쉽게 만들어야 해요.

closing: Small steps matter. Thanks for such a thoughtful chat!
closing_ko: 작은 실천이 중요해요. 생각 깊은 대화 고마워요!

title: Choosing a Restaurant for a Business Dinner
situation_ko: 해외 거래처 손님과의 저녁 식사 장소를 동료와 상의해요.
ai_role: A coworker helping to plan a business dinner

key_phrases.text: I'd suggest a place with set menus.
We need to ask about dietary restrictions.

questions.q: We're taking our client to dinner on Thursday. What kind of restaurant should we pick?
questions.q_ko: 목요일에 거래처 손님을 저녁에 모실 거예요. 어떤 식당이 좋을까요?
questions.sample: We should pick somewhere quiet so we can talk.
questions.sample_ko: 대화할 수 있게 조용한 곳을 골라야 해요.

questions.q: Good point. Should we choose Korean food or something more familiar to them?
questions.q_ko: 좋은 지적이에요. 한식이 좋을까요, 아니면 그분들에게 익숙한 음식이 좋을까요?
questions.sample: I'd suggest Korean food, but a mild dish, since it's a nice way to share our culture.
questions.sample_ko: 한식을 추천하지만 순한 요리로요. 우리 문화를 알리기 좋으니까요.

questions.q: I like that. What should we ask them before we book?
questions.q_ko: 좋아요. 예약 전에 그분들에게 뭘 물어봐야 할까요?
questions.sample: We need to ask about dietary restrictions and allergies.
questions.sample_ko: 식이 제한이나 알레르기가 있는지 물어봐야 해요.

questions.q: Right. Is it better to order for everyone or let them choose?
questions.q_ko: 맞아요. 모두를 위해 우리가 주문하는 게 나을까요, 직접 고르게 하는 게 나을까요?
questions.sample: I'd suggest a place with set menus, so it's easy and nobody feels pressure.
questions.sample_ko: 코스 메뉴가 있는 곳이 편하고 부담도 없을 것 같아요.

questions.q: Great idea. How should we handle the bill?
questions.sample: Our company should pay, and one of us should do it discreetly before we leave.
questions.sample_ko: 회사가 내야 하고, 나가기 전에 한 명이 눈에 띄지 않게 계산하면 돼요.

closing: Perfect, I'll make the reservation. Thanks for the great ideas!
closing_ko: 좋아요, 제가 예약할게요. 좋은 아이디어 고마워요!

title: Cooking for a Large Family Gathering
situation_ko: 명절이나 큰 모임을 위한 음식 준비에 대해 이야기해요.
ai_role: A relative helping in the kitchen

key_phrases.text: It takes days to prepare everything.
Everyone helps with a different task.
It's tiring, but it brings us together.

questions.q: The holiday is almost here. What dishes do you usually prepare?
questions.q_ko: 명절이 거의 다 됐어요. 보통 어떤 음식을 준비해요?
questions.sample: We make rice cakes, pancakes, and lots of side dishes. It takes days to prepare everything.
questions.sample_ko: 떡, 전, 반찬을 많이 만들어요. 모두 준비하는 데 며칠이 걸려요.

questions.q: Wow! How do you organize the work?
questions.sample: Everyone helps with a different task, like chopping, frying, and setting the table.
questions.sample_ko: 모두 썰기, 부치기, 상 차리기처럼 다른 일을 맡아요.

questions.q: That sounds fair. Do you think the work is divided equally between men and women?
questions.q_ko: 공평하게 들리네요. 일이 남녀 사이에 평등하게 나뉜다고 생각해요?
questions.sample: Not always. In the past women did most of it, but it's changing in our family.
questions.sample_ko: 항상 그렇진 않아요. 예전엔 여자들이 대부분 했지만 우리 가족은 변하고 있어요.

questions.q: Good to hear. Is it worth all the effort?
questions.q_ko: 다행이네요. 이 모든 수고가 가치가 있나요?
questions.sample: Yes. It's tiring, but it brings us together.
questions.sample_ko: 네. 힘들지만 가족을 하나로 모아 줘요.

questions.q: If you could change one thing about the holiday meal, what would it be?
questions.q_ko: 명절 음식에서 한 가지를 바꿀 수 있다면 뭘 바꾸고 싶어요?
questions.sample: I'd make fewer dishes so we waste less food and have more time to talk.
questions.sample_ko: 음식을 덜 만들어서 낭비를 줄이고 대화할 시간을 늘리고 싶어요.

closing: Beautiful. Food and family really do belong together.
closing_ko: 아름답네요. 음식과 가족은 정말 잘 어울려요.

title: Trying Unusual Food
situation_ko: 여행 중 낯선 음식을 먹어 본 경험에 대해 이야기해요.

key_phrases.text: I was nervous at first, but it was surprisingly good.
You never know until you try.

questions.q: Have you ever tried a food that seemed strange to you?
questions.q_ko: 이상해 보이는 음식을 먹어 본 적 있어요?
questions.sample: Yes, I tried raw octopus once. I was nervous at first, but it was surprisingly good.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 한 번 산낙지를 먹어 봤어요. 처음엔 긴장했는데 의외로 맛있었어요.

questions.q: Brave! What was the texture like?
questions.sample: The texture was strange, chewy and a bit slippery.

questions.q: Why did you decide to try it?
questions.sample: My friends encouraged me, and I didn't want to miss a local experience.
questions.sample_ko: 친구들이 권했고 현지 경험을 놓치고 싶지 않았어요.

questions.q: Is there any food you would never try?
questions.q_ko: 절대 안 먹어 볼 음식도 있어요?
questions.sample: Probably insects. I just can't get past the idea.
questions.sample_ko: 아마 곤충이요. 생각만 해도 못 하겠어요.

questions.q: Do you think trying new foods helps you understand a culture?
questions.q_ko: 새로운 음식을 먹어 보는 게 문화를 이해하는 데 도움이 된다고 생각해요?
questions.sample: Definitely. You never know until you try, and food tells you about people's history.
questions.sample_ko: 물론이죠. 먹어 보기 전엔 모르고, 음식은 사람들의 역사를 알려 줘요.

closing: I agree. Food is the best way to explore the world!
closing_ko: 저도 그래요. 음식은 세상을 탐험하는 최고의 방법이에요!

title: Meal Prep Advice
situation_ko: 바쁜 직장인이 일주일 식사를 미리 준비하는 방법을 이야기해요.
ai_role: A busy coworker who wants advice
user_role: A coworker with meal prep experience

key_phrases.text: I spend Sunday afternoon cooking for the week.
key_phrases.ko: 일요일 오후에 한 주 치 요리를 해요.

key_phrases.text: It saves both time and money.

questions.q: I never have time to cook on weekdays. How do you manage?
questions.q_ko: 저는 평일에 요리할 시간이 전혀 없어요. 어떻게 해요?
questions.sample: I spend Sunday afternoon cooking for the week.
questions.sample_ko: 일요일 오후에 한 주 치 요리를 해 둬요.

questions.q: Really? What kinds of food keep well?
questions.sample: Rice, roasted vegetables, and soups are good, and chicken stays fresh for three days.
questions.sample_ko: 밥, 구운 채소, 수프가 좋고 닭고기는 3일은 괜찮아요.

questions.q: How do you store everything?
questions.sample: I store it in separate containers and freeze some portions.

questions.q: Do you get bored of eating the same food?
questions.q_ko: 같은 음식을 먹다 보면 질리지 않아요?
questions.sample: Sometimes, so I use different sauces and vary the vegetables.
questions.sample_ko: 가끔요. 그래서 소스를 바꾸고 채소를 다르게 해요.

questions.q: Is it really worth the effort?
questions.sample: Yes, it saves both time and money, and I eat healthier.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 시간과 돈이 절약되고 더 건강하게 먹게 돼요.

closing: Every culture has its own way. Thanks for explaining yours!
