questions.q: You look tired lately. How do you balance work and your personal life?
questions.q_ko: 요즘 피곤해 보여요. 일과 개인 생활의 균형은 어떻게 맞춰요?
questions.sample: Honestly, it's hard, but I try to leave on time at least three days a week.
questions.sample_ko: 솔직히 어렵지만 적어도 주 3일은 정시에 퇴근하려고 해요.

questions.q: That's a good start. Why is balance important to you?
questions.q_ko: 좋은 시작이에요. 왜 균형이 중요하다고 생각해요?
questions.sample: Because if I don't rest, I get stressed and my work quality gets worse.
questions.sample_ko: 쉬지 않으면 스트레스를 받고 일의 질도 떨어지니까요.

questions.q: I feel the same. How do you recharge after a hard week?
questions.q_ko: 저도 그래요. 힘든 한 주 뒤에는 어떻게 재충전해요?
questions.sample: I sleep late, cook something nice, and go for a long walk.
questions.sample_ko: 늦잠 자고, 맛있는 걸 요리하고, 오래 산책해요.

questions.q: Sounds relaxing. Do you check work messages on your days off?
questions.q_ko: 편안하겠어요. 쉬는 날에도 업무 메시지를 확인해요?
questions.sample: I used to, but I've learned to set boundaries and turn off notifications.
questions.sample_ko: 예전엔 그랬지만 선을 긋는 법을 배워서 알림을 꺼 둬요.

questions.q: Smart. What advice would you give to someone who works too much?
questions.q_ko: 현명하네요. 일을 너무 많이 하는 사람에게 어떤 조언을 하겠어요?
questions.sample: I'd say your health is more important than any deadline, so take breaks.
questions.sample_ko: 건강이 어떤 마감보다 중요하니 쉬라고 말해 줄 거예요.

closing: Good advice. Let's both try to rest more this month!
closing_ko: 좋은 조언이에요. 이번 달엔 우리 둘 다 더 쉬어 봐요!

title: Handling a Disagreement
situation_ko: 프로젝트 방향을 두고 동료와 의견이 달라요.
ai_role: A coworker who disagrees with you
user_role: A team member in a disagreement

questions.q: I don't think your plan will work. I prefer the other approach. Why did you choose yours?
questions.q_ko: 당신 계획이 잘 될 것 같지 않아요. 저는 다른 방법이 좋아요. 왜 당신 방법을 선택했어요?
questions.sample: I chose it because it's cheaper and we can start right away.
questions.sample_ko: 더 저렴하고 바로 시작할 수 있어서 선택했어요.

questions.q: But it might be less reliable. What do you think about that risk?
questions.q_ko: 하지만 덜 안정적일 수 있어요. 그 위험은 어떻게 생각해요?
questions.sample: I see your point, but I think we can reduce the risk by testing it first.
questions.sample_ko: 무슨 말인지 알지만 먼저 시험해 보면 위험을 줄일 수 있다고 생각해요.

questions.q: Hmm. What's good about my approach, in your honest opinion?
questions.q_ko: 음. 솔직히 제 방법의 좋은 점은 뭐라고 생각해요?
questions.sample: It's more stable, and customers might trust it more.
questions.sample_ko: 더 안정적이고 고객들이 더 믿을 수 있을 거예요.

questions.q: Thanks for being fair. How can we solve this?
questions.q_ko: 공정하게 말해 줘서 고마워요. 이걸 어떻게 해결할 수 있을까요?
questions.sample: Let's find a middle ground, or test both ideas for a week.
questions.sample_ko: 절충안을 찾거나 두 아이디어를 일주일간 시험해 봐요.

questions.q: That's reasonable. Should we ask our manager to decide?
questions.sample: Yes, if we can't agree, we should show them the results and let them decide.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 합의가 안 되면 결과를 보여 드리고 결정하게 해요.

closing: Thanks for talking this through calmly. I feel better now.
closing_ko: 차분히 이야기해 줘서 고마워요. 이제 마음이 편해요.

title: Receiving Criticism
situation_ko: 상사에게 보고서에 대한 날카로운 지적을 들어요.

key_phrases.text: I can see why that's a problem.

questions.q: I read your report, and I have some concerns. The conclusion isn't very clear. How do you feel about that?
questions.q_ko: 보고서를 읽었는데 걱정되는 부분이 있어요. 결론이 명확하지 않아요. 어떻게 생각해요?
questions.sample: Thank you for being honest. I can see why that's a problem.
questions.sample_ko: 솔직하게 말해 줘서 고마워요. 왜 문제인지 알겠어요.

questions.q: I appreciate your attitude. What do you think made it unclear?
questions.q_ko: 당신의 태도가 고마워요. 뭐 때문에 불분명해졌다고 생각해요?
questions.sample: I think I included too much data and didn't explain the main point.
questions.sample_ko: 데이터를 너무 많이 넣고 핵심을 설명하지 않은 것 같아요.

questions.q: Exactly. How would you improve it?
questions.sample: I'd start with a short summary and keep only the most important charts.
questions.sample_ko: 짧은 요약으로 시작하고 가장 중요한 차트만 남길 거예요.

questions.q: That sounds good. How long will you need?
questions.sample: I can fix it by tomorrow afternoon.

questions.q: Fine. How do you usually feel when you get criticism?
questions.q_ko: 좋아요. 비판을 들으면 보통 어떤 기분이에요?
questions.sample: It's uncomfortable at first, but I know it helps me grow.
questions.sample_ko: 처음엔 불편하지만 성장에 도움이 된다는 걸 알아요.

closing: That's a great attitude. I'm looking forward to the new version.
closing_ko: 훌륭한 태도예요. 새 버전을 기대할게요.

title: Asking for a Raise
situation_ko: 성과를 바탕으로 연봉 인상을 요청해요.
user_role: An employee asking for a raise

key_phrases.text: I'd like to discuss my salary.
I understand if it's not possible now.

questions.q: Please, have a seat. What did you want to talk about?
questions.sample: I'd like to discuss my salary, if now is a good time.
questions.sample_ko: 괜찮은 때라면 연봉에 대해 이야기하고 싶어요.

questions.q: Of course. Why do you think you deserve a raise?
questions.q_ko: 물론이죠. 왜 인상받을 자격이 있다고 생각해요?
questions.sample: Over the past year, I've taken on more tasks and trained two new employees.
questions.sample_ko: 지난 1년간 업무를 더 맡고 신입 두 명을 교육했어요.

questions.q: That's true. How much of a raise are you hoping for?
questions.sample: Based on my research, I was hoping for around ten percent.

questions.q: That's a bit high for this budget. Would you consider other benefits, like extra vacation days?
questions.q_ko: 이번 예산으로는 조금 높아요. 휴가 같은 다른 혜택은 고려할 수 있어요?
questions.sample: Yes, I'd be open to that, especially more flexible hours.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 특히 유연 근무 같은 건 열려 있어요.

questions.q: I see. What if we can't do it right now?
questions.q_ko: 그렇군요. 지금 당장 안 되면 어떻게 할래요?
questions.sample: I understand if it's not possible now. Could we talk again in six months?
questions.sample_ko: 지금은 어려우시다면 이해해요. 6개월 뒤에 다시 이야기할 수 있을까요?

closing: That's fair. Let me talk to HR and get back to you next week.
closing_ko: 공정해요. 인사팀과 이야기하고 다음 주에 알려 줄게요.

title: Changing Jobs
situation_ko: 이직을 고민 중인 당신에게 친구가 조언해요.

questions.q: You seem unsure lately. What's on your mind?
questions.q_ko: 요즘 고민이 있어 보여요. 무슨 생각을 해요?
questions.sample: I'm thinking about changing jobs.

questions.q: Really? What's the main reason?
questions.sample: The main reason is that I'm not learning anything new anymore.
questions.sample_ko: 더 이상 새로 배우는 게 없어서요.

questions.q: I understand. Do you have another offer?
questions.sample: Yes, a startup offered me a position with a higher salary.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 스타트업에서 더 높은 연봉으로 제안했어요.

questions.q: Wow! But startups can be risky. What worries you most?
questions.q_ko: 와! 하지만 스타트업은 위험할 수 있어요. 가장 걱정되는 게 뭐예요?
questions.sample: I'm worried it might not be stable, and I'd have to work longer hours.
questions.sample_ko: 안정적이지 않을 수 있고 더 오래 일해야 할까 봐 걱정돼요.

questions.q: Fair. So, do you think the pros outweigh the cons?
questions.q_ko: 그렇죠. 그래서 장점이 단점보다 크다고 생각해요?
questions.sample: I think so, but I want to talk to some people there before I decide.
questions.sample_ko: 그런 것 같지만 결정하기 전에 거기 사람들과 이야기해 보고 싶어요.

closing: That's wise. Whatever you decide, I'll support you.
closing_ko: 현명해요. 뭘 결정하든 응원할게요.

title: Leading a Project
situation_ko: 처음으로 프로젝트 리더를 맡게 되어 계획을 이야기해요.

key_phrases.text: I'll make sure everyone knows their role.

questions.q: Congratulations on becoming the project leader! How do you feel?
questions.q_ko: 프로젝트 리더가 된 걸 축하해요! 기분이 어때요?
questions.sample: I'm excited, but also a little nervous because it's my first time.

questions.q: That's natural. What will be your first priority?
questions.q_ko: 자연스러운 일이에요. 가장 먼저 무엇을 할 거예요?
questions.sample: My first priority is to set clear goals and a realistic schedule.
questions.sample_ko: 명확한 목표와 현실적인 일정을 정하는 게 우선이에요.

questions.q: Good. How will you keep the team motivated?
questions.q_ko: 좋아요. 팀의 동기를 어떻게 유지할 거예요?
questions.sample: I'll make sure everyone knows their role and celebrate small wins together.
questions.sample_ko: 모두 자기 역할을 알게 하고 작은 성공도 함께 축하할 거예요.

questions.q: Nice. If you run into problems, what will you do?
questions.q_ko: 좋네요. 문제가 생기면 어떻게 할 거예요?
questions.sample: I'll talk to the team early and ask for help instead of hiding the problem.
questions.sample_ko: 문제를 숨기지 않고 일찍 팀과 이야기하고 도움을 구할 거예요.

questions.q: That's the right approach. What kind of leader do you want to be?
questions.q_ko: 옳은 접근이에요. 어떤 리더가 되고 싶어요?
questions.sample: I want to be a leader who listens and gives people trust and space to work.
questions.sample_ko: 잘 듣고 사람들을 믿고 일할 여유를 주는 리더가 되고 싶어요.

closing: I believe in you. Let me know how I can support you.
closing_ko: 당신을 믿어요. 제가 어떻게 도울 수 있을지 알려 줘요.

title: Company Culture
situation_ko: 이직 후보 회사의 문화에 대해 직원과 이야기해요.
ai_role: An employee at a company you may join

questions.q: Thanks for visiting our office. What would you like to know about us?
questions.q_ko: 저희 사무실에 방문해 줘서 고마워요. 저희에 대해 뭐가 궁금해요?
questions.sample: I'd like to know what the culture is like here.

questions.q: We're pretty open and friendly. What kind of workplace do you prefer?
questions.q_ko: 저희는 꽤 열려 있고 친근해요. 어떤 직장을 선호해요?
questions.sample: I prefer a place where people share ideas freely and respect each other.
questions.sample_ko: 아이디어를 자유롭게 나누고 서로 존중하는 곳이 좋아요.

questions.q: That's what we value too. Why is that important to you?
questions.q_ko: 저희도 그걸 중시해요. 왜 그게 중요해요?
questions.sample: That's important to me because I do my best work when I feel safe to speak up.
questions.sample_ko: 의견을 편하게 말할 수 있을 때 제 최선을 다하기 때문이에요.

questions.q: Makes sense. What did your last workplace do badly?
questions.q_ko: 이해해요. 이전 직장은 어떤 점이 아쉬웠어요?
questions.sample: Decisions were made only by managers, and employees rarely got feedback.
questions.sample_ko: 결정은 관리자만 내렸고 직원은 피드백을 거의 못 받았어요.

questions.q: I see. Do you think you'd fit in well here?
questions.q_ko: 그렇군요. 여기에 잘 어울릴 것 같아요?
questions.sample: I think so. Everyone seems friendly, and I like the open space.
questions.sample_ko: 그런 것 같아요. 다들 친절해 보이고 열린 공간이 마음에 들어요.

closing: Great. We'd love to see you join us. Thanks for visiting!
closing_ko: 좋아요. 함께하면 좋겠어요. 방문해 줘서 고마워요!

title: Managing Stress
situation_ko: 마감 압박으로 힘들어하는 당신에게 동료가 걱정해 줘요.

key_phrases.ko: 요즘 감당이 안 될 만큼 벅차요.

questions.q: You've seemed stressed this week. Is everything okay?
questions.q_ko: 이번 주에 스트레스 받는 것 같아 보여요. 괜찮아요?
questions.sample: Honestly, I've been feeling overwhelmed with all these deadlines.
questions.sample_ko: 솔직히 마감이 너무 많아서 감당이 안 돼요.

questions.q: I'm sorry. What's the biggest source of stress for you?
questions.q_ko: 안됐어요. 가장 큰 스트레스 원인이 뭐예요?
questions.sample: I think it's having too many tasks and not enough time to do them well.
questions.sample_ko: 할 일은 너무 많은데 잘 할 시간이 부족한 것 같아요.

questions.q: That sounds hard. What do you do to calm down?
questions.sample: It helps me to take a short walk or listen to music.
questions.sample_ko: 잠깐 걷거나 음악을 들으면 도움이 돼요.

questions.q: Good habits. Have you talked to your manager about your workload?
questions.q_ko: 좋은 습관이에요. 업무량에 대해 팀장님과 이야기해 봤어요?
questions.sample: Not yet. I was afraid it would look like I can't handle it.
questions.sample_ko: 아직요. 제가 감당 못하는 것처럼 보일까 봐 두려웠어요.

questions.q: I understand, but they'd want to know. What will you do?
questions.q_ko: 이해하지만 팀장님은 알고 싶어 할 거예요. 어떻게 할 거예요?
questions.sample: I think I should ask for support and choose which tasks are most important.
questions.sample_ko: 도움을 요청하고 가장 중요한 일을 정해야 할 것 같아요.

closing: I'm here if you need to talk. You're not alone.
closing_ko: 이야기하고 싶으면 언제든 있어요. 혼자가 아니에요.

title: Time Management
situation_ko: 일을 효율적으로 하는 방법에 대해 동료와 이야기해요.

key_phrases.text: I make a to-do list every morning.
key_phrases.ko: 매일 아침 할 일 목록을 만들어요.

key_phrases.text: I focus on one thing at a time.
It saves me a lot of time.

questions.q: You always seem so organized. How do you plan your day?
questions.q_ko: 항상 정리가 잘 되어 있는 것 같아요. 하루를 어떻게 계획해요?
questions.sample: I make a to-do list every morning and mark the most important tasks.
questions.sample_ko: 매일 아침 할 일 목록을 만들고 가장 중요한 일에 표시해요.

questions.q: Smart. What do you do when someone interrupts you?
questions.sample: I politely say I'll help later, because I try to focus on one thing at a time.
questions.sample_ko: 한 번에 하나에 집중하려고 하니까 나중에 도와주겠다고 정중히 말해요.

questions.q: I find that hard. Do you think multitasking is a good idea?
questions.q_ko: 저는 그게 어려워요. 멀티태스킹이 좋은 방법이라고 생각해요?
questions.sample: Not really. In my experience, it makes you slower and you make more mistakes.
questions.sample_ko: 별로요. 제 경험상 더 느려지고 실수도 늘어요.

questions.q: Interesting. How do you handle sudden urgent tasks?
questions.q_ko: 흥미롭네요. 갑자기 급한 일이 생기면 어떻게 해요?
questions.sample: I check what can wait, move it to tomorrow, and handle the urgent one first.
questions.sample_ko: 미룰 수 있는 걸 확인해 내일로 옮기고 급한 걸 먼저 처리해요.

questions.q: That makes sense. Do you use any apps or tools?
questions.sample: I use a simple calendar app. It saves me a lot of time.
questions.sample_ko: 간단한 캘린더 앱을 써요. 시간이 많이 절약돼요.

closing: Thanks for the tips. I'll try them starting tomorrow!
closing_ko: 팁 고마워요. 내일부터 해 볼게요!

title: Presenting an Idea
situation_ko: 새로운 아이디어를 임원진에게 제안해요.

key_phrases.text: We could start with a small trial.
key_phrases.ko: 작은 시범 운영부터 시작할 수 있어요.

questions.q: I have ten minutes. What idea would you like to share?
questions.sample: I'd like to propose a monthly learning day, where employees can study new skills.
questions.sample_ko: 직원들이 새 기술을 배울 수 있는 월간 학습의 날을 제안하고 싶어요.

questions.q: Interesting. Why do you think we need it?
questions.sample: Because technology changes fast, and employees who keep learning bring more value to the company.
questions.sample_ko: 기술이 빠르게 변하고, 계속 배우는 직원이 회사에 더 큰 가치를 주기 때문이에요.

questions.q: What's the main benefit for the company?
questions.sample: The main benefit is better skills and higher motivation, which can reduce people leaving.
questions.sample_ko: 역량이 높아지고 동기가 올라가 퇴사도 줄일 수 있다는 점이에요.

questions.q: But it would cost us working time. How would you respond to that concern?
questions.q_ko: 하지만 근무 시간이 줄어요. 그 우려에는 어떻게 답하겠어요?
questions.sample: I think the long-term gain is bigger than the cost. We could start with a small trial.
questions.sample_ko: 장기적 이득이 비용보다 크다고 생각해요. 작은 시범 운영부터 시작할 수 있어요.

questions.q: A trial seems reasonable. How would we measure whether it works?
questions.q_ko: 시범 운영은 합리적이네요. 효과가 있는지 어떻게 측정할까요?
questions.sample: We could use a survey on satisfaction and track how many new skills people use at work.
questions.sample_ko: 만족도 설문과 업무에서 쓰는 새 기술 수를 확인하면 돼요.

closing: Thank you for a well-prepared idea. We'll discuss it and get back to you.
closing_ko: 잘 준비한 아이디어 고마워요. 논의한 뒤 알려 줄게요.

title: Favorite Movie
situation_ko: 새 친구가 어떤 영화를 좋아하는지 물어봐요.
user_role: a Korean learner who likes movies

questions.q: Do you like movies?
questions.sample: Yes, I do. I like movies a lot.

questions.q: Oh nice! What kind of movies do you like?
questions.sample: I like comedy movies.

questions.q: Great! When do you watch movies?
questions.sample: I watch movies on Saturday night.

questions.q: Who do you watch movies with?
questions.sample: I watch with my friend.

questions.q: What was the last movie you saw?
questions.sample: It was a funny movie about a dog. I liked it.

closing: Thanks for chatting! I need to watch more comedy movies now.
closing_ko: 이야기해 줘서 고마워요! 이제 코미디 영화를 더 봐야겠어요.

title: Music I Like
situation_ko: 버스에서 옆자리 사람이 어떤 음악을 듣는지 물어봐요.
ai_role: a friendly person sitting next to the learner
user_role: a Korean learner who listens to music

questions.q: Hi! Do you like music?
questions.sample: Yes, I love music.

questions.q: Cool! What music do you like?
questions.sample: I like pop and ballad songs.

questions.q: Who is your favorite singer?
questions.sample: My favorite singer is IU.

questions.q: When do you listen to music?
questions.sample: I listen on the bus and at home.

questions.q: What are you listening to now?
questions.sample: I'm listening to a quiet piano song.

closing: Nice! Maybe I will try that song later. Have a good day!
closing_ko: 좋네요! 나중에 그 노래를 들어 볼게요. 좋은 하루 보내세요!

title: Playing Sports
situation_ko: 동네 친구가 어떤 운동을 하는지 물어봐요.
user_role: a Korean learner who plays a sport

questions.q: Do you play any sports?
questions.sample: Yes, I play badminton.

questions.q: That sounds fun! How often do you play?
questions.sample: I play twice a week.

questions.q: Where do you play?
questions.sample: I play at the sports center near my home.

questions.q: Do you play alone or with friends?
questions.sample: I play with my coworkers.

questions.q: Why do you like this sport?
questions.sample: It's fun and it's good for my health.

closing: That's great! Sports are a good habit. See you around!
closing_ko: 멋져요! 운동은 좋은 습관이에요. 또 만나요!

title: Reading Books
situation_ko: 도서관에서 직원이 어떤 책을 좋아하는지 물어봐요.

questions.q: Hello! Do you like reading?
questions.sample: Yes, I like reading.

questions.q: Great! What kind of books do you like?
questions.sample: I like novels and travel books.

questions.q: When do you read?
questions.sample: I read before bed.

questions.q: How many books do you read a month?
questions.q_ko: 한 달에 책을 몇 권 읽어요?
questions.sample: I read two books a month.

questions.q: What book do you want today?
questions.sample: I want an easy English book.

closing: I know a good one for you. Please follow me to the shelf!
closing_ko: 딱 맞는 책을 알아요. 책장으로 따라오세요!

title: A Relaxing Walk in the Park
situation_ko: 공원에서 산책하다가 다른 산책객과 인사해요.
ai_role: a friendly person walking in the park
user_role: a visitor walking in the park

questions.q: Good morning! Do you come to this park often?
questions.q_ko: 좋은 아침이에요! 이 공원에 자주 오세요?
questions.sample: Yes, I come here every morning.

questions.q: Nice! How long do you walk?
questions.sample: I walk for thirty minutes.

questions.q: Do you walk alone?
questions.sample: Sometimes alone, sometimes with my wife.
questions.sample_ko: 혼자 걸을 때도 있고 아내와 걸을 때도 있어요.

questions.q: What do you like about this park?
questions.sample: I like the trees and the fresh air.

questions.q: What do you do after your walk?
questions.sample: I drink coffee and go to work.

closing: Have a lovely walk and a great day!
closing_ko: 즐거운 산책 되시고 좋은 하루 보내세요!

title: First Day at the Gym
situation_ko: 헬스장에 처음 등록하러 와서 직원과 이야기해요.

questions.q: Welcome to our gym! Is this your first time?
questions.q_ko: 저희 헬스장에 오신 걸 환영해요! 처음이세요?
questions.sample: Yes, I'm new here.

questions.q: Great! Why do you want to exercise?
questions.sample: I want to be healthy.

questions.q: Good reason! When can you come?
questions.q_ko: 좋은 이유네요! 언제 올 수 있어요?
questions.sample: I can come after work, at seven.
questions.sample_ko: 퇴근 후 일곱 시에 올 수 있어요.

questions.q: How many days a week do you want to come?
questions.sample: Three days a week.

questions.q: Do you like running or lifting weights?
questions.sample: I like running more.

closing: Perfect! Let me show you around. Your first workout starts today!
closing_ko: 좋아요! 안내해 드릴게요. 첫 운동은 오늘부터 시작이에요!

title: Cooking at Home
situation_ko: 친구가 집에서 요리를 자주 하는지 물어봐요.
user_role: a friend who cooks at home

questions.q: Do you cook at home?
questions.sample: Yes, I cook on weekends.

questions.q: Cool! What do you usually cook?
questions.sample: I make pasta and kimchi stew.

questions.q: Is it easy?
questions.sample: Yes, it's easy and tasty.

questions.q: Who eats your food?
questions.sample: My family eats it.

questions.q: What do you want to cook next?
questions.sample: I want to cook a chicken dish.

closing: Yum! Please invite me for dinner sometime!
closing_ko: 맛있겠다! 언제 저녁 식사에 초대해 주세요!

title: Drawing for Fun
situation_ko: 카페에서 스케치북을 보고 옆 사람이 말을 걸어요.
ai_role: a curious person at a cafe
user_role: a person drawing in a sketchbook

questions.q: Excuse me, are you drawing?
questions.sample: Yes, I draw for fun.

questions.q: That's cool! What do you like to draw?
questions.sample: I like to draw flowers and cats.

questions.q: How long have you drawn?
questions.sample: About one year.

questions.q: Do you draw every day?
questions.sample: No, I draw three times a week.

questions.q: Do you show your drawings to friends?
questions.sample: Sometimes. I'm a little shy.

closing: Your drawings sound lovely. Keep going and enjoy it!
closing_ko: 그림이 멋질 것 같아요. 계속 즐겁게 그리세요!

title: Taking Photos with My Phone
situation_ko: 여행지에서 사진 찍는 모습을 보고 다른 여행객이 말을 걸어요.

questions.q: Hi! Do you like taking photos?
questions.sample: Yes, I take photos every day.

questions.q: Fun! What do you take photos of?
questions.sample: I take photos of food and flowers.

questions.q: Do you use a camera or a phone?
questions.sample: I use my phone.

questions.q: What do you think of this view?
questions.sample: I love this view. It's beautiful.

questions.q: Would you like me to take your picture?
questions.sample: Yes, please. Thank you!

closing: Say cheese! That's a great photo. Enjoy your trip!
closing_ko: 웃으세요! 정말 멋진 사진이에요. 즐거운 여행 되세요!

title: Growing Plants
situation_ko: 꽃집에서 점원이 어떤 식물을 키우는지 물어봐요.

questions.q: Hello! Do you have any plants at home?
questions.sample: Yes, I have two small plants.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 작은 화분이 두 개 있어요.

questions.q: Lovely! Where do you keep them?
questions.sample: I keep them by the window.

questions.q: How often do you water them?
questions.sample: I water them twice a week.

questions.q: Do you like flowers or green plants?
questions.sample: I like green plants.

questions.q: What would you like today?
questions.sample: I want an easy plant for my desk.
questions.sample_ko: 책상에 둘 키우기 쉬운 식물을 원해요.

closing: I have the perfect one. Let me wrap it up for you!
closing_ko: 딱 맞는 게 있어요. 포장해 드릴게요!

title: Watching K-Dramas
situation_ko: 외국인 친구가 한국 드라마에 대해 물어봐요.
ai_role: a foreign friend interested in Korean dramas

questions.q: Do you watch Korean dramas?
questions.sample: Yes, I watch them at night.

questions.q: Cool! What drama do you like?
questions.sample: I like a drama about a doctor.

questions.q: What is the story about?
questions.sample: It's about doctors and their friends.

questions.q: Who is your favorite actor?
questions.sample: My favorite actor is Gong Yoo.

questions.q: Which drama do you recommend to me?
questions.sample: I recommend a funny love story.

closing: Thank you! I will watch it this weekend.
closing_ko: 고마워요! 이번 주말에 볼게요.

title: Karaoke Night
situation_ko: 직장 동료가 노래방에 가자고 해요.

questions.q: Do you like singing?
questions.sample: Yes, but I'm not a good singer.

questions.q: Haha, that's okay! Do you want to go to karaoke tonight?
questions.q_ko: 하하, 괜찮아요! 오늘 밤에 노래방 갈래요?
questions.sample: Yes, let's go together.

questions.q: What song will you sing?
questions.sample: I'll sing a slow song.

questions.q: What time is good for you?
questions.sample: Eight o'clock is good.

questions.q: Should we invite more people?
questions.sample: Yes, let's invite Mina.

closing: Great, it's a plan! I can't wait for tonight.
closing_ko: 좋아요, 약속이에요! 오늘 밤이 기대돼요.

title: My Free Time
situation_ko: 월요일 아침에 동료가 주말에 뭘 했는지 물어봐요.

questions.q: Good morning! How was your weekend?
questions.sample: It was good. I had a good time.

questions.q: Nice! What did you do?
questions.sample: I watched a movie and met a friend.

questions.q: Where did you meet your friend?
questions.sample: We met at a cafe.

questions.q: What do you usually do in your free time?
questions.sample: I usually sleep, walk, or watch videos.

questions.q: What do you want to do next weekend?
questions.sample: I want to go hiking.

closing: Sounds great! Let's get back to work now. Have a good week!
closing_ko: 좋네요! 이제 일하러 가요. 좋은 한 주 보내세요!

title: Swimming Pool
situation_ko: 수영장에서 강사가 수영 경험을 물어봐요.

key_phrases.ko: 저는 수영을 조금 할 수 있어요.

questions.q: Hi! Can you swim?
questions.sample: I can swim a little.

questions.q: Good! Why do you want to swim?
questions.sample: It's good for my back.

questions.q: Are you afraid of deep water?
questions.sample: Yes, a little.

questions.q: How many days can you come?
questions.sample: I can come on Tuesday and Thursday.

questions.q: What do you want to learn first?
questions.sample: I want to learn freestyle.

closing: No problem! We'll start slowly. See you on Tuesday!
closing_ko: 문제없어요! 천천히 시작할 거예요. 화요일에 봬요!

title: Mobile Games
situation_ko: 친구가 휴대폰 게임에 대해 물어봐요.
ai_role: a friend who plays mobile games

questions.q: Do you play games on your phone?
questions.sample: Yes, I do.

questions.q: Fun! What game do you play?
questions.sample: I play a puzzle game.

questions.q: When do you play?
questions.sample: I play on the subway.

questions.q: How long do you play every day?
questions.sample: I play for thirty minutes.

questions.q: Can you teach me the game?
questions.sample: Sure! It's easy. Let me show you.

closing: Thanks! I'll download it right now.
closing_ko: 고마워요! 지금 바로 다운로드할게요.

title: Going to a Concert
situation_ko: 친구가 지난주 콘서트에 갔다 왔는지 물어봐요.
ai_role: a friend who loves live music
user_role: a friend who went to a concert

key_phrases.text: We sang along the whole time.

questions.q: I heard you went to a concert last weekend. Who did you see?
questions.q_ko: 지난 주말에 콘서트 갔다고 들었어요. 누구를 봤어요?
questions.sample: I saw Coldplay. It was an amazing show.

questions.q: Wow! How did you get the tickets?
questions.sample: I booked online, and they sold out in ten minutes.

questions.q: Lucky you! What was the best part?
questions.q_ko: 운이 좋네요! 제일 좋았던 부분은 뭐예요?
questions.sample: The best part was when everyone sang along.
questions.sample_ko: 모두가 따라 부를 때가 제일 좋았어요.

questions.q: Did you go with someone?
questions.sample: I went with my sister. She's a huge fan.

questions.q: Would you go to another concert soon?
questions.sample: Yes, I'd like to see a Korean band in the winter.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 겨울에 한국 밴드 공연을 보고 싶어요.

closing: That sounds unforgettable. Next time, take me with you!
closing_ko: 잊지 못할 경험이었겠네요. 다음엔 저도 데려가 주세요!

title: Hiking Plans
situation_ko: 산악회 회원이 이번 주말 등산 계획을 물어봐요.
ai_role: a member of a hiking club

key_phrases.text: I'd like to try an easy trail.

questions.q: We're going hiking this Saturday. Have you hiked before?
questions.q_ko: 이번 토요일에 등산 가요. 전에 등산해 본 적 있어요?
questions.sample: Yes, a few times, but only on easy trails.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 몇 번 해 봤는데 쉬운 코스만 가 봤어요.

questions.q: No problem! What kind of trail would you like to try?
questions.q_ko: 괜찮아요! 어떤 코스를 해 보고 싶어요?
questions.sample: I'd like a trail with a nice view but not too steep.
questions.sample_ko: 경치가 좋지만 너무 가파르지 않은 코스가 좋아요.

questions.q: We can do that. What should you bring, do you think?
questions.q_ko: 그렇게 할 수 있어요. 뭘 가져와야 할 것 같아요?
questions.sample: I'll bring water, snacks, and a jacket.

questions.q: Do you have hiking boots?
questions.sample: Not yet. Should I buy a pair before Saturday?
questions.sample_ko: 아직 없어요. 토요일 전에 사야 할까요?

questions.q: What do you enjoy most about being in the mountains?
questions.q_ko: 산에 있을 때 가장 좋은 점이 뭐예요?
questions.sample: I enjoy the quiet and the fresh air.

closing: Perfect. We'll meet at the station at eight. See you there!
closing_ko: 좋아요. 8시에 역에서 만나요. 거기서 봐요!

title: Signing Up for a Cooking Class
situation_ko: 첫 요리 수업에서 강사가 수강생에게 질문해요.
user_role: a student in a cooking class

key_phrases.text: I'd like to learn how to make pasta.

questions.q: Welcome to the class! Have you taken a cooking class before?
questions.q_ko: 수업에 오신 걸 환영해요! 전에 요리 수업 들어 본 적 있어요?
questions.sample: No, this is my first time. I'm a beginner.

questions.q: That's fine! Why did you sign up?
questions.sample: I want to cook healthy meals instead of ordering delivery.
questions.sample_ko: 배달 음식 대신 건강한 식사를 직접 만들고 싶어서요.

questions.q: Good idea! What would you like to learn to make?
questions.q_ko: 좋은 생각이에요! 뭘 만드는 법을 배우고 싶어요?
questions.sample: I'd like to learn how to make pasta from scratch.
questions.sample_ko: 파스타를 처음부터 만드는 법을 배우고 싶어요.

questions.q: Can you use a knife safely?
questions.sample: I think so, but could you show me again slowly?
questions.sample_ko: 그런 것 같은데, 천천히 다시 보여 주실래요?

questions.q: Who will eat your dishes at home?
questions.sample: My roommate. He says he'll be my taste tester.

closing: Wonderful! Put on your apron and let's get started.
closing_ko: 좋아요! 앞치마를 두르고 시작해 볼까요.

title: Learning Guitar
situation_ko: 기타 학원 상담에서 선생님이 목표를 물어봐요.

questions.q: Hi! Have you ever played a guitar?
questions.q_ko: 안녕하세요! 기타 쳐 본 적 있어요?
questions.sample: Only once, at a friend's house.

questions.q: Okay! Why do you want to learn now?
questions.sample: I've always wanted to play, and I finally have time.
questions.sample_ko: 늘 치고 싶었는데 이제 시간이 생겼어요.

questions.q: What song would you like to play first?
questions.sample: I'd like to play a simple pop song.

questions.q: How much time can you practice each day?
questions.sample: About thirty minutes every evening.

questions.q: Do you have your own guitar, or do you need one?
questions.sample: I need one. Can you recommend a good beginner guitar?
questions.sample_ko: 필요해요. 초보용으로 좋은 기타를 추천해 주실래요?

closing: Great, we'll start with three easy chords. Your fingers will hurt at first, but it gets better!
closing_ko: 좋아요, 쉬운 코드 세 개로 시작할게요. 처음엔 손가락이 아프지만 점점 나아져요!

title: Weekend Camping Trip
situation_ko: 캠핑장에서 옆 텐트 이웃이 말을 걸어요.
ai_role: a friendly camper at the next tent
user_role: a camper on a weekend trip

key_phrases.text: We came here for the weekend.

questions.q: Hi there! Is this your first time camping here?
questions.sample: Yes, we came here for the weekend with my family.

questions.q: Nice! How did you find this place?
questions.sample: A coworker recommended it. The lake is really close.
questions.sample_ko: 동료가 추천해 줬어요. 호수가 아주 가까워요.

questions.q: It's lovely. What are you planning to cook tonight?
questions.q_ko: 멋진 곳이죠. 오늘 저녁엔 뭘 요리할 거예요?
questions.sample: We're going to grill some pork and roast marshmallows.

questions.q: Sounds delicious! Are you ready for the cold night?
questions.sample: I hope so. We brought warm blankets and a heater.
questions.sample_ko: 그러길 바라요. 따뜻한 담요와 난로를 가져왔어요.

questions.q: What do you like most about camping?
questions.sample: I like being away from the city and looking at the stars.
questions.sample_ko: 도시를 떠나 별을 볼 수 있어서 좋아요.

closing: Enjoy your night under the stars. Come say hi if you need anything!
closing_ko: 별빛 아래서 즐거운 밤 보내세요. 필요한 게 있으면 언제든 오세요!

title: A Day of Fishing
situation_ko: 강가에서 낚시하는 사람이 초보 낚시꾼에게 말을 걸어요.

questions.q: Good morning! Have you caught anything yet?
questions.sample: Not yet. I've been here for two hours.

questions.q: Don't worry, it takes patience. Is this your first time fishing?
questions.q_ko: 걱정 마세요, 인내심이 필요해요. 낚시는 처음이에요?
questions.sample: Yes, my uncle gave me this rod.

questions.q: Nice rod! Do you know what bait to use?
questions.q_ko: 좋은 낚싯대네요! 어떤 미끼를 써야 하는지 알아요?
questions.sample: I'm using worms, but I'm not sure that's right.

questions.q: That works fine here. What made you try fishing?
questions.q_ko: 여기선 괜찮아요. 낚시는 왜 해 보려고 했어요?
questions.sample: I wanted a quiet hobby to relax after work.
questions.sample_ko: 퇴근 후에 쉴 수 있는 조용한 취미를 원했어요.

questions.q: What will you do if you catch a fish?
questions.sample: I'll take a photo and let it go.

closing: That's the spirit! Be patient, and your first catch will come soon.
closing_ko: 그 마음가짐이에요! 참을성 있게 기다리면 곧 첫 물고기가 올 거예요.

title: Board Game Night
situation_ko: 보드게임 카페에서 친구가 게임을 고르자고 해요.
ai_role: a friend at a board game cafe

key_phrases.text: How do you play this game?

questions.q: We have so many games here! What kind do you want to play?
questions.q_ko: 여기 게임이 정말 많네요! 어떤 걸 하고 싶어요?
questions.sample: Something easy to learn, so everyone can join.
questions.sample_ko: 배우기 쉬워서 모두가 함께할 수 있는 게 좋아요.

questions.q: Good idea. Are you a competitive person when you play?
questions.q_ko: 좋은 생각이에요. 게임할 때 승부욕이 강한 편이에요?
questions.sample: A little. I hate losing, but I try to be friendly.
questions.sample_ko: 조금요. 지는 걸 싫어하지만 친절하게 하려고 해요.

questions.q: Ha! Have you ever played this one before?
questions.q_ko: 하하! 이 게임 해 본 적 있어요?
questions.sample: No, how do you play it?

questions.q: I'll explain the rules. Do you prefer teamwork games or playing against each other?
questions.q_ko: 규칙을 설명해 줄게요. 협동 게임이 좋아요, 서로 겨루는 게 좋아요?
questions.sample: I prefer playing against each other. It's more exciting.
questions.sample_ko: 서로 겨루는 게 좋아요. 더 신나거든요.

questions.q: Great game! Should we play another round?
questions.q_ko: 멋진 게임이었어요! 한 판 더 할까요?
questions.sample: Yes, let's play one more round. I want revenge!
questions.sample_ko: 네, 한 판만 더 해요. 복수하고 싶어요!

closing: Ha-ha, you're on! Let me shuffle the cards.
closing_ko: 하하, 좋아요! 카드를 섞을게요.

title: Volunteering at a Shelter
situation_ko: 동물 보호소 봉사활동 첫날 담당자가 이야기를 나눠요.
ai_role: a volunteer coordinator at an animal shelter

key_phrases.ko: 저는 매주 일요일에 올 수 있어요.

questions.q: Thank you for volunteering with us! What made you want to help?
questions.q_ko: 봉사해 주셔서 감사해요! 왜 돕고 싶으셨어요?
questions.sample: I love animals, and I wanted to do something useful.
questions.sample_ko: 동물을 좋아하고 뭔가 의미 있는 일을 하고 싶었어요.

questions.q: That's wonderful. Have you worked with animals before?
questions.q_ko: 멋지네요. 전에 동물과 일해 본 적 있어요?
questions.sample: I have a dog at home, so I'm good with animals.
questions.sample_ko: 집에 개가 있어서 동물을 잘 다뤄요.

questions.q: Great. How often can you come?
questions.sample: I can come every Sunday morning.
questions.sample_ko: 매주 일요일 아침에 올 수 있어요.

questions.q: Which job would you like to do, walking dogs or cleaning the cages?
questions.q_ko: 개 산책과 우리 청소 중 어떤 일을 하고 싶어요?
questions.sample: I'd like to walk the dogs, if that's okay.

questions.q: Do you have any questions for me?
questions.sample: Yes, do I need to wear special clothes?

closing: Just wear comfortable clothes. We're so happy to have you!
closing_ko: 편한 옷이면 돼요. 함께하게 되어 정말 기뻐요!

title: Visiting an Art Museum
situation_ko: 미술관에서 도슨트가 관람객에게 질문해요.

questions.q: Welcome to the museum! Do you visit art museums often?
questions.q_ko: 미술관에 오신 걸 환영해요! 미술관에 자주 가요?
questions.sample: Not often, maybe twice a year.
questions.sample_ko: 자주는 아니고 일 년에 두 번 정도요.

questions.q: I see. Is there a painting here that you like?
questions.q_ko: 그렇군요. 여기 마음에 드는 그림이 있어요?
questions.sample: I like the blue landscape painting over there.
questions.sample_ko: 저쪽에 있는 파란 풍경화가 마음에 들어요.

questions.q: Good eye! How does it make you feel?
questions.sample: It makes me feel calm, like I'm near the sea.
questions.sample_ko: 바다 근처에 있는 것처럼 마음이 편안해져요.

questions.q: Do you like old paintings or modern art?
questions.q_ko: 옛날 그림이 좋아요, 현대 미술이 좋아요?
questions.sample: I like modern art because it's creative.

questions.q: Is there anything you'd like to ask me?
questions.sample: Yes, can I take photos here?

closing: Photos are fine without flash. Please enjoy the rest of the gallery!
closing_ko: 플래시만 끄면 사진 찍어도 돼요. 나머지 전시도 즐겁게 관람하세요!

title: Salsa Dance Class
situation_ko: 댄스 수업 쉬는 시간에 파트너가 말을 걸어요.
ai_role: a dance partner in a class
user_role: a student in a dance class

key_phrases.text: I keep stepping on your feet.
The rhythm is hard for me.

questions.q: Hi, I'm your partner for today! Is this your first dance class?
questions.q_ko: 안녕하세요, 오늘 파트너예요! 첫 댄스 수업이에요?
questions.sample: Yes, and I keep stepping on your feet. Sorry!
questions.sample_ko: 네, 그리고 계속 발을 밟네요. 죄송해요!

questions.q: Don't worry, it happens! Why did you join?
questions.q_ko: 걱정 마요, 흔한 일이에요! 왜 등록했어요?
questions.sample: I'm learning for fun and to meet new people.
questions.sample_ko: 재미로, 그리고 새로운 사람들을 만나려고 배워요.

questions.q: Good reasons. What's the hardest part for you?
questions.sample: The rhythm is hard for me. I get lost when it speeds up.

questions.q: You're doing better than you think. Have you danced at parties before?
questions.q_ko: 생각보다 잘하고 있어요. 파티에서 춤춰 본 적 있어요?
questions.sample: Only at weddings, and I just stood and clapped.

questions.q: Would you like to practice together after class?
questions.sample: Sure, that would be a big help. Thank you!
questions.sample_ko: 좋아요, 큰 도움이 될 거예요. 고마워요!

closing: Great! One, two, three... let's dance again!
closing_ko: 좋아요! 하나, 둘, 셋... 다시 춤춰 봐요!

title: Favorite YouTube Channels
situation_ko: 점심시간에 동료가 즐겨 보는 유튜브 채널을 물어봐요.

key_phrases.text: I subscribe to a few channels.
I learn a lot from it.

questions.q: What do you do after work, watch videos?
questions.q_ko: 퇴근 후에는 뭐 해요, 영상 봐요?
questions.sample: Yes, I watch YouTube before I sleep.

questions.q: Same here! Which channels do you subscribe to?
questions.sample: I subscribe to a cooking channel and a travel vlog.

questions.q: Interesting. What do you like about the cooking channel?
questions.q_ko: 흥미롭네요. 요리 채널의 어떤 점이 좋아요?
questions.sample: The recipes are simple, and I learn a lot from it.

questions.q: Have you tried any of the recipes?
questions.q_ko: 레시피를 따라 해 본 적 있어요?
questions.sample: Yes, I made egg fried rice last week, and it was good.

questions.q: Could you send me the link to that channel?
questions.sample: Of course, I'll send it to you after lunch.

closing: Thanks! Now I have something to watch tonight.
closing_ko: 고마워요! 오늘 밤에 볼 게 생겼네요.

title: Listening to Podcasts
situation_ko: 출근길 지하철에서 지인이 팟캐스트를 추천해요.

questions.q: I see you have earphones in. Do you listen to podcasts?
questions.sample: Yes, I listen on my commute.

questions.q: Nice! What kind of podcasts do you like?
questions.sample: I like news and short English lessons.

questions.q: Does it really help you with English?
questions.sample: Yes, it helps me practice listening.

questions.q: How long is your commute?
questions.sample: About forty minutes each way.

questions.q: I have a good podcast about travel stories. Want a recommendation?
questions.q_ko: 여행 이야기를 다루는 좋은 팟캐스트가 있어요. 추천해 줄까요?
questions.sample: Yes, please. I'd love a recommendation.

closing: I'll text you the name. Enjoy your ride!
closing_ko: 이름을 문자로 보내 줄게요. 즐거운 출근길 되세요!

title: Book Club Meeting
situation_ko: 독서 모임에서 사회자가 이번 달 책에 대해 물어봐요.

key_phrases.text: I finished the book last night.

questions.q: Welcome, everyone! Did you finish this month's book?
questions.q_ko: 모두 환영해요! 이번 달 책 다 읽었어요?
questions.sample: Yes, I finished it last night.

questions.q: Great! What did you think of it?
questions.sample: I enjoyed it. The story was warm and easy to read.

questions.q: Who was your favorite character?
questions.sample: My favorite character was the old grandmother, because she was wise.

questions.q: What about the ending? Did it surprise you?
questions.sample: Yes, I didn't expect it. I almost cried.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 예상 못 했어요. 거의 울 뻔했어요.

questions.q: Do you have a book you'd like us to read next month?
questions.q_ko: 다음 달에 읽고 싶은 책이 있어요?
questions.sample: Yes, I'd like to suggest a mystery novel.

closing: A mystery sounds fun! Thanks, everyone, see you next month.
closing_ko: 추리 소설 재미있겠네요! 모두 감사해요, 다음 달에 봬요.

title: Trying Yoga
situation_ko: 요가 스튜디오 체험 수업 후 강사가 소감을 물어봐요.
user_role: a student at a trial class

questions.q: How did you like your first yoga class?
questions.sample: It was harder than I thought, but I feel relaxed now.

questions.q: That's what we like to hear! Which pose was the hardest?
questions.q_ko: 그런 말씀이 반가워요! 어떤 자세가 제일 어려웠어요?
questions.sample: The one where I had to balance on one leg.

questions.q: Many people find that hard. Are you flexible?
questions.q_ko: 많은 분이 어려워해요. 몸이 유연한 편이에요?
questions.sample: No, I'm not very flexible, but I want to improve.
questions.sample_ko: 아니요, 별로 유연하지 않지만 좋아지고 싶어요.

questions.q: Why did you want to try yoga?
questions.sample: I sit at a desk all day, and my shoulders hurt.
questions.sample_ko: 하루 종일 책상에 앉아 있어서 어깨가 아파요.

questions.q: Would you like to sign up for a monthly class?
questions.sample: Yes, I'd like to sign up for two classes a week.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 일주일에 두 번 수업으로 등록하고 싶어요.

closing: Wonderful! I'll get the form ready. Remember to drink water!
closing_ko: 좋아요! 신청서를 준비할게요. 물 많이 드세요!

title: Cycling Along the River
situation_ko: 자전거 대여소에서 직원이 코스를 안내해요.
ai_role: a bike rental shop staff member

key_phrases.text: I'd like to rent a bike for two hours.
key_phrases.ko: 두 시간 동안 자전거를 빌리고 싶어요.

key_phrases.text: Where can I get a drink?

questions.q: Hello! What can I help you with today?
questions.sample: I'd like to rent a bike for two hours.
questions.sample_ko: 두 시간 동안 자전거를 빌리고 싶어요.

questions.q: Sure! Have you ridden along the river before?
questions.q_ko: 그럼요! 강변에서 타 본 적 있어요?
questions.sample: No, this is my first time. Is the path flat?

questions.q: Yes, it's very flat and easy. Are you riding alone?
questions.q_ko: 네, 아주 평평하고 쉬워요. 혼자 타요?
questions.sample: No, I'm riding with my friend.

questions.q: Good. Do you want a regular bike or an electric one?
questions.q_ko: 좋아요. 일반 자전거로 할래요, 전기 자전거로 할래요?
questions.sample: A regular one, please. I want some exercise.

questions.q: Do you need any advice about where to stop?
questions.sample: Yes, where can I get a cold drink?
questions.sample_ko: 네, 시원한 음료는 어디서 살 수 있나요?

closing: There's a convenience store near the bridge. Enjoy your ride and be safe!
closing_ko: 다리 근처에 편의점이 있어요. 즐겁고 안전하게 타세요!

title: A Local Festival
situation_ko: 동네 축제에서 자원봉사자가 방문객에게 말을 걸어요.

questions.q: Welcome to the festival! Is this your first time here?
questions.q_ko: 축제에 오신 걸 환영해요! 여기 처음이세요?
questions.sample: Yes, there's so much to see!

questions.q: Glad you like it! Who did you come with?
questions.sample: I came with my kids and my husband.

questions.q: How nice! What would you like to see first?
questions.sample: The street performance sounds fun.

questions.q: The show starts at two. Are you hungry? We have lots of food.
questions.sample: Yes, where is the food stand?

questions.q: What kind of food do you want to try?
questions.sample: I want to try the fried chicken and hotteok.

closing: Both are by the main gate. Have a wonderful day at the festival!
closing_ko: 둘 다 정문 근처에 있어요. 축제에서 즐거운 하루 보내세요!

title: Photography Walk
situation_ko: 사진 동호회 모임에서 회원이 취미를 물어봐요.

key_phrases.text: Could you give me some tips?

questions.q: Nice to meet you! How long have you been into photography?
questions.sample: Only a few months. I just bought a camera.
questions.sample_ko: 몇 달 안 됐어요. 카메라를 막 샀어요.

questions.q: Congratulations! What do you like to photograph?
questions.sample: I like taking street photos of people and old buildings.
questions.sample_ko: 사람들과 오래된 건물의 거리 사진을 찍는 걸 좋아해요.

questions.q: That's interesting. Is it hard to photograph strangers?
questions.q_ko: 흥미롭네요. 낯선 사람 찍는 게 어렵진 않아요?
questions.sample: Yes, I feel shy, so I usually ask first.

questions.q: Smart. Do you edit your photos afterwards?
questions.sample: A little. I change the brightness on my phone.

questions.q: What would you like to learn from our club?
questions.sample: Could you give me some tips about lighting?

closing: Of course! Let's walk together and I'll show you my favorite spots.
closing_ko: 물론이죠! 같이 걸으면서 제가 좋아하는 장소를 보여 줄게요.

title: Baking Cookies
situation_ko: 이웃이 쿠키 냄새가 좋다며 말을 걸어요.

questions.q: Something smells amazing! Are you baking?
questions.q_ko: 냄새가 정말 좋네요! 뭐 굽고 있어요?
questions.sample: Yes, I'm baking chocolate chip cookies.

questions.q: Yum! Do you bake often?
questions.sample: Almost every weekend. I bake when I'm stressed.
questions.sample_ko: 거의 주말마다요. 스트레스 받을 때 구워요.

questions.q: That's a nice way to relax. Where did you learn?
questions.q_ko: 편하게 쉬는 좋은 방법이네요. 어디서 배웠어요?
questions.sample: I followed recipes online, and I watched many videos.
questions.sample_ko: 온라인 레시피를 따라 하고 영상도 많이 봤어요.

questions.q: Have you ever had a baking disaster?
questions.sample: Yes, once I forgot the sugar. They tasted terrible.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 한번은 설탕을 깜빡했어요. 맛이 끔찍했어요.

questions.q: Ha-ha! Can I try one of today's cookies?
questions.q_ko: 하하! 오늘 쿠키 하나 먹어 봐도 될까요?
questions.sample: Of course, please try one. Tell me what you think!
questions.sample_ko: 물론이죠, 하나 드셔 보세요. 어떤지 말해 주세요!

closing: Mmm, delicious! You could open your own bakery.
closing_ko: 음, 맛있어요! 빵집 차려도 되겠어요.

title: Training for a 10K Run
situation_ko: 러닝 모임에서 회원이 대회 준비에 대해 물어봐요.
user_role: a runner preparing for a race

key_phrases.text: I run three times a week.

questions.q: Hey! I heard you're signing up for a race. Is that true?
questions.sample: Yes, I'm training for a 10K next month.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 다음 달 10km 대회를 준비하고 있어요.

questions.q: Awesome! How often do you run?
questions.sample: I run three times a week, mostly in the morning.
questions.sample_ko: 일주일에 세 번, 주로 아침에 달려요.

questions.q: That's a good routine. How far can you run now?
questions.q_ko: 좋은 루틴이네요. 지금은 얼마나 뛸 수 있어요?
questions.sample: About seven kilometers without stopping.

questions.q: Do you have any problems, like pain?
questions.sample: My knees get sore sometimes, so I stretch a lot.
questions.sample_ko: 가끔 무릎이 아파서 스트레칭을 많이 해요.

questions.q: What's your goal for the race?
questions.sample: I just want to finish in under an hour.
questions.sample_ko: 한 시간 안에 들어오는 게 목표예요.

closing: You can do it! We'll cheer for you at the finish line.
closing_ko: 할 수 있어요! 결승선에서 응원할게요.

title: Gaming with Friends
situation_ko: 온라인 게임을 하다가 친구가 음성 채팅으로 말을 걸어요.

questions.q: Hey, you're online! How long have you been playing this game?
questions.q_ko: 어, 접속했네요! 이 게임 한 지 얼마나 됐어요?
questions.sample: About a year. I play after dinner most days.

questions.q: Cool. What's your favorite thing about it?
questions.q_ko: 멋지네요. 이 게임의 제일 좋은 점이 뭐예요?
questions.sample: I like that I can team up with friends.
questions.sample_ko: 친구들과 같은 팀을 할 수 있어서 좋아요.

questions.q: Same! Do you prefer playing together or alone?
questions.q_ko: 저도요! 같이 하는 게 좋아요, 혼자가 좋아요?
questions.sample: Together. It's more fun when we talk and laugh.

questions.q: How do you stop yourself from playing too late?
questions.q_ko: 너무 늦게까지 하지 않으려면 어떻게 해요?
questions.sample: I set an alarm for eleven o'clock.

questions.q: Want to team up for a match right now?
questions.sample: Sure, invite me. Watch out behind you!

closing: Haha, thanks! Okay, loading the match now. Good luck!
closing_ko: 하하, 고마워요! 자, 지금 경기를 불러올게요. 행운을 빌어요!

title: Explaining K-Pop
situation_ko: 외국인 동료가 K-팝이 왜 인기 있는지 궁금해해요.
ai_role: a foreign coworker curious about K-pop

key_phrases.text: They train for years before debuting.

questions.q: I keep hearing about K-pop. Why do you think it's so popular worldwide?
questions.q_ko: K-팝 이야기를 계속 듣게 돼요. 왜 전 세계에서 인기가 있다고 생각해요?
questions.sample: One reason is the strong performances. The music, dance, and videos all work together.
questions.sample_ko: 한 가지 이유는 공연이 뛰어나다는 거예요. 음악, 춤, 영상이 함께 어우러지거든요.

questions.q: That makes sense. I heard idols train for years. Is that true?
questions.q_ko: 일리 있네요. 아이돌이 몇 년간 훈련한다고 들었어요. 사실이에요?
questions.sample: Yes, many train for several years before debuting, which is tough but it shows in their skills.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 많은 사람이 데뷔 전에 몇 년간 훈련해요. 힘들지만 실력에서 드러나요.

questions.q: Do you think that's healthy for young people?
questions.sample: Honestly, I'm not sure. It can be too stressful, so I hope companies take better care of them.
questions.sample_ko: 솔직히 잘 모르겠어요. 스트레스가 너무 클 수 있어서 회사들이 더 잘 보살폈으면 해요.

questions.q: Which group should I start with as a beginner?
questions.sample: I'd recommend BTS or NewJeans, because their songs are catchy and easy to enjoy.
questions.sample_ko: BTS나 뉴진스를 추천해요. 노래가 귀에 쏙 들어오고 듣기 편해요.

questions.q: Do you think K-pop will stay popular for a long time?
questions.q_ko: K-팝이 오랫동안 인기를 유지할 거라고 생각해요?
questions.sample: I think so, because it keeps changing and mixing with other styles of music.
questions.sample_ko: 그렇다고 생각해요. 계속 변화하고 다른 음악 스타일과 섞이니까요.

closing: Thanks for the great explanation. I'll make a K-pop playlist tonight!
closing_ko: 설명 고마워요. 오늘 밤 K-팝 플레이리스트를 만들어 볼게요!

title: Why K-Dramas Are Addictive
situation_ko: 해외 친구가 K-드라마에 빠진 이유를 이야기하며 한국인의 의견을 물어봐요.
ai_role: an overseas friend who is hooked on K-dramas
user_role: a Korean friend who knows K-dramas

key_phrases.text: It's not as realistic as it looks.
That's one thing people often misunderstand.

questions.q: I can't stop watching K-dramas lately! Why do you think they're so addictive?
questions.q_ko: 요즘 K-드라마를 멈출 수가 없어요! 왜 이렇게 중독성 있다고 생각해요?
questions.sample: I think the stories are emotional, and each episode ends with a cliffhanger.
questions.sample_ko: 이야기가 감성적이고 매 회 끝이 궁금해지게 끝나서 그런 것 같아요.

questions.q: Yes! Are Korean workplaces and schools really like in the dramas?
questions.q_ko: 맞아요! 한국의 직장이나 학교가 정말 드라마 같아요?
questions.sample: Not really. It's not as realistic as it looks, but the pressure to study and work hard is real.
questions.sample_ko: 그렇진 않아요. 보이는 것만큼 현실적이진 않지만, 공부와 일에 대한 압박은 실제로 있어요.

questions.q: Interesting. What do you personally like most about them?
questions.q_ko: 흥미롭네요. 개인적으로 가장 좋아하는 점은 뭐예요?
questions.sample: What I like most is the music and the beautiful scenery. They make simple scenes feel special.
questions.sample_ko: 음악과 아름다운 풍경이 가장 좋아요. 평범한 장면도 특별하게 느껴져요.

questions.q: Do you ever get tired of the same love-story pattern?
questions.q_ko: 비슷한 사랑 이야기 패턴에 질릴 때는 없어요?
questions.sample: Sometimes, so I've started watching thrillers and historical dramas instead.
questions.sample_ko: 가끔요. 그래서 요즘은 스릴러나 사극을 봐요.

questions.q: Can you recommend a drama that isn't a love story?
questions.q_ko: 사랑 이야기가 아닌 드라마를 추천해 줄래요?
questions.sample: Try a legal drama about a lawyer. It's smart, funny, and the characters are really lovable.
questions.sample_ko: 변호사가 나오는 법정 드라마를 봐 보세요. 똑똑하고 웃기고 인물들이 정말 사랑스러워요.

closing: Great, that's going on my list. Thanks for the tips!
closing_ko: 좋아요, 제 목록에 넣을게요. 팁 고마워요!

title: Cinema or Streaming
situation_ko: 친구와 영화를 극장에서 볼지 집에서 볼지 토론해요.
ai_role: a friend who loves streaming at home
user_role: a friend who prefers the cinema

questions.q: Do you prefer watching movies at the cinema or streaming at home?
questions.q_ko: 영화는 극장에서 보는 게 좋아요, 집에서 스트리밍으로 보는 게 좋아요?
questions.sample: I prefer the cinema because the big screen and sound make the story more powerful.
questions.sample_ko: 극장이 더 좋아요. 큰 화면과 소리가 이야기를 더 강렬하게 만들어요.

questions.q: But tickets are expensive these days. Is it worth the price?
questions.q_ko: 하지만 요즘 티켓이 비싸잖아요. 그만한 가치가 있나요?
questions.sample: For big action movies, yes. For small dramas, I'd rather wait and stream them.
questions.sample_ko: 큰 액션 영화라면 그래요. 작은 드라마는 기다렸다가 스트리밍으로 볼래요.

questions.q: Good point. What bothers you most about watching at the cinema?
questions.q_ko: 좋은 지적이에요. 극장에서 보는 게 제일 불편한 점은 뭐예요?
questions.sample: People using their phones or talking. It really breaks my focus.
questions.sample_ko: 휴대폰을 쓰거나 떠드는 사람들이요. 집중이 완전히 깨져요.

questions.q: At home, I can pause and eat snacks. Don't you think that's better?
questions.q_ko: 집에서는 멈추고 간식도 먹을 수 있잖아요. 그게 더 낫지 않아요?
questions.sample: It's comfortable, I agree. On the other hand, I often get distracted and check my phone.
questions.sample_ko: 편하긴 해요. 반면에 저는 산만해져서 자꾸 휴대폰을 보게 돼요.

questions.q: So what should we do this weekend?
questions.sample: Let's go to the cinema this time, and next time we can stream something at your place.
questions.sample_ko: 이번엔 극장에 가고, 다음엔 네 집에서 스트리밍으로 봐요.

closing: Deal! I'll book the tickets tonight. You pick the snacks!
closing_ko: 좋아요! 오늘 밤에 표를 예매할게요. 간식은 네가 골라!

title: Expensive Hobbies
situation_ko: 취미에 돈을 얼마나 써야 하는지 친구와 이야기해요.
ai_role: a friend discussing spending on hobbies
user_role: a friend with a costly hobby

key_phrases.text: I try to stick to a budget.

questions.q: Your new camera must have been expensive. Do you think it was worth it?
questions.q_ko: 새 카메라 비쌌겠어요. 그만한 가치가 있었다고 생각해요?
questions.sample: Yes, it's worth it to me. The photos are so much better, and I enjoy my weekends more.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 저에게는 가치 있어요. 사진이 훨씬 좋아졌고 주말이 더 즐거워졌어요.

questions.q: How do you keep from overspending on your hobby?
questions.q_ko: 취미에 돈을 너무 쓰지 않으려면 어떻게 해요?
questions.sample: I try to stick to a monthly budget and wait a week before buying anything big.
questions.sample_ko: 월 예산을 지키고 큰 걸 사기 전엔 일주일 기다려요.

questions.q: Do you think expensive equipment makes you better?
questions.q_ko: 비싼 장비가 실력을 늘려 준다고 생각해요?
questions.sample: Not really. Practice matters more, and good gear only helps after you learn the basics.
questions.sample_ko: 그렇진 않아요. 연습이 더 중요하고, 좋은 장비는 기본을 익힌 뒤에 도움이 돼요.

questions.q: What would you tell someone who wants to start but is worried about the cost?
questions.q_ko: 시작하고 싶지만 비용이 걱정되는 사람에게 뭐라고 말하겠어요?
questions.sample: You can start cheaply. Borrow equipment or buy used things first, and upgrade later.
questions.sample_ko: 저렴하게 시작할 수 있어요. 장비를 빌리거나 중고를 사고 나중에 업그레이드하세요.

questions.q: Is there any hobby you gave up because it cost too much?
questions.q_ko: 돈이 너무 많이 들어서 포기한 취미가 있어요?
questions.sample: Yes, golf. The fees and equipment were too much for me.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 골프요. 비용과 장비가 제겐 너무 부담이었어요.

closing: Smart thinking. A good hobby doesn't have to be expensive to be fun.
closing_ko: 현명한 생각이에요. 좋은 취미가 꼭 비쌀 필요는 없죠.

title: Turning a Hobby into a Job
situation_ko: 친구가 취미를 직업으로 삼아도 될지 조언을 구해요.
ai_role: a friend who loves baking and is thinking of quitting a job

key_phrases.ko: 일단 파트타임으로 시작해 보는 게 어때?

questions.q: I'm thinking of quitting my job to open a small bakery. What do you think?
questions.q_ko: 직장을 그만두고 작은 빵집을 열까 생각 중이에요. 어떻게 생각해요?
questions.sample: It sounds exciting, but I'd think carefully. Do you have enough savings?
questions.sample_ko: 신나는 일이지만 신중히 생각해 보세요. 저축은 충분해요?

questions.q: I have about six months of savings. Is that enough?
questions.sample: Probably not. The risk is that new shops often take a year to make a profit.
questions.sample_ko: 아마 부족할 거예요. 새 가게는 이익을 내는 데 보통 1년이 걸리는 위험이 있어요.

questions.q: Good point. What if I start small first?
questions.q_ko: 좋은 지적이에요. 먼저 작게 시작하면 어때요?
questions.sample: Why don't you start part-time? You could sell at weekend markets and see how people react.
questions.sample_ko: 파트타임으로 시작해 보는 게 어때요? 주말 마켓에서 팔면서 반응을 볼 수 있어요.

questions.q: I'm also afraid baking will stop being fun if it becomes work.
questions.q_ko: 일이 되면 빵 굽는 게 즐겁지 않을까 봐 걱정도 돼요.
questions.sample: That's a real concern. If I were you, I'd keep some baking just for myself.
questions.sample_ko: 실제로 걱정될 만해요. 저라면 나만을 위한 베이킹은 남겨 두겠어요.

questions.q: Would you ever turn your own hobby into a job?
questions.q_ko: 당신은 취미를 직업으로 삼을 생각이 있어요?
questions.sample: Maybe not. I like my hobbies as a break from work, so I want to keep them separate.
questions.sample_ko: 아마 아닐 거예요. 취미는 일에서 벗어나는 휴식이라 분리해 두고 싶어요.

closing: Thanks for being honest. I'll try the weekend market first!
closing_ko: 솔직하게 말해 줘서 고마워요. 일단 주말 마켓부터 해 볼게요!

title: Hobbies and Social Media
situation_ko: SNS에 취미를 올리는 일에 대해 친구와 토론해요.
ai_role: a friend who posts everything online
user_role: a friend who is cautious about social media

questions.q: I post my hiking photos online all the time. Do you share your hobbies on social media?
questions.q_ko: 저는 등산 사진을 항상 SNS에 올려요. 당신은 취미를 SNS에 공유해요?
questions.sample: Not much. I do it for myself, so I rarely post.
questions.sample_ko: 별로요. 저는 저를 위해 하는 거라 거의 안 올려요.

questions.q: Why not? Don't you want people to see your work?
questions.q_ko: 왜요? 사람들이 작품을 봐 주길 바라지 않아요?
questions.sample: Sometimes, but I see your point. Still, it puts pressure on me to make everything look perfect.
questions.sample_ko: 가끔은요. 무슨 말인지 알지만, 모든 걸 완벽하게 보여야 한다는 부담이 돼요.

questions.q: Do you think social media makes hobbies more fun or less fun?
questions.q_ko: SNS가 취미를 더 재미있게 만든다고 생각해요, 덜 재미있게 만든다고 생각해요?
questions.sample: Both. It's great for finding ideas, but people sometimes do things just to get likes.
questions.sample_ko: 둘 다요. 아이디어를 얻기엔 좋지만 좋아요를 얻으려고 하는 사람도 있어요.

questions.q: Have you ever learned a hobby from an online community?
questions.q_ko: 온라인 커뮤니티에서 취미를 배운 적 있어요?
questions.sample: Yes, I learned knitting from a group. People there were kind and shared a lot of tips.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 한 모임에서 뜨개질을 배웠어요. 사람들이 친절했고 팁도 많이 알려 줬어요.

questions.q: If you could give advice to beginners, what would it be?
questions.sample: Enjoy it first, and don't compare yourself with others online.
questions.sample_ko: 먼저 즐기고 온라인에서 다른 사람과 비교하지 말라고 하겠어요.

closing: That's a healthy way to look at it. Maybe I'll post a little less!
closing_ko: 건강한 관점이네요. 저도 조금 덜 올려야겠어요!

title: Learning Piano as an Adult
situation_ko: 성인이 되어 피아노를 시작한 이유를 친구가 물어봐요.

key_phrases.text: It's never too late to learn.
It gives me a sense of achievement.

questions.q: I heard you started piano at forty. What made you decide to learn?
questions.q_ko: 마흔에 피아노를 시작했다고 들었어요. 왜 배우기로 했어요?
questions.sample: I quit piano as a child, and I always regretted it. I decided it's never too late to learn.
questions.sample_ko: 어릴 때 그만두고 늘 후회했어요. 배우기에 늦은 때란 없다고 생각했어요.

questions.q: How is it different from learning as a child?
questions.q_ko: 어릴 때 배우는 것과 어떻게 달라요?
questions.sample: Adults understand music better, but our fingers are less flexible, so progress is slow, but steady.
questions.sample_ko: 어른은 음악을 더 잘 이해하지만 손가락이 덜 유연해서 느리긴 해도 꾸준히 늘어요.

questions.q: What's the hardest part for you?
questions.sample: Finding time to practice. After a long day at work I'm tired, but I try to play for twenty minutes.
questions.sample_ko: 연습할 시간을 내는 거예요. 일하고 나면 피곤하지만 20분이라도 치려고 해요.

questions.q: What do you get out of it?
questions.sample: It gives me a sense of achievement, and it helps me forget my work stress.
questions.sample_ko: 성취감을 주고 업무 스트레스를 잊게 해 줘요.

questions.q: Would you recommend learning an instrument as an adult?
questions.q_ko: 어른이 되어 악기를 배우는 걸 추천해요?
questions.sample: Definitely, as long as you choose music you love and you don't expect perfection.
questions.sample_ko: 물론이죠. 좋아하는 음악을 고르고 완벽함을 기대하지 않는다면요.

closing: You've inspired me. Maybe I'll look for a violin class!
closing_ko: 덕분에 힘이 나네요. 바이올린 수업을 알아봐야겠어요!

title: Travel or Stay Home
situation_ko: 휴일을 어떻게 보내는 게 좋은지 동료와 의견을 나눠요.
user_role: a coworker who likes staying home

key_phrases.ko: 저는 집에 있는 게 더 좋아요, 왜냐하면...

questions.q: The holiday is coming up. Are you going to travel somewhere?
questions.q_ko: 연휴가 다가오네요. 어디 여행 갈 거예요?
questions.sample: Probably not. I'd rather stay home because traveling during holidays is crowded and expensive.
questions.sample_ko: 아마 안 갈 거예요. 연휴 여행은 붐비고 비싸서 집에 있는 게 더 좋아요.

questions.q: But isn't staying home boring?
questions.sample: Not at all. I read, cook, and play games. I really need that time to recharge.
questions.sample_ko: 전혀요. 책 읽고 요리하고 게임해요. 재충전하는 시간이 꼭 필요해요.

questions.q: Don't you want to see new places and meet new people?
questions.q_ko: 새로운 곳을 보고 새로운 사람을 만나고 싶지 않아요?
questions.sample: Sometimes, but I'd choose a quiet weekday trip instead of a busy holiday.
questions.sample_ko: 가끔은요. 하지만 붐비는 연휴보다 조용한 평일 여행을 고르겠어요.

questions.q: That's a fair point. What was the best trip you've ever had?
questions.q_ko: 일리 있네요. 지금까지 가장 좋았던 여행은 뭐예요?
questions.sample: A short trip to Jeju. We walked on the coast and ate fresh seafood, and nothing was rushed.
questions.sample_ko: 제주도 짧은 여행이었어요. 해안을 걷고 신선한 해산물을 먹었고, 서두르지 않았어요.

questions.q: Do you think people are born as travelers or homebodies?
questions.sample: I think it's a matter of personality, but also of how you grew up.
questions.sample_ko: 성격 차이이기도 하고 자란 환경에도 영향을 받는다고 생각해요.

closing: Maybe we're both right. Enjoy your holiday your way!
closing_ko: 둘 다 맞는 것 같아요. 각자 방식대로 연휴 즐기세요!

title: E-books or Paper Books
situation_ko: 서점에서 점원과 책을 읽는 방식에 대해 의견을 나눠요.

key_phrases.text: I like the feel of paper.

questions.q: Do you usually read paper books or e-books?
questions.sample: Mostly paper books. I like the feel of paper, and I remember the content better.
questions.sample_ko: 주로 종이책이요. 종이의 느낌이 좋고 내용도 더 잘 기억나요.

questions.q: Interesting. Doesn't carrying heavy books bother you?
questions.q_ko: 흥미롭네요. 무거운 책을 들고 다니는 게 불편하지 않아요?
questions.sample: A little. For trips, e-books are more convenient, so it depends on the situation.
questions.sample_ko: 조금요. 여행 때는 전자책이 더 편해서 상황에 따라 달라요.

questions.q: Do you think people read less these days than before?
questions.q_ko: 요즘 사람들이 예전보다 책을 덜 읽는다고 생각해요?
questions.sample: Yes, because phones take up our attention. But I think reading is still important for thinking deeply.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 휴대폰이 집중력을 빼앗으니까요. 하지만 깊이 생각하려면 독서가 여전히 중요하다고 봐요.

questions.q: How can people get into the habit of reading?
questions.q_ko: 사람들이 독서 습관을 들이려면 어떻게 해야 할까요?
questions.sample: Start with short books you like, and read ten minutes a day instead of forcing yourself.
questions.sample_ko: 좋아하는 짧은 책으로 시작해서 억지로 하지 말고 하루 10분씩 읽으세요.

questions.q: What kind of book are you looking for today?
questions.sample: Something thought-provoking, maybe an essay collection by a Korean author.
questions.sample_ko: 생각할 거리를 주는 책이요, 한국 작가의 에세이집이면 좋겠어요.

closing: I have a few in mind. Let me show you the essay shelf.
closing_ko: 몇 권 생각나는 게 있어요. 에세이 책장으로 안내해 드릴게요.

title: Being a Sports Fan
situation_ko: 야구장에서 옆자리 팬과 응원하는 팀에 대해 이야기해요.
ai_role: a fan sitting next to the learner at a stadium

key_phrases.text: Win or lose, I enjoy the atmosphere.

questions.q: Great game so far! How long have you supported this team?
questions.q_ko: 지금까지 멋진 경기네요! 이 팀은 얼마나 응원했어요?
questions.sample: I've supported them since I was a child. My father took me to games every summer.
questions.sample_ko: 어릴 때부터 응원했어요. 아버지가 여름마다 경기장에 데려가셨어요.

questions.q: Wow, a loyal fan! Why do you think people get so emotional about sports?
questions.q_ko: 와, 충성스러운 팬이네요! 사람들은 왜 스포츠에 그렇게 감정이 올라온다고 생각해요?
questions.sample: Because we share it with other people. Win or lose, I enjoy the atmosphere and feel part of a group.
questions.sample_ko: 다른 사람들과 함께 나누기 때문이에요. 이기든 지든 분위기를 즐기고 한 무리가 된 기분이 들어요.

questions.q: True. What do you think of that last decision by the referee?
questions.q_ko: 맞아요. 방금 심판 판정은 어떻게 생각해요?
questions.sample: Honestly, that decision was questionable, but I guess it's part of the game.

questions.q: Do you think sports fans can sometimes go too far?
questions.q_ko: 스포츠 팬들이 가끔 도를 넘는다고 생각해요?
questions.sample: Yes, some people get violent or rude. Supporting a team should be fun and respectful.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 폭력적이거나 무례한 사람도 있어요. 응원은 즐겁고 서로 존중해야 해요.

questions.q: If the team loses today, how will you feel?
questions.q_ko: 오늘 팀이 지면 기분이 어떨 것 같아요?
questions.sample: Disappointed, but I'll be back next week. That's what being a fan means.
questions.sample_ko: 실망하겠지만 다음 주에 또 올 거예요. 그게 팬이라는 거죠.

closing: Well said! Let's cheer for the final innings together!
closing_ko: 말씀 잘하셨어요! 마지막 이닝도 같이 응원해요!

title: Are Video Games Bad
situation_ko: 게임을 많이 하는 것에 대해 부모님과 의견을 나눠요.
user_role: a young adult who enjoys gaming

questions.q: You play games for hours. Don't you think that's a waste of time?
questions.q_ko: 몇 시간씩 게임하잖아요. 시간 낭비라고 생각하지 않아요?
questions.sample: I don't think so. It's fine as long as I finish my work first.
questions.sample_ko: 그렇게 생각하지 않아요. 할 일을 먼저 끝내는 한 괜찮아요.

questions.q: What do you get from playing games?
questions.sample: I relax, and I stay in touch with friends. Some games also improve my planning skills.
questions.sample_ko: 긴장을 풀고 친구들과 연락도 이어 가요. 계획 세우는 능력이 늘어나는 게임도 있고요.

questions.q: But I've read that games can be addictive. Does that worry you?
questions.q_ko: 하지만 게임이 중독될 수 있다고 읽었어요. 걱정되지 않아요?
questions.sample: A little, which is why I set limits for myself, like no games after eleven.
questions.sample_ko: 조금요. 그래서 밤 11시 이후엔 안 하는 식으로 스스로 제한을 둬요.

questions.q: Do you think young people today have different hobbies from mine?
questions.q_ko: 요즘 젊은 사람들은 제 세대와 취미가 다르다고 생각해요?
questions.sample: Yes, many hobbies are online now. But people still enjoy hiking and cafes, just in a new way.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 온라인 취미가 많아졌어요. 하지만 등산이나 카페도 여전히 즐기죠, 새로운 방식으로요.

questions.q: Would you play a game with me sometime?
questions.sample: Of course! I'd love to show you what I play, and it might change your mind.
questions.sample_ko: 물론이죠! 제가 하는 게임을 보여 드리고 싶어요, 생각이 바뀌실지도 몰라요.

closing: All right, I'll give it a try. Please be patient with me!
closing_ko: 좋아요, 한번 해 볼게요. 천천히 가르쳐 줘요!

title: Understanding Modern Art
situation_ko: 현대 미술 전시에서 친구가 작품을 어떻게 느끼는지 물어봐요.
ai_role: a friend at a modern art exhibit

key_phrases.text: To be honest, I don't get it.
Art doesn't have to be pretty.

questions.q: What do you think of this piece? It's just a white canvas with one red line.
questions.q_ko: 이 작품은 어떻게 생각해요? 흰 캔버스에 빨간 선 하나뿐이에요.
questions.sample: To be honest, I don't get it at first, but it reminds me of a calm morning with a sunrise.
questions.sample_ko: 솔직히 처음엔 이해가 안 됐는데 해가 뜨는 고요한 아침이 떠올라요.

questions.q: Interesting! Do you think anyone could make this, and does that matter?
questions.q_ko: 흥미롭네요! 누구나 만들 수 있다고 생각해요, 그리고 그게 중요한가요?
questions.sample: Maybe anyone could make it, but the idea is what matters, and the artist thought of it first.
questions.sample_ko: 누구나 만들 수 있을지 몰라도 중요한 건 아이디어이고, 그 작가가 먼저 생각해 낸 거죠.

questions.q: Do you think art should be beautiful?
questions.sample: Not necessarily. Art doesn't have to be pretty. It can make you think or feel something strong.
questions.sample_ko: 꼭 그렇진 않아요. 예술이 꼭 예쁠 필요는 없고 생각이나 강한 감정을 끌어낼 수도 있어요.

questions.q: Which room did you enjoy the most so far?
questions.sample: The video room. The sound and light made me feel like I was inside the artwork.
questions.sample_ko: 영상 전시실이요. 소리와 빛 덕분에 작품 안에 있는 기분이었어요.

questions.q: Would you buy art for your home if you could afford it?
questions.q_ko: 여유가 있다면 집에 걸 미술품을 사겠어요?
questions.sample: Yes, probably a painting by a young local artist, so I could support their career.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 아마 젊은 지역 작가의 그림을 사서 그분의 활동을 응원하고 싶어요.

closing: That's a lovely idea. Let's see the next room!
closing_ko: 멋진 생각이에요. 다음 전시실을 보러 가요!

title: Indoor or Outdoor Hobbies
situation_ko: 친구와 어떤 취미가 더 좋은지 가볍게 토론해요.
ai_role: a friend who loves outdoor hobbies
user_role: a friend who prefers indoor hobbies

key_phrases.text: I'm more of an indoor person.
I'd be open to trying it.

questions.q: Do you prefer indoor hobbies or outdoor hobbies?
questions.q_ko: 실내 취미가 좋아요, 야외 취미가 좋아요?
questions.sample: I'm more of an indoor person. I enjoy reading, drawing, and cooking.
questions.sample_ko: 저는 실내파예요. 독서, 그림, 요리를 즐겨요.

questions.q: Why do you prefer to stay inside?
questions.sample: The weather affects my plans outdoors, and I'm easily tired by crowds and noise.
questions.sample_ko: 야외는 날씨가 계획에 영향을 주고, 사람 많고 시끄러운 데선 쉽게 지쳐요.

questions.q: But fresh air and sunlight are good for you. Don't you miss them?
questions.q_ko: 하지만 맑은 공기와 햇빛은 몸에 좋잖아요. 그리워지지 않아요?
questions.sample: Sometimes, so I take a short walk after lunch. That's enough for me.
questions.sample_ko: 가끔은요. 그래서 점심 후에 짧게 산책해요. 저에겐 그걸로 충분해요.

questions.q: What if I invited you on a camping trip? Would you join?
questions.sample: I'd be open to trying it once, if we pick a place with good facilities.
questions.sample_ko: 시설이 좋은 곳이라면 한번 해 볼 의향은 있어요.

questions.q: What's the biggest benefit of your favorite hobby?
questions.q_ko: 가장 좋아하는 취미의 가장 큰 장점은 뭐예요?
questions.sample: It lets me create something with my own hands, and I feel proud when I finish it.
questions.sample_ko: 직접 뭔가를 만들 수 있고 끝냈을 때 뿌듯해요.

closing: Great answers! Let's mix it up and try a picnic with a book.
closing_ko: 멋진 대답이에요! 반반 섞어서 책 들고 피크닉 가요.

title: Giving Up a Hobby
situation_ko: 오랫동안 하던 취미를 그만둔 이유를 친구가 물어봐요.
ai_role: a friend who noticed the learner stopped a hobby
user_role: a friend who quit a hobby

key_phrases.text: I might pick it up again.

questions.q: You used to play tennis every weekend. Did you stop?
questions.sample: Yes, I stopped about six months ago.

questions.q: Why did you stop?
questions.sample: I didn't have enough time after my promotion, and I also hurt my wrist.
questions.sample_ko: 승진 후에 시간이 부족했고 손목도 다쳤어요.

questions.q: I'm sorry to hear that. Do you miss it?
questions.sample: I do, especially the feeling after a good match, but I've found new ways to move.
questions.sample_ko: 그리워요, 특히 경기 잘 끝낸 후의 기분이요. 하지만 다른 운동을 찾았어요.

questions.q: Do you think it's okay to give up a hobby, or should people stick with it?
questions.q_ko: 취미를 그만두는 건 괜찮다고 생각해요, 아니면 끝까지 해야 한다고 생각해요?
questions.sample: It's okay. Hobbies are supposed to be enjoyable, so if you lose interest, you should let go.
questions.sample_ko: 괜찮다고 생각해요. 취미는 즐거워야 하니까 흥미를 잃으면 놓아줘도 돼요.

questions.q: Will you ever go back to tennis?
questions.sample: I might pick it up again once my wrist heals and my schedule is calmer.
questions.sample_ko: 손목이 낫고 일정이 여유로워지면 다시 시작할지도 몰라요.

closing: If you do, call me. I'll be your practice partner!
closing_ko: 다시 하게 되면 불러요. 제가 연습 상대가 되어 줄게요!

title: Hobbies and Stress
situation_ko: 상담 시간에 상담사가 취미가 스트레스 해소에 어떻게 도움이 되는지 물어봐요.

key_phrases.text: It helps me clear my head.
I try to make time for myself.
key_phrases.ko: 저 자신을 위한 시간을 만들려고 해요.

questions.q: Thanks for coming in. How has your stress level been lately?
questions.q_ko: 와 주셔서 감사해요. 요즘 스트레스는 어떤가요?
questions.sample: Pretty high. Work is busy, and I tend to overthink things at night.
questions.sample_ko: 꽤 높아요. 일이 바쁘고 밤에 생각이 많아져요.

questions.q: That sounds tough. What do you do to relax?
questions.sample: I go for a run or play the guitar. It helps me clear my head.
questions.sample_ko: 달리거나 기타를 쳐요. 머리를 비우는 데 도움이 돼요.

questions.q: Why do you think these activities help you?
questions.q_ko: 이런 활동이 왜 도움이 된다고 생각해요?
questions.sample: Because I focus on one thing, and I stop thinking about deadlines for a while.
questions.sample_ko: 한 가지에 집중하게 되어 잠시 마감 걱정을 잊거든요.

questions.q: Do you find it hard to make time for them?
questions.sample: Yes, especially during busy weeks, but I try to make time for myself at least twice a week.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 특히 바쁜 주에는요. 그래도 최소 일주일에 두 번은 저를 위한 시간을 만들려고 해요.

questions.q: What new activity might you try to feel even better?
questions.q_ko: 더 나아지기 위해 새로 해 볼 만한 활동이 있나요?
questions.sample: Maybe meditation or pottery. I've heard working with clay is very calming.
questions.sample_ko: 명상이나 도예를 해 볼까 해요. 흙을 만지면 마음이 아주 차분해진다고 들었어요.

closing: Those are wonderful choices. Remember, rest is part of being productive.
closing_ko: 훌륭한 선택이에요. 쉬는 것도 생산적인 일의 일부라는 걸 기억하세요.

title: A Headache at the Clinic
situation_ko: 머리가 아파서 동네 병원에 가서 의사 선생님과 이야기해요.
ai_role: A friendly doctor at a small clinic

questions.q: Hello. What's the problem today?
questions.sample: I have a headache.

questions.q: I see. Does it hurt a lot?
questions.sample: Yes, it hurts a lot.

questions.q: Okay. When did it start?
questions.sample: It started yesterday.

questions.q: Did you sleep well last night?
questions.sample: No, I slept only four hours.

questions.q: I see. Do you drink enough water every day?
questions.sample: No, not really.

closing: Thank you. Please rest, drink water, and come back if it gets worse.
closing_ko: 고마워요. 쉬고 물을 마시고, 더 심해지면 다시 오세요.

title: Cold Medicine at the Pharmacy
situation_ko: 감기에 걸려서 약국에서 약사에게 약을 부탁해요.

questions.q: Hi there. How can I help you?
questions.sample: I have a cold. I need some medicine.

questions.q: Oh, I'm sorry. Do you have a sore throat?
questions.sample: Yes, my throat hurts.

questions.q: I see. Do you have a cough?
questions.sample: Yes, a little.

questions.q: Okay. Are you allergic to any medicine?
questions.q_ko: 알겠어요. 먹으면 안 되는 약 알레르기가 있어요?
questions.sample: No, I'm not.

questions.q: Good. Do you want pills or syrup?
questions.sample: Pills, please.

closing: Here you go. Take one after each meal, and get well soon!
closing_ko: 여기 있어요. 식사 후에 한 알씩 드시고, 빨리 나으세요!

title: Toothache at the Dentist
situation_ko: 이가 아파서 치과 선생님께 어디가 아픈지 말해요.

questions.q: Hello. What's wrong with your tooth?
questions.sample: My tooth hurts.

questions.q: I see. Which side is it?
questions.sample: On the left side.

questions.q: Okay. Does cold water make it hurt?
questions.sample: Yes, it hurts a lot.

questions.q: Thank you. How many times do you brush your teeth a day?
questions.sample: Two times a day.

questions.q: Good. Do you like sweet food?
questions.sample: Yes, I love chocolate.

closing: Okay, open wide. I'll be gentle. It won't take long.
closing_ko: 자, 크게 벌려 주세요. 살살 할게요. 오래 안 걸려요.

title: I Can't Sleep
situation_ko: 요즘 잠을 잘 못 자서 친구에게 이야기해요.
user_role: A friend who cannot sleep well

key_phrases.text: I go to bed at midnight.

questions.q: You look tired. Are you okay?
questions.sample: I can't sleep well these days.

questions.q: Oh no. What time do you go to bed?
questions.sample: I go to bed at midnight.

questions.q: I see. Do you use your phone in bed?
questions.sample: Yes, I watch videos.

questions.q: Hmm. Do you drink coffee in the evening?
questions.sample: Yes, sometimes.

questions.q: I see. How many hours do you want to sleep?
questions.sample: I want to sleep eight hours.

closing: Try no phone before bed tonight. I hope you sleep well!
closing_ko: 오늘 밤은 자기 전에 휴대폰을 하지 마세요. 푹 자길 바라요!

title: A Healthy Breakfast
situation_ko: 동료와 아침에 무엇을 먹는지 이야기해요.
ai_role: A coworker who likes healthy food

questions.q: Good morning! Did you eat breakfast today?
questions.sample: Yes, I ate toast and eggs.

questions.q: Nice! Do you eat breakfast every day?
questions.sample: No, sometimes I skip it.

questions.q: I see. Do you like fruit?
questions.sample: Yes, I like apples.

questions.q: Great. What do you drink in the morning?
questions.sample: I drink coffee.

questions.q: Oh, I see. What is your favorite healthy food?
questions.q_ko: 아, 그렇군요. 가장 좋아하는 건강 음식이 뭐예요?
questions.sample: I like salad.

closing: Nice talking with you. Let's have a healthy breakfast together sometime!
closing_ko: 이야기해서 좋았어요. 언제 같이 건강한 아침 먹어요!

title: Calling in Sick
situation_ko: 몸이 아파서 회사에 전화해서 오늘 못 간다고 말해요.

questions.q: Hello. What's up?
questions.sample: I'm sick today. I can't come to work.

questions.q: Oh, I'm sorry to hear that. What's wrong?
questions.sample: I have a fever.

questions.q: I see. Are you going to see a doctor?
questions.sample: Yes, I'm going this afternoon.

questions.q: Good. Do you need anything from the office?
questions.sample: No, I'm fine.

questions.q: Okay. When can you come back?
questions.sample: Maybe tomorrow.

closing: Thanks for calling. Rest well and take care!
closing_ko: 전화 줘서 고마워요. 푹 쉬고 몸조심하세요!

title: Do You Exercise?
situation_ko: 새 이웃과 어떤 운동을 하는지 이야기해요.

questions.q: Hi! Do you exercise?
questions.sample: Yes, I walk every day.

questions.q: That's nice! How long do you walk?
questions.sample: About thirty minutes.

questions.q: Great. Do you like sports?
questions.sample: Yes, I like swimming.

questions.q: Cool! When do you swim?
questions.sample: On weekends.

questions.q: Nice. Do you exercise alone or with friends?
questions.sample: I exercise alone.

closing: It was nice to meet you. Let's walk together sometime!
closing_ko: 만나서 반가웠어요. 언제 같이 걸어요!

title: I Lost My Wallet
situation_ko: 가게에서 지갑을 잃어버려서 직원에게 도움을 청해요.
user_role: A customer who lost a wallet

questions.q: Hello. Can I help you?
questions.sample: Yes, I lost my wallet.

questions.q: Oh no. What color is it?
questions.sample: It's black.

questions.q: Okay. Where did you sit?
questions.sample: I sat near the window.

questions.q: I see. What's in the wallet?
questions.sample: My cards and some money.

questions.q: Thank you. What's your phone number?

closing: Don't worry. If we find it, we'll call you right away.
closing_ko: 걱정 마세요. 찾으면 바로 전화드릴게요.

title: An Eye Test
situation_ko: 글자가 잘 안 보여서 안과에서 시력 검사를 받아요.

questions.q: Hello. What's the problem?
questions.sample: I can't see well.

questions.q: I see. Do you wear glasses?
questions.sample: Yes, I do.

questions.q: Okay. Are your eyes tired?
questions.sample: Yes, they are tired by evening.

questions.q: I see. Do you use a computer a lot?
questions.sample: Yes, eight hours a day.

questions.q: Okay. Can you read the small letters?
questions.q_ko: 알겠어요. 작은 글자를 읽을 수 있어요?
questions.sample: No, they're too small.

closing: Thank you. Now let's try some new lenses.
closing_ko: 고마워요. 이제 새 렌즈를 써 볼게요.

title: My Stomach Hurts
situation_ko: 배가 아파서 엄마에게 어디가 아픈지 말해요.
user_role: A child or grown son/daughter with a stomachache

questions.q: What's wrong? You look pale.
questions.sample: My stomach hurts.

questions.q: Oh dear. What did you eat today?
questions.sample: I ate pizza and ice cream.

questions.q: I see. Did you eat a lot?
questions.sample: Yes, I ate too much.

questions.q: Hmm. Do you want some warm tea?
questions.sample: Yes, please.

questions.q: Okay. Do you feel sick or just full?
questions.sample: I just feel full.

closing: Okay, sit down and rest. You'll feel better soon.
closing_ko: 그래, 앉아서 쉬어. 곧 나아질 거야.

title: My Allergy
situation_ko: 식당에서 먹을 수 없는 음식이 있다고 직원에게 말해요.
user_role: A customer with a food allergy

questions.q: Welcome! Are you ready to order?
questions.sample: Yes. But I'm allergic to nuts.

questions.q: Thank you for telling me. What would you like?
questions.sample: I'd like a chicken salad.

questions.q: Okay. Do you want it without nuts?
questions.sample: Yes, no nuts, please.

questions.q: Sure. Do you have any other allergies?
questions.sample: No, only nuts.

questions.q: Got it. What would you like to drink?
questions.sample: Water, please.

closing: Thank you. I'll tell the kitchen. Your food will be ready soon.
closing_ko: 감사합니다. 주방에 말해 둘게요. 곧 음식이 나올 거예요.

title: Drinking Water
situation_ko: 친구와 하루에 물을 얼마나 마시는지 이야기해요.
ai_role: A friend who wants to be healthier

questions.q: Hey! I'm trying to drink more water. Do you drink a lot?
questions.q_ko: 안녕! 나 물을 더 마시려고 하는 중이야. 너는 많이 마셔?
questions.sample: No, I drink only two cups a day.

questions.q: Oh, really? Why not more?
questions.q_ko: 아, 정말? 왜 더 안 마셔?
questions.sample: I forget.

questions.q: I see. Do you drink soda or juice?
questions.sample: Sometimes soda.

questions.q: Hmm. Do you have a water bottle?
questions.sample: Yes, I have a blue one.

questions.q: Nice! Do you take it to work?
questions.sample: Yes, every day.

closing: Let's both drink more water this week. You can do it!
closing_ko: 이번 주엔 우리 둘 다 물을 더 마시자. 할 수 있어!

title: Locked Out
situation_ko: 열쇠 없이 문이 잠겨서 관리인에게 도움을 청해요.
user_role: A resident who is locked out

questions.q: Hello. Can I help you?
questions.sample: Yes, I'm locked out.

questions.q: Oh no. Which room is yours?
questions.sample: Room 502.

questions.q: Okay. Where is your key?
questions.sample: It's inside the room.

questions.q: I see. Do you have your ID?
questions.sample: Yes, I have it here.

questions.q: Good. Is anyone at home?
questions.sample: No, no one is home.

closing: Don't worry. I have a spare key. Let's go together.
closing_ko: 걱정 마세요. 여분 열쇠가 있어요. 같이 가요.

title: A Hurt Knee
situation_ko: 넘어져서 무릎을 다쳐서 직장 동료가 괜찮은지 물어봐요.

questions.q: Oh no! Are you okay?
questions.sample: I fell down. My knee hurts.

questions.q: I'm sorry. Where did you fall?
questions.sample: On the stairs.

questions.q: I see. Is there any blood?
questions.sample: Yes, a little.

questions.q: Okay. Can you walk?
questions.sample: Yes, but slowly.

questions.q: Good. Do you want a bandage?
questions.sample: Yes, please. Thank you.

closing: Sit here and rest. I'll get the first aid kit.
closing_ko: 여기 앉아서 쉬세요. 구급상자를 가져올게요.

title: Getting a Flu Shot
situation_ko: 독감 예방주사를 맞으러 병원에 가서 간호사와 이야기해요.

questions.q: Hello. How can I help you?
questions.sample: I want a flu shot.

questions.q: Sure. Do you have a fever today?
questions.sample: No, I feel fine.

questions.q: Good. Are you allergic to anything?
questions.sample: No, I'm not.

questions.q: Okay. Which arm do you want?
questions.sample: My left arm, please.

questions.q: Sure. Are you afraid of needles?
questions.sample: Yes, a little.

closing: All done! That was quick. Please rest today.
closing_ko: 다 됐어요! 금방이었죠. 오늘은 쉬세요.

title: Describing a Fever
situation_ko: 열과 기침이 있어서 의사에게 증상을 자세히 설명해요.

key_phrases.text: I've had a fever for two days.

questions.q: Hello. What brings you in today?
questions.sample: I've had a fever for two days, and I feel very weak.
questions.sample_ko: 이틀째 열이 나고 기운이 하나도 없어요.

questions.q: I see. Do you have any other symptoms, like a cough?
questions.q_ko: 그렇군요. 기침 같은 다른 증상도 있어요?
questions.sample: Yes, I have a dry cough, especially at night.

questions.q: Okay. Have you taken any medicine?
questions.sample: I took some fever medicine yesterday, but it didn't help much.
questions.sample_ko: 어제 해열제를 먹었는데 별로 도움이 안 됐어요.

questions.q: I see. Have you been around anyone who was sick?
questions.q_ko: 그렇군요. 아픈 사람과 접촉한 적 있어요?
questions.sample: Yes, my coworker had a cold last week.

questions.q: Thanks. Are you eating and drinking normally?
questions.q_ko: 고마워요. 식사와 수분 섭취는 평소처럼 하고 있어요?
