questions.sample: I'm drinking a lot, but I don't feel like eating.

closing: Thank you for explaining. Let me check your throat and give you a prescription.
closing_ko: 설명해 주셔서 고마워요. 목을 살펴보고 처방전을 써 드릴게요.

title: Booking a Doctor's Appointment
situation_ko: 전화로 병원에 진료 예약을 해요.

key_phrases.text: I'd like to make an appointment.
Do you have anything on Friday?

questions.q: Good morning, Sunrise Clinic. How can I help you?
questions.sample: Hi, I'd like to make an appointment with a doctor.

questions.q: Sure. Is this your first time here?
questions.sample: Yes, it's my first visit.

questions.q: Okay. What is the reason for your visit?
questions.sample: I've had back pain for a week.

questions.q: I see. We have an opening Friday morning or Monday afternoon. Which do you prefer?
questions.q_ko: 그렇군요. 금요일 오전이나 월요일 오후에 자리가 있어요. 어느 쪽이 좋으세요?
questions.sample: Friday morning is better for me.

questions.q: Great. Can I have your name and phone number?
questions.sample: My name is Jin Park, and my number is 010-2345-6789.

closing: You're all set for Friday at 10. Please bring your insurance card.
closing_ko: 금요일 10시로 예약됐어요. 보험증을 가져오세요.

title: Picking Up a Prescription
situation_ko: 병원에서 받은 처방전으로 약국에서 약을 받아요.

key_phrases.text: How often should I take it?

questions.q: Hi. How can I help you?
questions.sample: Hi, I have a prescription from Dr. Kim.

questions.q: Thanks. Is this the first time you're taking this medicine?
questions.q_ko: 감사합니다. 이 약은 처음 드시는 건가요?
questions.sample: Yes, it's my first time.

questions.q: Okay. Are you taking any other medicine right now?
questions.q_ko: 알겠어요. 지금 드시는 다른 약이 있어요?
questions.sample: Just vitamins. Nothing else.

questions.q: Good. Do you have any questions about how to take it?
questions.q_ko: 좋아요. 복용법에 대해 궁금한 게 있어요?
questions.sample: How often should I take it, and before or after meals?
questions.sample_ko: 얼마나 자주, 식전인지 식후인지 알려 주세요.

questions.q: Sure. Would you like a printed sheet with the instructions?
questions.sample: Yes, please. That would help me remember.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 주세요. 기억하는 데 도움이 될 거예요.

closing: Take one pill after breakfast and dinner. Feel better soon!
closing_ko: 아침과 저녁 식사 후에 한 알씩 드세요. 빨리 나으세요!

title: A Dental Cleaning
situation_ko: 정기 치아 검진과 스케일링을 받으러 치과에 가요.
user_role: A patient for a dental check-up

key_phrases.text: It's been a year since my last visit.
I floss a few times a week.

questions.q: Welcome! When was your last dental visit?
questions.q_ko: 어서 오세요! 마지막으로 치과에 온 게 언제였어요?
questions.sample: It's been about a year.

questions.q: I see. Do you have any pain or problems right now?
questions.q_ko: 그렇군요. 지금 아프거나 불편한 곳이 있어요?
questions.sample: Not really, but my gums bleed sometimes when I brush.
questions.sample_ko: 딱히 없는데, 양치할 때 가끔 잇몸에서 피가 나요.

questions.q: Okay. How often do you brush your teeth?
questions.sample: Twice a day, morning and night.
questions.sample_ko: 하루 두 번, 아침과 밤에 해요.

questions.q: Good. Do you use dental floss?
questions.sample: I try to, but only a few times a week.
questions.sample_ko: 노력은 하는데 일주일에 몇 번밖에 못 써요.

questions.q: I see. Do you drink a lot of coffee or tea?
questions.sample: Yes, about three cups of coffee a day.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 하루에 커피 세 잔쯤 마셔요.

closing: Thanks. Let's begin the cleaning. Just raise your hand if you need a break.
closing_ko: 고마워요. 스케일링을 시작할게요. 쉬고 싶으면 손을 들어 주세요.

title: Buying New Glasses
situation_ko: 안경이 부러져서 새 안경을 맞추러 안경점에 가요.
ai_role: An optician at an eyewear shop

questions.q: Hi there! What can I do for you?
questions.sample: My glasses broke, so I need a new pair.

questions.q: Oh, I'm sorry. Do you know your prescription?
questions.sample: No, I don't. Can you check my eyes first?
questions.sample_ko: 아니요, 몰라요. 먼저 시력을 재 주실 수 있나요?

questions.q: Of course. What kind of frames do you like, thick or thin?
questions.q_ko: 물론이죠. 어떤 테를 좋아하세요, 두꺼운 거요, 얇은 거요?
questions.sample: I prefer thin, light frames because I wear them all day.
questions.sample_ko: 하루 종일 쓰니까 얇고 가벼운 테가 좋아요.

questions.q: Nice choice. What's your budget?
questions.sample: Around one hundred thousand won, if possible.

questions.q: Okay. Do you also want blue-light lenses for computer work?
questions.q_ko: 알겠어요. 컴퓨터 작업용 블루라이트 렌즈도 원하세요?
questions.sample: Yes, I work at a computer all day, so that sounds good.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 하루 종일 컴퓨터를 하니까 좋겠어요.

closing: Great. Your glasses will be ready in about three days. We'll text you.
closing_ko: 좋아요. 안경은 3일쯤 뒤에 준비돼요. 문자 드릴게요.

title: Trouble Falling Asleep
situation_ko: 몇 주째 잠들기 힘들어서 의사와 수면 습관을 이야기해요.

key_phrases.text: I wake up several times at night.

questions.q: Hello. What seems to be the problem?
questions.sample: I haven't been sleeping well for about three weeks.

questions.q: I'm sorry to hear that. Is it hard to fall asleep, or do you wake up at night?
questions.q_ko: 안타깝네요. 잠들기가 힘든가요, 아니면 밤에 깨나요?
questions.sample: Both. I take an hour to fall asleep, and I wake up several times.
questions.sample_ko: 둘 다요. 잠드는 데 한 시간 걸리고 밤에 여러 번 깨요.

questions.q: I see. What do you think is causing it?
questions.sample: Maybe work. My mind keeps racing about deadlines.
questions.sample_ko: 아마 일 때문인 것 같아요. 마감 생각에 머리가 계속 돌아가요.

questions.q: That makes sense. What do you usually do before bed?
questions.q_ko: 이해돼요. 보통 자기 전에 뭘 해요?
questions.sample: I check my email and watch videos on my phone.

questions.q: Okay. How do you feel during the day?
questions.sample: I feel exhausted, and it's hard to focus at work.

closing: Thank you. Let's start with a regular bedtime and no screens before sleep.
closing_ko: 고마워요. 규칙적인 취침 시간과 자기 전 화면 안 보기부터 시작해 봐요.

title: Stress at Work
situation_ko: 요즘 일이 너무 많아서 믿을 만한 동료와 스트레스를 이야기해요.

key_phrases.text: I'm under a lot of pressure.
I can't switch off after work.

questions.q: Hey, you seem stressed lately. What's going on?
questions.q_ko: 요즘 스트레스 받아 보여요. 무슨 일이에요?
questions.sample: I have too much work, and I'm under a lot of pressure.

questions.q: That sounds hard. What's the hardest part?
questions.sample: The deadlines. I can't switch off even after I go home.
questions.sample_ko: 마감이에요. 집에 가도 머리가 안 쉬어요.

questions.q: I understand. How does the stress affect you?
questions.sample: I get headaches, and I'm often in a bad mood.
questions.sample_ko: 두통이 생기고 기분이 자주 안 좋아요.

questions.q: Hmm. What do you do to relax?
questions.sample: I take a walk or listen to music, which helps a bit.
questions.sample_ko: 산책하거나 음악을 듣는데, 조금 도움이 돼요.

questions.q: Good idea. Would it help to talk to your manager about your workload?
questions.q_ko: 좋은 생각이에요. 업무량에 대해 매니저와 이야기하면 도움이 될까요?
questions.sample: Maybe. I'm a little nervous, but I think I should.
questions.sample_ko: 그럴지도요. 조금 긴장되지만 해야 할 것 같아요.

closing: I'm here if you want to talk. Let's get lunch tomorrow and take a real break.
closing_ko: 얘기하고 싶으면 언제든 말해요. 내일 점심 같이 먹고 제대로 쉬어요.

title: Joining a Gym
situation_ko: 헬스장에 가서 회원 등록과 운동 목표를 상담해요.

key_phrases.text: I want to lose some weight.
Can I try it for a day first?

questions.q: Welcome to FitLife! Are you interested in joining?
questions.q_ko: 핏라이프에 오신 걸 환영해요! 등록에 관심 있으세요?
questions.sample: Yes, I'd like to know about your membership.

questions.q: Great! What are your goals?
questions.sample: I want to lose a little weight and get stronger.
questions.sample_ko: 살을 조금 빼고 체력을 키우고 싶어요.

questions.q: Nice. Have you worked out before?
questions.sample: Only walking. I'm a complete beginner at the gym.

questions.q: No problem. How many days a week can you come?
questions.q_ko: 괜찮아요. 일주일에 며칠 올 수 있어요?
questions.sample: Probably three days, after work.
questions.sample_ko: 퇴근 후에 3일쯤 올 수 있을 것 같아요.

questions.q: Perfect. Would you like a three-month or a one-year plan?
questions.sample: Three months, please. I'd like to see if I enjoy it first.
questions.sample_ko: 3개월로 할게요. 먼저 잘 맞는지 보고 싶어요.

closing: Wonderful. Let me show you around and book your first session with a trainer.
closing_ko: 좋아요. 시설을 보여 드리고 트레이너와 첫 수업을 잡아 드릴게요.

title: Trying to Eat Healthier
situation_ko: 영양사와 식습관을 점검하고 더 건강하게 먹는 방법을 이야기해요.
user_role: A client who wants to eat better

key_phrases.text: I'd like to cut down on sugar.
I don't have time to cook.

questions.q: Hello! What would you like to work on today?
questions.q_ko: 안녕하세요! 오늘은 어떤 걸 해 보고 싶으세요?
questions.sample: I want to eat healthier because I feel tired a lot.
questions.sample_ko: 자주 피곤해서 더 건강하게 먹고 싶어요.

questions.q: Good goal. What does a typical day of eating look like for you?
questions.q_ko: 좋은 목표예요. 평소 하루 식사는 어떤가요?
questions.sample: I skip breakfast, eat lunch out, and have a big dinner late.
questions.sample_ko: 아침은 거르고, 점심은 사 먹고, 저녁은 늦게 많이 먹어요.

questions.q: I see. How often do you eat vegetables?
questions.sample: Not often. Maybe a few times a week.

questions.q: Okay. Do you have a sweet tooth?
questions.sample: Yes, I drink sweet coffee and eat snacks in the afternoon.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 단 커피를 마시고 오후에 간식도 먹어요.

questions.q: Thanks for being honest. What's the biggest challenge for you?
questions.q_ko: 솔직히 말해 줘서 고마워요. 가장 어려운 점이 뭐예요?
questions.sample: I don't have time to cook after work.

closing: That's very common. We'll start with small, easy changes, like a simple breakfast.
closing_ko: 흔한 일이에요. 간단한 아침 식사 같은 작고 쉬운 변화부터 시작해 봐요.

title: An Insurance Claim
situation_ko: 병원비를 돌려받으려고 보험사에 전화해서 문의해요.

key_phrases.text: I'd like to file a claim.

questions.q: Thank you for calling. How can I help you?
questions.sample: I'd like to file a claim for a doctor's visit.
questions.sample_ko: 진료 받은 것에 대해 보험금을 청구하고 싶어요.

questions.q: Certainly. When was the visit?
questions.sample: It was last Tuesday, October 13th.

questions.q: Thank you. What was the treatment for?
questions.sample: I hurt my wrist, so I got an X-ray and a bandage.
questions.sample_ko: 손목을 다쳐서 엑스레이를 찍고 붕대를 감았어요.

questions.q: I see. Do you have the receipt and the doctor's note?
questions.sample: Yes, I have both. Can I send them by email?
questions.sample_ko: 네, 둘 다 있어요. 이메일로 보내도 되나요?

questions.q: Yes, that works. Would you like the payment sent to your bank account?
questions.q_ko: 네, 가능해요. 보험금을 은행 계좌로 보내 드릴까요?
questions.sample: Yes, please. How long will it take?

closing: It usually takes about five business days. Thank you for calling!
closing_ko: 보통 영업일 기준 5일쯤 걸려요. 전화 주셔서 감사합니다!

title: At the Emergency Room
situation_ko: 갑자기 다쳐서 응급실에 가서 접수 직원과 이야기해요.

questions.q: Hello. What happened?
questions.sample: I cut my hand badly with a kitchen knife.

questions.q: I'm sorry. When did it happen?
questions.sample: About thirty minutes ago.

questions.q: Is it still bleeding?
questions.sample: Yes, it won't stop, even with a towel.

questions.q: Okay. Do you have any allergies or take any medicine?
questions.q_ko: 알겠어요. 알레르기가 있거나 먹는 약이 있어요?
questions.sample: No allergies, and I don't take any medicine.

questions.q: Good. Did anyone come with you?
questions.sample: Yes, my wife is parking the car.

closing: Thank you. Please sit down. A nurse will see you right away.
closing_ko: 고마워요. 앉아 계세요. 간호사가 바로 봐 드릴 거예요.

title: Telling My Boss I'm Sick
situation_ko: 독감에 걸려서 상사에게 며칠 쉬어야 한다고 전화로 말해요.

key_phrases.text: I think I caught the flu.
The doctor told me to rest.

questions.q: Hello, this is Ms. Lee. Is everything okay?
questions.sample: Not really. I think I caught the flu, so I can't come in today.
questions.sample_ko: 별로 안 좋아요. 독감에 걸린 것 같아서 오늘 출근을 못 해요.

questions.q: Oh, I'm sorry. How long have you felt sick?
questions.sample: Since last night. I have a high fever and body aches.

questions.q: I see. Have you seen a doctor?
questions.sample: Yes, this morning. The doctor told me to rest for three days.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 오늘 아침에요. 의사가 사흘 쉬라고 했어요.

questions.q: Okay. Is there any urgent work I should know about?
questions.sample: I have a report due Thursday. I can finish it remotely if I feel better.
questions.sample_ko: 목요일까지 보고서가 있어요. 나아지면 원격으로 끝낼 수 있어요.

questions.q: Please don't push yourself. Who can cover your meeting tomorrow?
questions.q_ko: 무리하지 마세요. 내일 회의는 누가 대신할 수 있을까요?
questions.sample: Maybe Daniel. I'll send him my notes this afternoon.
questions.sample_ko: 아마 다니엘이요. 오늘 오후에 제 메모를 보낼게요.

closing: Thanks for letting me know. Focus on getting better. We'll manage.
closing_ko: 알려 줘서 고마워요. 회복에 집중해요. 저희가 알아서 할게요.

title: Check-up Results
situation_ko: 건강검진 결과를 들으러 병원에 가서 의사와 이야기해요.

questions.q: Hello. Thanks for coming in. How have you been feeling lately?
questions.q_ko: 안녕하세요. 와 주셔서 고마워요. 요즘 컨디션은 어때요?
questions.sample: I've been fine, but I get tired easily.

questions.q: I see. Your results are mostly good. Your cholesterol is a little high. Does that run in your family?
questions.q_ko: 그렇군요. 결과는 대부분 좋아요. 콜레스테롤이 조금 높아요. 가족력이 있나요?
questions.sample: Yes, my father had the same problem.

questions.q: Okay. How would you describe your diet?
questions.sample: I eat a lot of fried food and meat, and not many vegetables.
questions.sample_ko: 튀김과 고기를 많이 먹고 채소는 별로 안 먹어요.

questions.q: Do you exercise regularly?
questions.sample: Not really. I sit all day at work.

questions.q: Understood. What small change could you make this month?
questions.q_ko: 알겠어요. 이번 달에 할 수 있는 작은 변화가 뭘까요?
questions.sample: I could walk for thirty minutes after dinner and eat less fried food.
questions.sample_ko: 저녁 식사 후 30분 걷고 튀김을 줄일 수 있을 것 같아요.

closing: That's a great plan. Let's check again in three months.
closing_ko: 좋은 계획이에요. 석 달 뒤에 다시 확인해 봐요.

title: Food Allergy at a Restaurant
situation_ko: 새우 알레르기가 있어서 식당 직원에게 메뉴를 자세히 물어봐요.
user_role: A diner with a shellfish allergy

key_phrases.text: Could the chef make it without it?
key_phrases.ko: 요리사가 그것 없이 만들어 줄 수 있나요?

questions.q: Good evening! Do you have any questions about the menu?
questions.q_ko: 안녕하세요! 메뉴에 대해 궁금한 점 있으세요?
questions.sample: Yes, I have a shellfish allergy. Does the pasta contain shrimp?
questions.sample_ko: 네, 갑각류 알레르기가 있어요. 파스타에 새우가 들어 있나요?

questions.q: Yes, the seafood pasta does. How serious is your allergy?
questions.q_ko: 네, 해산물 파스타에는 들어가요. 알레르기가 심한 편이에요?
questions.sample: Quite serious. I get a rash and my throat swells.
questions.sample_ko: 꽤 심해요. 두드러기가 나고 목이 부어요.

questions.q: Thank you for telling me. We can make the chicken dish in a separate pan. Would that be okay?
questions.q_ko: 알려 줘서 고마워요. 치킨 요리는 별도 팬에 만들 수 있어요. 괜찮을까요?
questions.sample: That would be great. Could you also check the sauce for shellfish?
questions.sample_ko: 좋아요. 소스에도 갑각류가 들어 있는지 확인해 주실래요?

questions.q: Of course. Do you carry any allergy medicine with you?
questions.sample: Yes, I always carry it in my bag, just in case.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 만약을 위해 항상 가방에 넣고 다녀요.

questions.q: That's smart. Would you like anything to drink while you wait?
questions.q_ko: 현명하시네요. 기다리는 동안 마실 것을 드릴까요?
questions.sample: Sparkling water with lemon, please.

closing: Perfect. I'll tell the chef right now, and we'll take good care of you.
closing_ko: 좋아요. 지금 바로 요리사에게 말할게요. 잘 챙겨 드릴게요.

title: A Sprained Ankle
situation_ko: 운동하다 발목을 삐어서 정형외과에서 상태를 설명해요.
user_role: A patient with a sprained ankle

key_phrases.text: I can hardly put weight on it.

questions.q: Hi. What happened to your foot?
questions.sample: I twisted my ankle while playing basketball.

questions.q: I see. When did it happen?
questions.sample: Yesterday evening. It's swollen now.

questions.q: Okay. On a scale of one to ten, how bad is the pain?
questions.sample: About seven when I walk, and three when I rest.

questions.q: Did you put ice on it?
questions.sample: Yes, I iced it last night and kept my foot up.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 어젯밤에 얼음찜질을 하고 발을 올려 뒀어요.

questions.q: Good. Have you hurt this ankle before?
questions.q_ko: 잘했어요. 이 발목을 전에도 다친 적 있어요?
questions.sample: Yes, two years ago, on the same side.

closing: Thank you. Let's take an X-ray to be safe, and then we'll wrap it.
closing_ko: 고마워요. 안전하게 엑스레이를 찍고 붕대를 감을게요.

title: A Friend Feeling Down
situation_ko: 요즘 기운이 없어 보이는 친구에게 이야기를 듣고 위로해요.
ai_role: A friend who has been feeling down

key_phrases.text: Do you want to talk about it?
Maybe you should talk to someone.

questions.q: Hi... I haven't been feeling like myself lately.
questions.sample: I'm sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about it?

questions.q: Thanks. I feel tired all the time, and nothing seems fun. Has that ever happened to you?
questions.q_ko: 고마워. 항상 피곤하고 아무것도 재미가 없어. 너도 그런 적 있어?
questions.sample: Yes, a few years ago. It was a hard time, but it got better.
questions.sample_ko: 응, 몇 년 전에. 힘든 시기였지만 나아졌어.

questions.q: That helps to hear. What helped you back then?
questions.q_ko: 그 말을 들으니 힘이 돼. 그때 뭐가 도움이 됐어?
questions.sample: Talking to my family and going for walks every day.
questions.sample_ko: 가족과 이야기하고 매일 산책한 게 도움이 됐어.

questions.q: I'll try that. Do you think I should see a professional?
questions.q_ko: 해 볼게. 전문가를 만나 보는 게 좋을까?
questions.sample: I think it might help. There's no shame in asking for support.
questions.sample_ko: 도움이 될 것 같아. 도움을 청하는 건 부끄러운 일이 아니야.

questions.q: Maybe you're right. Would you come for a walk with me this weekend?
questions.q_ko: 네 말이 맞을지도 몰라. 이번 주말에 나랑 산책할래?
questions.sample: Of course! How about Saturday morning?

closing: Thank you for listening. It really means a lot to me.
closing_ko: 들어 줘서 고마워. 정말 큰 힘이 돼.

title: Reporting a Lost Wallet
situation_ko: 지하철에서 지갑을 잃어버려서 경찰서에 신고해요.
user_role: A person who lost a wallet

key_phrases.text: I'd like to report a lost wallet.
I think I left it on the subway.

questions.q: Hello. How can I help you?
questions.sample: I'd like to report a lost wallet.

questions.q: I'm sorry to hear that. Where do you think you lost it?
questions.sample: I think I left it on the subway, on line 2.

questions.q: What time was that?
questions.sample: Around six o'clock this evening, during rush hour.

questions.q: Can you describe the wallet and what was inside?
questions.q_ko: 지갑 모양과 안에 든 것을 설명해 주시겠어요?
questions.sample: It's brown leather. It has two credit cards, my ID, and about fifty thousand won.
questions.sample_ko: 갈색 가죽이고, 신용카드 두 장, 신분증, 5만 원쯤 들어 있어요.

questions.q: Thank you. Have you canceled your cards?
questions.sample: Yes, I called the bank on the way here.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 여기 오는 길에 은행에 전화했어요.

closing: Good. I've filed the report. We'll call you if someone turns it in.
closing_ko: 잘하셨어요. 신고를 접수했어요. 누가 맡기면 연락드릴게요.

title: Calling a Locksmith
situation_ko: 열쇠를 두고 나와 집에 못 들어가서 열쇠 수리 업체에 전화해요.
user_role: A person locked out of their apartment

key_phrases.text: I'm locked out of my apartment.
How soon can you get here?

questions.q: Hello, Quick Lock service. What's the problem?
questions.sample: I'm locked out of my apartment. I left my key inside.
questions.sample_ko: 집에 못 들어가요. 열쇠를 안에 두고 나왔어요.

questions.q: I see. What type of lock is it, a key lock or a digital lock?
questions.sample: It's a digital lock, but the battery died.

questions.q: Okay. What's your address?
questions.sample: It's 25 Maple Street, apartment 303.

questions.q: Got it. Can you show ID that proves you live there?
questions.q_ko: 알겠어요. 거기 산다는 걸 증명할 신분증을 보여 주실 수 있어요?
questions.sample: Yes, I have my ID with this address on it.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 이 주소가 적힌 신분증이 있어요.

questions.q: Good. Is it okay if we come in about thirty minutes?
questions.sample: That's fine. How much will it cost?

closing: It's about forty thousand won. Please wait at the door, and we'll be there soon.
closing_ko: 약 4만 원이에요. 문 앞에서 기다려 주세요. 곧 도착할게요.

title: Back Pain from Sitting
situation_ko: 사무실에서 오래 앉아 일해서 허리가 아파 물리치료사와 상담해요.
user_role: An office worker with back pain

key_phrases.text: I sit for about nine hours a day.
The pain gets worse in the afternoon.
I rarely get up to stretch.

questions.q: Hello! Where does it hurt?
questions.sample: My lower back hurts, especially in the afternoon.

questions.q: I see. How long have you had this pain?
questions.sample: About a month. It started after I changed jobs.

questions.q: Okay. What does your workday look like?
questions.sample: I sit at a desk for about nine hours and rarely get up.
questions.sample_ko: 책상에 아홉 시간쯤 앉아 있고 거의 일어나지 않아요.

questions.q: Do you ever feel numbness or pain going down your leg?
questions.q_ko: 다리로 저리거나 통증이 내려가는 느낌이 있어요?
questions.sample: No, only in my back.

questions.q: Good. Do you stretch or exercise at all?
questions.sample: Not really. I'd like to start, but I don't know where to begin.
questions.sample_ko: 별로요. 시작하고 싶은데 어디서부터 해야 할지 모르겠어요.

closing: Let's start with simple stretches you can do at your desk every hour.
closing_ko: 한 시간마다 책상에서 할 수 있는 간단한 스트레칭부터 시작해 봐요.

title: Asking About Vitamins
situation_ko: 요즘 피곤해서 약국에서 비타민에 대해 상담해요.

key_phrases.text: Can I take it with my other pills?

questions.q: Hi! What can I help you find?
questions.sample: I've been feeling run down lately. I'm thinking about taking vitamins.
questions.sample_ko: 요즘 몸이 지쳐서 비타민을 먹어 볼까 해요.

questions.q: I see. How is your diet? Do you eat fruit and vegetables?
questions.q_ko: 그렇군요. 식단은 어때요? 과일과 채소를 먹나요?
questions.sample: Not enough. I often eat instant food because I'm busy.
questions.sample_ko: 충분하지 않아요. 바빠서 인스턴트를 자주 먹어요.

questions.q: Okay. Do you get much sun or go outside?
questions.q_ko: 알겠어요. 햇볕을 쬐거나 밖에 자주 나가요?
questions.sample: Not much. I work indoors from morning until night.

questions.q: I understand. Are you taking any other medicine?
questions.sample: Just a blood pressure pill. Can I take vitamins with it?
questions.sample_ko: 혈압약만 먹어요. 비타민을 같이 먹어도 되나요?

questions.q: Generally yes, but check with your doctor too. Do you prefer pills or gummies?
questions.q_ko: 보통은 괜찮지만 의사와도 확인해 보세요. 알약과 젤리 중 어느 쪽이 좋으세요?
questions.sample: Gummies, because I don't like swallowing pills.
questions.sample_ko: 알약 삼키는 걸 싫어해서 젤리가 좋아요.

closing: Here's a good multivitamin gummy. Remember, healthy food and sleep matter most too.
closing_ko: 괜찮은 종합비타민 젤리예요. 건강한 식사와 수면이 가장 중요하다는 것도 기억하세요.

title: Getting a Second Opinion
situation_ko: 수술을 권유받은 뒤 다른 병원에서 두 번째 의견을 들어요.
user_role: A patient seeking a second opinion

key_phrases.text: I'd like another opinion before deciding.
key_phrases.ko: 결정 전에 다른 의견을 듣고 싶어요.

key_phrases.text: What are the risks and alternatives?
I'm worried about the recovery time.

questions.q: Welcome. I've read your records. Why did you decide to come for a second opinion?
questions.q_ko: 어서 오세요. 기록을 읽어 봤어요. 왜 두 번째 의견을 들으러 오기로 하셨어요?
questions.sample: My doctor recommended surgery, and I'd like to be sure before making such a big decision.
questions.sample_ko: 의사가 수술을 권했는데, 큰 결정이라 확신하고 싶었어요.

questions.q: That's very reasonable. How much does the problem affect your daily life?
questions.q_ko: 아주 합리적이에요. 그 문제가 일상에 얼마나 영향을 주나요?
questions.sample: It's painful to climb stairs, and I can't play sports anymore, which really bothers me.
questions.sample_ko: 계단 오르기가 아프고 더는 운동을 못 해서 많이 속상해요.

questions.q: I see. Have you tried any non-surgical treatments?
questions.q_ko: 그렇군요. 수술이 아닌 치료는 해 보셨어요?
questions.sample: I did physical therapy for two months, but it didn't help as much as I'd hoped.
questions.sample_ko: 두 달간 물리치료를 받았는데 기대만큼 효과가 없었어요.

questions.q: Understood. What worries you most about surgery?
questions.q_ko: 알겠어요. 수술에서 가장 걱정되는 게 뭐예요?
questions.sample: The recovery time. I can't take a long break from work.
questions.sample_ko: 회복 기간이요. 직장을 오래 쉴 수가 없어요.

questions.q: That's a fair concern. What would you like to know from me today?
questions.q_ko: 충분히 이해돼요. 오늘 저에게 무엇을 알고 싶으세요?
questions.sample: I'd like to know the risks, whether there are other options, and what happens if I wait.
questions.sample_ko: 위험이 뭔지, 다른 방법이 있는지, 기다리면 어떻게 되는지 알고 싶어요.

closing: Let's go over your scans together and compare all your options carefully.
closing_ko: 함께 검사 결과를 보면서 모든 선택지를 꼼꼼히 비교해 봐요.

title: Burnout and Balance
situation_ko: 일에 지친 친구와 번아웃의 원인과 해결 방법을 이야기해요.
ai_role: A friend who works in HR
user_role: A friend who feels burned out

key_phrases.text: I think it would be good to take time off.

questions.q: You've seemed exhausted for a while. What's been going on?
questions.q_ko: 한동안 지쳐 보였어요. 무슨 일이 있었어요?
questions.sample: I feel completely burned out. I work late almost every night, and I never get a real break.
questions.sample_ko: 완전히 번아웃된 것 같아요. 거의 매일 야근하고 제대로 쉬지를 못해요.

questions.q: That sounds draining. Why do you think it got this bad?
questions.q_ko: 기운이 빠지겠어요. 왜 이렇게까지 됐다고 생각해요?
questions.sample: I find it hard to say no, so I keep taking on extra tasks.
questions.sample_ko: 거절을 못 해서 계속 일을 더 맡게 돼요.

questions.q: I get that. What would help you most right now?
questions.q_ko: 이해해요. 지금 무엇이 가장 도움이 될까요?
questions.sample: I think I need to set boundaries and take a few days off to recover.
questions.sample_ko: 선을 정하고 며칠 쉬면서 회복해야 할 것 같아요.

questions.q: That sounds wise. Do you think your company supports people taking time off?
questions.q_ko: 현명하네요. 회사가 휴가를 쓰는 걸 지지해 주는 분위기인가요?
questions.sample: Officially yes, but people feel guilty if they use their vacation days.
questions.sample_ko: 공식적으로는 그렇지만 휴가를 쓰면 눈치를 봐요.

questions.q: In your opinion, how can a workplace help prevent burnout?
questions.q_ko: 당신 생각에 직장은 번아웃을 막기 위해 어떻게 도울 수 있을까요?
questions.sample: I think realistic workloads and managers who respect people's free time would make a big difference.
questions.sample_ko: 현실적인 업무량과 직원의 개인 시간을 존중하는 관리자가 큰 차이를 만들 것 같아요.

closing: Thank you for being so open with me. Please take care of yourself first.
closing_ko: 솔직하게 얘기해 줘서 고마워요. 먼저 자신을 잘 돌보세요.

title: Sleep Habits and Productivity
situation_ko: 동료와 잠이 일의 효율에 어떤 영향을 주는지 의견을 나눠요.

key_phrases.text: In my experience, sleep affects my focus.
key_phrases.ko: 제 경험상 잠이 집중력에 영향을 줘요.

key_phrases.text: I'd rather sleep than work late.

questions.q: I read that most adults need seven to nine hours of sleep. How much do you usually get?
questions.q_ko: 성인은 대부분 7~9시간을 자야 한다고 읽었어요. 보통 얼마나 자요?
questions.sample: Probably six hours on weekdays, but I try to catch up on weekends.

questions.q: Interesting. Do you notice a difference in your work when you sleep badly?
questions.q_ko: 흥미롭네요. 잠을 못 자면 일에서 차이가 느껴져요?
questions.sample: Definitely. In my experience, I make more mistakes and get irritated more easily.
questions.sample_ko: 확실히요. 제 경험상 실수가 늘고 더 쉽게 짜증이 나요.

questions.q: I feel the same. Some people say they work better at night. Do you think that's true?
questions.q_ko: 저도 그래요. 어떤 사람들은 밤에 일이 더 잘된다고 하던데, 사실일까요?
questions.sample: Maybe for some people, but I think most of us just get used to being tired.
questions.sample_ko: 일부는 그럴 수도 있지만 대부분은 피곤함에 익숙해진 것뿐인 것 같아요.

questions.q: That's a good point. Should companies allow short naps at work?
questions.q_ko: 좋은 지적이에요. 회사가 근무 중 짧은 낮잠을 허용해야 할까요?
questions.sample: I think so. A twenty-minute nap could boost focus, and it would cost nothing.
questions.sample_ko: 그렇게 생각해요. 20분 낮잠은 집중력을 높일 수 있고 비용도 안 들어요.

questions.q: Nice idea. What's one thing you could do to improve your sleep this month?
questions.q_ko: 좋은 생각이에요. 이번 달에 수면을 개선하려면 어떤 걸 할 수 있을까요?
questions.sample: I'd stop using my phone an hour before bed and go to bed at the same time each night.
questions.sample_ko: 자기 한 시간 전엔 휴대폰을 끄고 매일 같은 시간에 잘 거예요.

closing: Good plan. Let's compare notes in a month and see who sleeps better!
closing_ko: 좋은 계획이에요. 한 달 뒤에 누가 더 잘 자는지 비교해 봐요!

title: A Denied Insurance Claim
situation_ko: 보험사가 치료비 지급을 거절해서 상담원에게 이유를 묻고 재심사를 요청해요.

key_phrases.text: I don't understand why it was denied.
According to my policy, it should be covered.
I'd like to appeal the decision.

questions.q: Thank you for calling. How can I help you today?
questions.q_ko: 전화 주셔서 감사합니다. 오늘 무엇을 도와드릴까요?
questions.sample: I received a letter saying my claim was denied, and I don't understand why.
questions.sample_ko: 청구가 거절됐다는 편지를 받았는데 이유를 모르겠어요.

questions.q: I'm sorry for the confusion. Which treatment was the claim for?
questions.q_ko: 혼란을 드려 죄송합니다. 어떤 치료에 대한 청구였나요?
questions.sample: It was for physical therapy after my knee injury, six sessions in total.
questions.sample_ko: 무릎 부상 후 물리치료였고 총 여섯 번 받았어요.

questions.q: I see. The letter says it was not considered medically necessary. What do you think about that?
questions.q_ko: 그렇군요. 편지에는 의학적으로 필요하지 않다고 되어 있네요. 어떻게 생각하세요?
questions.sample: I disagree, because my doctor prescribed it, and according to my policy, it should be covered.
questions.sample_ko: 동의할 수 없어요. 의사가 처방했고 제 약관상 보장되어야 하니까요.

questions.q: Do you have any documents that support your case?
questions.sample: Yes, I have the doctor's prescription and a letter explaining why the therapy was needed.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 처방전과 치료가 왜 필요했는지 설명하는 소견서가 있어요.

questions.q: Good. What outcome are you hoping for?
questions.sample: I'd like to appeal the decision and have the full amount reconsidered.
questions.sample_ko: 이의를 제기해서 전액을 다시 심사받고 싶어요.

closing: Understood. I'll open an appeal and email you the form. You'll hear back within two weeks.
closing_ko: 알겠습니다. 이의 신청을 접수하고 양식을 이메일로 보내 드릴게요. 2주 안에 답변드려요.

title: Going Vegetarian
situation_ko: 채식을 시작하려는 친구와 장단점을 이야기해요.
ai_role: A friend who is thinking about becoming vegetarian

key_phrases.text: I think it can be healthy if it's balanced.
key_phrases.ko: 균형 잡히면 건강할 수 있다고 생각해요.

key_phrases.text: The main problem is getting enough protein.

questions.q: I'm thinking about becoming vegetarian. What do you think about that?
questions.q_ko: 채식을 해 볼까 생각 중이야. 어떻게 생각해?
questions.sample: I think it can be healthy if your meals are balanced.
questions.sample_ko: 식단이 균형 잡혀 있으면 건강할 수 있다고 생각해.

questions.q: That's reassuring. What do you think the biggest challenge would be?
questions.q_ko: 안심이 되네. 가장 어려운 점이 뭘 것 같아?
questions.sample: Probably getting enough protein, and eating out can be difficult in Korea.
questions.sample_ko: 단백질을 충분히 먹는 것과, 한국에서는 외식이 어려울 수 있다는 점 같아.

questions.q: True. Why do you think more people are choosing a vegetarian diet these days?
questions.q_ko: 맞아. 요즘 왜 더 많은 사람들이 채식을 선택한다고 생각해?
questions.sample: I think some do it for health and others care about animals and the environment.
questions.sample_ko: 건강 때문에 하는 사람도 있고 동물과 환경을 생각해서 하는 사람도 있는 것 같아.

questions.q: Do you think it's possible to start slowly instead of changing everything at once?
questions.q_ko: 한꺼번에 바꾸지 않고 천천히 시작하는 게 가능할까?
questions.sample: Yes, I think that's easier. You could start with one meatless day a week.
questions.sample_ko: 응, 그게 더 쉬울 것 같아. 일주일에 하루 고기 없는 날부터 시작해도 돼.

questions.q: Great idea. Would you try a meatless day with me?
questions.q_ko: 좋은 생각이야. 나랑 같이 고기 없는 날 해 볼래?
questions.sample: Sure, why not? It might be fun to try new recipes together.
questions.sample_ko: 좋아, 왜 안 되겠어? 같이 새로운 요리를 해 보면 재미있을 거야.

closing: Deal! I'll find a few easy recipes this weekend.
closing_ko: 좋아! 이번 주말에 쉬운 레시피를 몇 개 찾아 볼게.

title: Taking a Mental Health Day
situation_ko: 정신적으로 지쳐서 상사에게 하루 쉬고 싶다고 솔직하게 요청해요.
user_role: An employee asking for a mental health day

key_phrases.text: I think a day off would help me recover.
key_phrases.ko: 하루 쉬면 회복에 도움이 될 것 같아요.

key_phrases.text: I'll make sure my tasks are covered.

questions.q: You wanted to talk to me. What's on your mind?
questions.q_ko: 할 얘기가 있다고 했죠. 무슨 일이에요?
questions.sample: I've been feeling overwhelmed lately, and I'd like to take a day off to recharge.
questions.sample_ko: 요즘 압도당하는 기분이라서 재충전하려고 하루 쉬고 싶어요.

questions.q: Thank you for being honest. What has been the main cause?
questions.q_ko: 솔직하게 말해 줘서 고마워요. 가장 큰 원인이 뭐예요?
questions.sample: I think it's the combination of tight deadlines and personal worries at home.
questions.sample_ko: 빡빡한 마감과 집안의 개인적인 걱정이 겹쳐서인 것 같아요.

questions.q: I see. Do you think one day will be enough, or would you need more support?
questions.q_ko: 그렇군요. 하루면 충분할까요, 아니면 더 지원이 필요할까요?
questions.sample: I think one day will help, but I'd also like to talk about adjusting my workload.
questions.sample_ko: 하루면 도움이 될 것 같지만 업무량 조정에 대해서도 이야기하고 싶어요.

questions.q: That's reasonable. How can I best support you?
questions.sample: It would help if we could set clearer priorities so I don't feel everything is urgent.
questions.sample_ko: 모든 게 급하다고 느끼지 않게 우선순위를 더 분명히 정해 주시면 도움이 돼요.

questions.q: Good idea. Who will cover your urgent tasks while you're away?
questions.q_ko: 좋은 생각이에요. 쉬는 동안 급한 업무는 누가 맡을까요?
questions.sample: I'll finish the urgent ones today and ask Sam to cover the rest. I'll leave clear notes.
questions.sample_ko: 급한 건 오늘 끝내고 나머지는 샘에게 부탁할게요. 메모를 분명히 남길게요.

closing: Approved. Take tomorrow off, and let's talk about your workload when you're back.
closing_ko: 승인할게요. 내일 쉬고, 돌아오면 업무량에 대해 이야기해 봐요.

title: A Running Injury
situation_ko: 달리기를 하다 무릎이 아파서 스포츠 의학 의사와 원인과 대책을 이야기해요.

key_phrases.text: I increased my distance too quickly.
I don't want to stop running completely.
What's the best way to recover?

questions.q: Hi. What brings you in today?
questions.sample: I've had knee pain for two weeks since I started training for a ten-kilometer race.
questions.sample_ko: 10km 대회를 준비하며 훈련한 뒤로 2주째 무릎이 아파요.

questions.q: I see. Tell me about your training. How much were you running before?
questions.q_ko: 그렇군요. 훈련에 대해 말해 보세요. 전에는 얼마나 달렸어요?
questions.sample: Only about three kilometers twice a week, and then I jumped to eight kilometers in a few weeks.
questions.sample_ko: 일주일에 두 번 3km 정도만 달리다가 몇 주 만에 8km로 늘렸어요.

questions.q: That may be part of the problem. What kind of shoes do you wear?
questions.q_ko: 그게 원인 중 하나일 수 있어요. 어떤 신발을 신어요?
questions.sample: The same pair for three years. I think they're worn out.
questions.sample_ko: 3년째 같은 신발이에요. 많이 닳은 것 같아요.

questions.q: Probably. How important is running for you?
questions.q_ko: 아마 그럴 거예요. 달리기가 당신에게 얼마나 중요해요?
questions.sample: Very important. It helps with my stress, so I don't want to stop completely.
questions.sample_ko: 아주 중요해요. 스트레스를 풀어 줘서 완전히 멈추고 싶지 않아요.

questions.q: I understand. Would you be willing to cycle or swim for a few weeks while it heals?
questions.q_ko: 이해해요. 나을 동안 몇 주간 자전거나 수영으로 대신할 수 있겠어요?
questions.sample: Yes, if it helps me get back to running safely. What's the best way to recover?
questions.sample_ko: 네, 안전하게 달리기로 돌아갈 수 있다면요. 회복하는 가장 좋은 방법이 뭐예요?

closing: Rest, ice, and some gentle strength exercises should help. We'll build back slowly.
closing_ko: 휴식, 냉찜질, 가벼운 근력 운동이 도움이 될 거예요. 천천히 다시 늘려 가요.

title: Too Much Screen Time
situation_ko: 눈이 자주 피로해서 안과 의사와 화면 사용 습관에 대해 이야기해요.

key_phrases.text: My eyes feel dry and tired.
I spend most of the day looking at screens.
I probably should take more breaks.
key_phrases.ko: 휴식을 더 자주 가져야 할 것 같아요.

questions.q: What seems to be the problem?
questions.sample: My eyes feel dry and tired, especially in the evening, and I sometimes get headaches.
questions.sample_ko: 특히 저녁에 눈이 건조하고 피곤하고, 가끔 두통도 있어요.

questions.q: I see. How many hours a day do you look at screens?
questions.q_ko: 그렇군요. 하루에 몇 시간 화면을 보세요?
questions.sample: Probably ten hours or more, counting work and my phone.
questions.sample_ko: 일과 휴대폰을 합치면 아마 10시간 이상일 거예요.

questions.q: That's a lot. Do you take breaks during the day?
questions.sample: Not really. I get so focused that I forget, so I probably should take more breaks.
questions.sample_ko: 별로요. 집중하면 잊어버려서 휴식을 더 자주 가져야 할 것 같아요.

questions.q: Do you think technology has made our eyes worse in general?
questions.q_ko: 기술 때문에 전반적으로 눈이 더 나빠졌다고 생각해요?
questions.sample: I think so, since we look at close screens all day instead of far away. But it also makes life easier.
questions.sample_ko: 그런 것 같아요. 멀리 보지 않고 가까운 화면만 하루 종일 보니까요. 하지만 삶을 편하게 해 주기도 해요.

questions.q: True. What changes could you realistically make?
questions.q_ko: 맞아요. 현실적으로 어떤 변화를 줄 수 있을까요?
questions.sample: I could set a timer to look away every twenty minutes and cut my phone use at night.
questions.sample_ko: 20분마다 시선을 돌리도록 타이머를 맞추고 밤에는 휴대폰 사용을 줄일 수 있어요.

closing: Those are great steps. I'll also suggest some eye drops. Come back in a month.
closing_ko: 좋은 방법이에요. 인공눈물도 권해 드릴게요. 한 달 뒤에 다시 오세요.

title: Lost Passport Abroad
situation_ko: 해외여행 중 여권과 가방을 도난당해서 대사관 직원에게 도움을 청해요.
user_role: A traveler whose passport was stolen

key_phrases.text: My bag was stolen, and my passport was inside.
I have a flight in three days.
What documents do I need to bring?

questions.q: Hello. How can I help you?
questions.sample: My bag was stolen yesterday, and my passport was inside.
questions.sample_ko: 어제 가방을 도난당했는데 여권이 안에 있었어요.

questions.q: I'm very sorry. Did you report it to the police?
questions.sample: Yes, I filed a report this morning. I have a copy here.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 오늘 아침에 신고했어요. 사본이 여기 있어요.

questions.q: Good. Do you have a copy of your passport or any other photo ID?
questions.q_ko: 잘했어요. 여권 사본이나 다른 사진 신분증이 있으세요?
questions.sample: I have a photo of my passport on my phone, and my driver's license is at home in Korea.
questions.sample_ko: 휴대폰에 여권 사진이 있고, 운전면허증은 한국 집에 있어요.

questions.q: That will help. When do you need to travel?
questions.sample: I have a flight in three days, so it's quite urgent. Is that possible?
questions.sample_ko: 사흘 뒤에 비행기가 있어서 꽤 급해요. 가능할까요?

questions.q: We'll do our best to issue an emergency travel document. How are you managing otherwise, with your money and phone?
questions.q_ko: 긴급 여행 증명서를 최대한 빨리 발급해 드릴게요. 돈과 휴대폰 등 다른 건 어떻게 하고 계세요?
questions.sample: I canceled my cards, and a friend is helping me with some cash until I get new ones.
questions.sample_ko: 카드는 정지했고, 새 카드가 나올 때까지 친구가 현금을 도와주고 있어요.

closing: Please fill out this form and bring two photos tomorrow. We'll help you get home safely.
closing_ko: 이 양식을 작성하시고 내일 사진 두 장을 가져오세요. 안전하게 귀국하도록 도와드릴게요.

title: Fast Food and Health
situation_ko: 패스트푸드가 건강에 미치는 영향과 정책에 대해 동료와 의견을 나눠요.

key_phrases.text: In my opinion, it's fine in moderation.
The problem is that it's so cheap and convenient.
I agree up to a point.

questions.q: Let's talk about something different. Do you think fast food is really that bad for you?
questions.q_ko: 다른 이야기를 해 봐요. 패스트푸드가 정말 그렇게 나쁘다고 생각해요?
questions.sample: In my opinion, it's fine in moderation, but eating it every day is not healthy.
questions.sample_ko: 제 생각엔 적당히 먹으면 괜찮지만, 매일 먹는 건 건강하지 않아요.

questions.q: That's fair. Why do you think so many people eat it so often?
questions.q_ko: 공정한 말이에요. 왜 그렇게 많은 사람이 자주 먹는다고 생각해요?
questions.sample: The problem is that it's cheap, fast, and convenient, especially for busy people.
questions.sample_ko: 문제는 값싸고 빠르고 편하다는 거예요. 특히 바쁜 사람들에게는요.

questions.q: Good point. Some countries put extra taxes on sugary drinks. Do you think that's a good idea?
questions.q_ko: 좋은 지적이에요. 일부 나라는 단 음료에 세금을 더 매겨요. 좋은 생각일까요?
questions.sample: I agree up to a point. It might reduce sugar intake, but it could hurt people with low incomes.
questions.sample_ko: 어느 정도는 동의해요. 설탕 섭취를 줄일 수는 있지만 저소득층에게는 부담이 될 수 있어요.

questions.q: Interesting. What else could be done to help people eat better?
questions.q_ko: 흥미롭네요. 사람들이 더 잘 먹도록 또 무엇을 할 수 있을까요?
questions.sample: I think healthy options should be cheaper, and schools should teach kids about cooking and nutrition.
questions.sample_ko: 건강한 선택지가 더 저렴해야 하고, 학교에서 요리와 영양을 가르쳐야 한다고 생각해요.

questions.q: I like that. How do you personally try to balance it?
questions.q_ko: 좋은 생각이에요. 당신은 개인적으로 어떻게 균형을 맞추려고 해요?
questions.sample: I cook at home most days and allow myself fast food once a week as a treat.
questions.sample_ko: 저는 대부분 집에서 요리하고, 일주일에 한 번은 보상으로 패스트푸드를 먹어요.

closing: That's a sensible balance. Thanks for the great conversation!
closing_ko: 합리적인 균형이네요. 좋은 대화 고마워요!

title: Online or In-Person Doctor
situation_ko: 화상 진료와 직접 방문 진료 중 어느 쪽이 나은지 친구와 의견을 나눠요.
ai_role: A friend who just tried a video doctor visit

key_phrases.text: A doctor can't examine you properly online.
It depends on how serious it is.

questions.q: I just had my first video appointment with a doctor. Have you ever tried one?
questions.q_ko: 방금 처음으로 화상 진료를 받아 봤어. 너는 해 본 적 있어?
questions.sample: Yes, once, for a cold. It was convenient because I didn't have to leave home.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 한 번요. 감기 때문에요. 집을 나서지 않아도 돼서 편했어요.

questions.q: Same here. What do you think are the biggest advantages?
questions.q_ko: 나도 그래. 가장 큰 장점이 뭐라고 생각해?
questions.sample: It saves time and travel, and it's great for minor problems or follow-up visits.
questions.sample_ko: 시간과 이동이 절약되고, 가벼운 증상이나 재진에 아주 좋아요.

questions.q: True. And what about the disadvantages?
questions.sample: A doctor can't examine you properly online, so serious problems might be missed.
questions.sample_ko: 온라인으로는 제대로 진찰할 수 없어서 심각한 문제를 놓칠 수 있어요.

questions.q: Good point. Do you think online visits will replace in-person ones one day?
questions.q_ko: 좋은 지적이야. 언젠가 온라인 진료가 대면 진료를 대체할까?
questions.sample: I don't think so completely. It depends on how serious the problem is, but they'll probably become more common.
questions.sample_ko: 완전히 대체하지는 않을 것 같아요. 증상이 얼마나 심한지에 따라 다르겠지만 더 흔해질 거예요.

questions.q: Interesting. Would you feel comfortable discussing private health problems over video?
questions.q_ko: 흥미롭네. 화상으로 민감한 건강 문제를 이야기하는 게 편할까?
questions.sample: Maybe not at first, because I worry about privacy. But I could get used to it if the service is secure.
questions.sample_ko: 처음엔 아닐 수도 있어요. 개인정보가 걱정되니까요. 하지만 서비스가 안전하다면 익숙해질 수 있어요.

closing: Thanks for sharing your thoughts. I think I'll use it for small things and go in person for big ones.
closing_ko: 생각을 나눠 줘서 고마워. 작은 일엔 화상 진료를 쓰고 큰 일엔 직접 가야겠어.

title: Quitting Smoking
situation_ko: 담배를 끊고 싶어서 의사와 이유와 방법을 상담해요.
ai_role: A doctor who helps people quit smoking
user_role: A smoker who wants to quit

key_phrases.text: I've tried to quit before, but I failed.
I want to quit for my family's sake.

questions.q: I'm glad you came in. What made you decide to quit smoking?
questions.q_ko: 와 주셔서 기쁘네요. 담배를 끊기로 한 이유가 뭐예요?
questions.sample: My daughter asked me to stop, and I've started to feel short of breath when I climb stairs.
questions.sample_ko: 딸이 끊어 달라고 했고, 계단을 오를 때 숨이 차기 시작했어요.

questions.q: Those are strong reasons. Have you tried to quit before?
questions.q_ko: 강력한 이유네요. 전에도 끊어 본 적 있어요?
questions.sample: Yes, twice. I managed two weeks the last time, but I started again when work got stressful.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 두 번요. 지난번엔 2주를 버텼는데 일이 힘들어지자 다시 피웠어요.

questions.q: That's very common. What situations make you want a cigarette most?
questions.q_ko: 아주 흔한 일이에요. 어떤 상황에서 담배가 가장 생각나요?
questions.sample: Stress is my biggest trigger, and also after meals and when I drink coffee.
questions.sample_ko: 스트레스가 가장 큰 계기예요. 식사 후나 커피를 마실 때도 생각나요.

questions.q: Good to know. What do you think could replace the habit in those moments?
questions.q_ko: 알아 두면 좋겠네요. 그런 순간에 이 습관을 무엇으로 대신할 수 있을까요?
questions.sample: Maybe chewing gum or going for a short walk. Exercise might help with the stress too.
questions.sample_ko: 껌을 씹거나 짧게 산책하는 게 좋겠어요. 운동도 스트레스에 도움이 될 거예요.

questions.q: Great ideas. Who could support you along the way?
questions.q_ko: 좋은 생각이에요. 과정에서 누가 도와줄 수 있을까요?
questions.sample: My wife and daughter would support me, and I could tell a few friends at work too.
questions.sample_ko: 아내와 딸이 응원해 줄 거고, 직장 친구 몇 명에게도 말할 수 있어요.

closing: You have good reasons and good support. Let's set a quit date and make a plan together.
closing_ko: 좋은 이유와 든든한 지지가 있어요. 금연 날짜를 정하고 함께 계획을 세워 봐요.

title: Caring for a Sick Parent
situation_ko: 몸이 불편해진 부모님을 어떻게 돌볼지 형제와 의논해요.

key_phrases.text: I think we should share the responsibility.
I'm worried about her being alone.

questions.q: Mom's knee is getting worse, and she's having trouble with stairs. How do you think she's doing?
questions.q_ko: 엄마 무릎이 더 안 좋아져서 계단 오르기가 힘드시대. 엄마가 어떻게 지내시는 것 같아?
questions.sample: I'm worried. She says she's fine, but I think she's hiding how much pain she's in.
questions.sample_ko: 걱정돼요. 괜찮다고 하시지만 얼마나 아픈지 숨기시는 것 같아요.

questions.q: I feel the same. What do you think we should do first?
questions.q_ko: 나도 그래. 먼저 뭘 해야 할 것 같아?
questions.sample: First, we should take her to a specialist and find out what treatment she really needs.
questions.sample_ko: 먼저 전문의에게 모시고 가서 어떤 치료가 정말 필요한지 알아봐야 해요.

questions.q: Good idea. She lives alone, so who will help her afterwards?
questions.q_ko: 좋은 생각이야. 혼자 사시니까, 그 후엔 누가 도와줄까?
questions.sample: I think we should share the responsibility. I can visit on weekends, and you could call every day.
questions.sample_ko: 책임을 나눠야 한다고 생각해요. 저는 주말마다 찾아뵙고, 언니가 매일 전화하면 어때요.

questions.q: That sounds fair. Do you think we should hire a caregiver?
questions.sample: Maybe for a few hours a day. It might be better than having her do everything alone.
questions.sample_ko: 하루 몇 시간만이라도요. 혼자 다 하시는 것보다 나을 거예요.

questions.q: What do you think she'd say about that?
questions.q_ko: 엄마는 그 얘기에 뭐라고 하실 것 같아?
questions.sample: She'd probably say no at first because she doesn't want to be a burden. We need to explain it gently.
questions.sample_ko: 처음엔 짐이 되기 싫다며 거절하실 거예요. 부드럽게 설명해 드려야 해요.

closing: Thanks for working this out with me. I feel better knowing we're a team.
closing_ko: 같이 의논해 줘서 고마워. 우리가 한 팀이라고 생각하니 마음이 놓여.

title: Gym or Outdoor Exercise
situation_ko: 운동할 때 헬스장과 야외 중 어느 쪽이 좋은지 친구와 이야기해요.
ai_role: A friend who loves outdoor sports
user_role: A friend who prefers indoor workouts

key_phrases.text: Personally, I prefer working out indoors.
The weather doesn't affect my routine.
key_phrases.ko: 날씨가 운동 일정에 영향을 안 줘요.

key_phrases.text: On the other hand, fresh air is great.

questions.q: I run in the park every morning, but my friends say the gym is better. Where do you like to exercise?
questions.q_ko: 난 매일 아침 공원에서 뛰는데 친구들은 헬스장이 낫대. 넌 어디서 운동하는 걸 좋아해?
questions.sample: Personally, I prefer the gym because the weather doesn't affect my routine.
questions.sample_ko: 개인적으로는 헬스장이 좋아. 날씨가 운동 일정에 영향을 안 주거든.

questions.q: That makes sense. What do you like most about working out indoors?
questions.q_ko: 일리 있네. 실내 운동의 어떤 점이 가장 좋아?
questions.sample: I like having all the machines and being able to track my progress. It also feels safer at night.
questions.sample_ko: 기구가 다 있고 진척을 기록할 수 있는 게 좋아. 밤에도 더 안전하게 느껴지고.

questions.q: I see. But don't you get bored being inside?
questions.q_ko: 그렇구나. 그래도 실내에 있으면 지루하지 않아?
questions.sample: Sometimes. On the other hand, I listen to podcasts, which makes it enjoyable.
questions.sample_ko: 가끔은 그래. 그래도 팟캐스트를 들으면서 하니까 재미있어.

questions.q: Nice trick. Do you think outdoor exercise has any benefits the gym doesn't?
questions.q_ko: 좋은 방법이네. 야외 운동에만 있는 장점이 있다고 생각해?
questions.sample: Yes, fresh air and sunlight are great for your mood, and it's free.
questions.sample_ko: 응, 맑은 공기와 햇빛은 기분에 아주 좋고 무료이기도 해.

questions.q: Exactly. Should we try mixing it up, like the gym on weekdays and hiking on weekends?
questions.q_ko: 맞아. 평일엔 헬스장, 주말엔 등산처럼 섞어서 해 볼까?
questions.sample: That sounds like a great plan. I'd enjoy the variety.
questions.sample_ko: 좋은 계획 같아. 변화가 있어서 즐거울 거야.

closing: Perfect. This Saturday, let's hike up the mountain and see how it feels!
closing_ko: 좋아. 이번 토요일에 산에 올라가서 어떤지 보자!

title: Calling Emergency Services
situation_ko: 길에서 사람이 쓰러지는 것을 보고 119에 전화해 상황을 설명해요.

key_phrases.text: A man collapsed on the street.
He's breathing, but he isn't responding.
I'll stay with him until help arrives.

questions.q: Emergency services. What's your emergency?
questions.sample: A man just collapsed on the street, and he isn't responding.
questions.sample_ko: 한 남자가 방금 길에서 쓰러졌는데 반응이 없어요.

questions.q: Stay calm. Where are you exactly?
questions.sample: I'm in front of the Green Cafe on Station Road, next to the bus stop.
questions.sample_ko: 역 앞길의 그린 카페 앞, 버스 정류장 옆이에요.

questions.q: Thank you. Is he breathing?
questions.sample: Yes, he's breathing, but very slowly, and his face is pale.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 숨은 쉬는데 아주 느리고 얼굴이 창백해요.

questions.q: Okay. Can you tell me what happened right before he collapsed?
questions.q_ko: 알겠어요. 쓰러지기 직전에 어떤 일이 있었는지 말해 주시겠어요?
questions.sample: He was walking and said he felt dizzy, and then he fell. He didn't hit his head hard, I think.
questions.sample_ko: 걷다가 어지럽다고 하더니 쓰러졌어요. 머리를 세게 부딪치진 않은 것 같아요.

questions.q: Good. Is anyone else there who can help you?
questions.q_ko: 좋아요. 도와줄 다른 사람이 근처에 있나요?
questions.sample: Yes, two people are here. One of them is waving down the ambulance for us.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 두 명이 있어요. 한 분이 구급차를 향해 손을 흔들고 있어요.

closing: Help is on the way. Please stay on the line and stay with him until the ambulance arrives.
closing_ko: 구급차가 가고 있어요. 전화를 끊지 말고 구급차가 올 때까지 그분 곁에 계세요.

title: Getting to Know Your New Neighbor
situation_ko: 옆집에 새로 이사 온 이웃을 복도에서 처음 만났어요.

key_phrases.text: Let me know if you need help.

questions.q: Hi! I just moved in. What's your name?
questions.q_ko: 안녕하세요! 저 방금 이사 왔어요. 이름이 뭐예요?
questions.sample: Hi, I'm Minho. Nice to meet you.

questions.q: Nice to meet you! Which apartment do you live in?
questions.sample: I live in apartment 302, next to you.

questions.q: Oh, great! How long have you lived here?
questions.q_ko: 아, 좋네요! 여기 얼마나 오래 사셨어요?
questions.sample: I have lived here for three years.

questions.q: Is this a good neighborhood?
questions.sample: Yes, it is quiet and safe.

questions.q: Is there a good supermarket near here?
questions.sample: Yes, there is one near the bus stop.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 버스 정류장 근처에 하나 있어요.

closing: Thank you so much! It was nice talking to you. See you around!
closing_ko: 정말 고마워요! 이야기 즐거웠어요. 또 봬요!

title: Introducing Yourself
situation_ko: 모임에서 처음 만난 사람에게 자기소개를 해요.
ai_role: A friendly person at a small meetup
user_role: A new member of the group

questions.q: Hello! Where are you from?
questions.sample: I'm from Korea. I'm from Busan.

questions.q: Oh nice! What do you do?
questions.sample: I work in an office. I'm an accountant.

questions.q: Do you like your job?
questions.sample: Yes, I like it. My team is nice.

questions.q: What do you do in your free time?
questions.sample: I like walking and watching movies.
questions.sample_ko: 걷는 것과 영화 보는 걸 좋아해요.

questions.q: Why did you join this group?
questions.sample: I want to make new friends.

closing: That's great! I'm happy you joined us. Welcome to the group!
closing_ko: 좋네요! 함께하게 되어 기뻐요. 모임에 온 걸 환영해요!

title: A New Friend in Class
situation_ko: 영어 수업에서 옆자리 친구와 처음 이야기해요.
ai_role: A classmate sitting next to the learner
user_role: A student in an English class

key_phrases.text: I want to speak better English.

questions.q: Hi, I'm new here. Is this your first class?
questions.q_ko: 안녕하세요, 저 여기 처음이에요. 이번이 첫 수업이에요?
questions.sample: No, I started last week.

questions.q: Oh, I see! Why are you learning English?
questions.sample: I want to travel and speak with people.

questions.q: That's a good reason! Is English difficult for you?
questions.sample: Speaking is difficult, but I like it.

questions.q: How often do you study English?
questions.sample: I study every day for thirty minutes.

questions.q: Do you want to practice together after class?
questions.sample: Yes, that sounds great!

closing: Awesome! Let's practice together. See you after class!
closing_ko: 좋아요! 같이 연습해요. 수업 끝나고 봐요!

title: Talking About Your Family
situation_ko: 새 친구가 당신의 가족에 대해 물어봐요.
user_role: A person talking about their family

questions.q: Tell me about your family. How many people are in your family?
questions.q_ko: 가족 이야기를 해 주세요. 가족이 몇 명이에요?
questions.sample: There are four people. My parents, my brother, and me.
questions.sample_ko: 네 명이에요. 부모님, 남동생, 그리고 저예요.

questions.q: Nice! Do you live with your family?
questions.sample: No, I live alone, but my family lives nearby.
questions.sample_ko: 아니요, 혼자 살지만 가족은 근처에 살아요.

questions.q: I see. What does your mother do?
questions.sample: She is a nurse. She works at a hospital.

questions.q: Who are you closest to in your family?
questions.sample: I am closest to my brother.

questions.q: What do you do together on weekends?
questions.sample: We eat dinner and watch TV.

closing: You have a lovely family. Thanks for sharing!
closing_ko: 멋진 가족이네요. 이야기해 줘서 고마워요!

title: Asking About Hobbies
situation_ko: 새로 알게 된 친구와 서로의 취미를 이야기해요.
ai_role: A new friend who loves hobbies

key_phrases.text: I'm not very good, but it's fun.

questions.q: What's your hobby?
questions.sample: I like cooking and hiking.

questions.q: Cool! When do you do it?
questions.sample: I do it on weekends.

questions.q: Do you do it alone or with friends?
questions.sample: I usually do it with my friend.

questions.q: How did you start this hobby?
questions.sample: My father taught me when I was young.

questions.q: Is there a new hobby you want to try?
questions.q_ko: 새로 해 보고 싶은 취미가 있어요?
questions.sample: I want to try swimming.

closing: That sounds fun! Maybe we can try something together someday.
closing_ko: 재미있겠어요! 언젠가 같이 뭔가 해 봐요.

title: Inviting a Friend for Coffee
situation_ko: 친구가 커피 한잔하자고 제안해요.
ai_role: A friend who wants to have coffee

questions.q: Hi! Do you want to get coffee with me?
questions.sample: Sure, I'd love to!

questions.q: Great! Which day is good for you?
questions.sample: How about Saturday?

questions.q: Saturday works! What time should we meet?
questions.sample: Let's meet at 3 o'clock.

questions.q: Where should we go?
questions.sample: There is a nice cafe near the station.

questions.q: What do you usually drink?
questions.sample: I usually drink an iced americano.

closing: Perfect! I can't wait. See you on Saturday!
closing_ko: 완벽해! 너무 기대돼. 토요일에 봐!

title: Saying Sorry
situation_ko: 약속에 늦어서 친구에게 미안하다고 말해요.
ai_role: A friend who waited for the learner

questions.q: Hey! I've been waiting for twenty minutes. What happened?
questions.sample: I'm so sorry. The bus was late.

questions.q: Oh, I see. Did you call me?
questions.sample: No, my phone battery was dead.

questions.q: That's too bad. Are you okay now?
questions.sample: Yes, I'm okay. Thank you.

questions.q: How can you make it up to me?
questions.sample: I'll buy you a coffee.

questions.q: Will you come early next time?
questions.sample: Yes, I will. It won't happen again.

closing: Okay, no problem! Let's go and enjoy our day.
closing_ko: 좋아, 괜찮아! 가서 즐거운 하루 보내자.

title: Congratulating a Friend
situation_ko: 친구가 시험에 합격했다는 좋은 소식을 전해요.
ai_role: A happy friend with good news

questions.q: Guess what! I passed my driving test!
questions.sample: Congratulations! I'm so happy for you!

questions.q: Thank you! I was so nervous. Did you ever take a test like that?
questions.q_ko: 고마워! 너무 긴장했어. 너도 그런 시험 본 적 있어?
questions.sample: Yes, I took one two years ago.

questions.q: Was it hard for you?
questions.sample: Yes, I failed the first time.

questions.q: Oh really? What did you do next?
questions.sample: I practiced more and passed.

questions.q: Do you want to celebrate with me tonight?
questions.sample: Yes! Let's have dinner.

closing: Yay! Thank you for being such a good friend. Dinner is on me!
closing_ko: 야호! 좋은 친구가 되어 줘서 고마워. 저녁은 내가 살게!

title: Chatting About Weekend Plans
situation_ko: 금요일에 친구가 주말에 뭐 하는지 물어봐요.

key_phrases.text: I'm going to visit my parents.

questions.q: It's Friday! What are you going to do this weekend?
questions.q_ko: 금요일이다! 이번 주말에 뭐 할 거야?
questions.sample: I'm going to visit my parents.

questions.q: That's nice! How will you get there?
questions.sample: I will take the train.

questions.q: How long is the trip?
questions.sample: It takes about two hours.

questions.q: What will you do there?
questions.sample: I will eat my mom's food and rest.

questions.q: Will you come back on Sunday?
questions.sample: Yes, I will come back Sunday night.

closing: Sounds lovely! Have a great weekend and safe travels.
closing_ko: 좋겠다! 즐거운 주말 보내고 조심히 다녀와.

title: Talking About Your Pet
situation_ko: 공원에서 만난 사람과 반려동물 이야기를 해요.
ai_role: A dog owner at the park
user_role: A pet owner or animal lover

questions.q: Hi! Do you have any pets?
questions.sample: Yes, I have a cat.

questions.q: Aww! What's her name?
questions.sample: Her name is Nabi.

questions.q: Cute name! How old is she?
questions.sample: She is two years old.

questions.q: What does she like to do?
questions.sample: She likes to sleep and play with a ball.
questions.sample_ko: 자는 걸 좋아하고 공 가지고 놀아요.

questions.q: Do you want another pet in the future?
questions.sample: Maybe a dog. I love dogs too.

closing: How lovely! Pets make life happy. Nice talking to you!
closing_ko: 정말 좋네요! 반려동물은 삶을 행복하게 해 주죠. 이야기 즐거웠어요!

title: Favorite Food Chat
situation_ko: 새 친구와 좋아하는 음식에 대해 이야기해요.

questions.q: What's your favorite food?
questions.sample: My favorite food is pizza.

questions.q: Yum! How often do you eat it?
questions.sample: I eat it once a week.

questions.q: Do you like spicy food?
questions.sample: Yes, I love spicy food.

questions.q: Do you cook at home?
questions.sample: Sometimes. I can make pasta.

questions.q: Is there a food you really don't like?
questions.sample: I don't like mushrooms.

closing: Now I'm hungry! Let's eat together sometime.
closing_ko: 이제 배고파졌어요! 언제 같이 먹어요.

title: Birthday Party Small Talk
situation_ko: 친구의 생일 파티에서 처음 보는 사람과 이야기해요.
ai_role: A guest at a birthday party

questions.q: Hi! I don't think we've met. How do you know the birthday girl?
questions.q_ko: 안녕하세요! 처음 뵙는 것 같은데요. 생일 맞은 친구를 어떻게 알아요?
questions.sample: We are old friends from school.

questions.q: That's nice! How long have you been friends?
questions.q_ko: 좋네요! 친구 된 지 얼마나 됐어요?
questions.sample: For about ten years.

questions.q: Wow, a long time! Did you bring a gift?
questions.sample: Yes, I brought flowers.

questions.q: Nice choice! Do you like the party?
questions.sample: Yes, the food is delicious.

questions.q: When is your birthday?
questions.sample: My birthday is in October.

closing: How fun! I'm glad I met you today. Enjoy the party!
closing_ko: 재미있네요! 오늘 만나서 반가웠어요. 파티 즐기세요!

title: Weather Small Talk
situation_ko: 버스 정류장에서 옆 사람과 날씨 이야기를 해요.
ai_role: A stranger at a bus stop
user_role: A person waiting for the bus

questions.q: Hello! How is the weather today for you?
questions.sample: It's very cold today.

questions.q: I agree! What's your favorite season?
questions.sample: I like spring. It is warm and pretty.

questions.q: Spring is lovely. What do you like to do in spring?
questions.q_ko: 봄은 좋죠. 봄에 뭘 하는 걸 좋아해요?
questions.sample: I like walking in the park.

questions.q: What do you do on rainy days?
questions.sample: I stay home and drink tea.

questions.q: Is your bus late too?
questions.sample: Yes, it is five minutes late.

closing: Oh, here comes my bus! Nice chatting with you. Stay warm!
closing_ko: 아, 제 버스가 오네요! 이야기 즐거웠어요. 따뜻하게 지내세요!

title: Talking About Your Hometown
situation_ko: 외국인 친구가 당신의 고향에 대해 궁금해해요.
user_role: A local telling about their hometown

questions.q: Where is your hometown?
questions.sample: I'm from Jeju. It's an island.

questions.q: Wow! What is it famous for?
questions.sample: It's famous for the sea and tangerines.

questions.q: Sounds beautiful! Is it a big place?
questions.sample: No, it's small, but very pretty.

questions.q: What food should I try there?
questions.q_ko: 거기서 어떤 음식을 먹어 봐야 해요?
questions.sample: You should try black pork and fish soup.

questions.q: Do you miss your hometown?
questions.sample: Yes, I miss my family and the sea.

closing: I really want to visit now. Thank you for telling me!
closing_ko: 이제 정말 가 보고 싶어요. 이야기해 줘서 고마워요!

title: Lunch With a Coworker
situation_ko: 직장 동료와 점심을 먹으면서 가벼운 이야기를 나눠요.

key_phrases.text: What do you want to eat?
I live far from the office.

questions.q: It's lunchtime! What do you want to eat?
questions.sample: I want to eat noodles.

questions.q: Good idea! How was your morning?
questions.sample: It was busy. I'm a little tired.

questions.q: Me too. How do you come to work?
questions.sample: I take the subway.

questions.q: How long does it take?
questions.sample: It takes about forty minutes.

questions.q: What do you do after work?
questions.sample: I go home and cook dinner.

closing: Thanks for having lunch with me. Let's do it again soon!
closing_ko: 점심 같이 해 줘서 고마워요. 곧 또 해요!

title: Party Small Talk
situation_ko: 친구 집들이에서 모르는 사람과 가벼운 대화를 시작해요.
ai_role: A guest at a housewarming party

key_phrases.text: How do you know the host?

questions.q: Hi there! Great party, isn't it? How do you know the host?
questions.q_ko: 안녕하세요! 파티 좋죠? 집주인은 어떻게 아세요?
questions.sample: We used to work together at the same company.

questions.q: Oh, nice! What do you do now?
questions.q_ko: 아, 그렇군요! 지금은 무슨 일 하세요?
questions.sample: I work in marketing for a small company.

questions.q: That sounds interesting! What do you enjoy most about it?
questions.sample: I like creating new ideas with my team.
questions.sample_ko: 팀과 새로운 아이디어를 만드는 게 좋아요.

questions.q: Have you tried the food yet? What do you recommend?
questions.sample: The pasta is really good. You should try it.

questions.q: Do you go to many parties like this?
questions.sample: Not really. I prefer small gatherings with friends.
questions.sample_ko: 별로요. 친구들과 작게 모이는 걸 더 좋아해요.

closing: It was great meeting you! I'm going to grab some food. Enjoy the rest of the night!
closing_ko: 만나서 정말 반가웠어요! 저는 음식 좀 가져올게요. 남은 밤 즐겁게 보내세요!

title: Catching Up With an Old Friend
situation_ko: 몇 년 만에 우연히 만난 옛 친구와 근황을 이야기해요.

key_phrases.text: What have you been up to?

questions.q: Oh my gosh, is that you? It's been so long! How have you been?
questions.q_ko: 세상에, 너 맞아? 정말 오랜만이다! 어떻게 지냈어?
questions.sample: I've been good! A lot has changed since school.
questions.sample_ko: 잘 지냈어! 학교 때 이후로 많은 게 바뀌었어.

questions.q: I can imagine! What are you doing these days?
questions.sample: I work at a design company, and I moved to Seoul.

questions.q: Wow, that's great! Do you like living in the city?
questions.q_ko: 와, 멋지다! 도시 생활은 마음에 들어?
questions.sample: I like it, but it's very busy and expensive.

questions.q: Are you still in touch with anyone from our class?
questions.q_ko: 우리 반 친구들 중에 아직 연락하는 사람 있어?
questions.sample: Yes, I talk to Jina sometimes. We meet once or twice a year.
questions.sample_ko: 응, 가끔 지나랑 얘기해. 1년에 한두 번 만나.

questions.q: We should meet up properly. When are you free?
questions.q_ko: 우리 제대로 한번 만나자. 언제 시간 돼?
questions.sample: I'm free next Saturday afternoon. Does that work for you?
questions.sample_ko: 다음 토요일 오후에 시간 돼. 너 괜찮아?

closing: Perfect, it's a plan! I'm so happy we ran into each other.
closing_ko: 좋아, 약속했다! 우연히 만나서 너무 기뻐.

title: Language Exchange Partner
situation_ko: 영어를 배우고 싶어 하는 사람과 언어 교환 첫 만남을 가져요.
ai_role: An English speaker who wants to learn Korean

key_phrases.text: How do you say this in English?

questions.q: Hi, nice to meet you! Why did you decide to join a language exchange?
questions.q_ko: 안녕하세요, 만나서 반가워요! 왜 언어 교환을 하기로 했어요?
questions.sample: I'd like to practice speaking English with a real person.
questions.sample_ko: 진짜 사람과 영어 말하기를 연습하고 싶어서요.

questions.q: That makes sense! How long have you been studying English?
questions.q_ko: 그렇군요! 영어 공부한 지 얼마나 됐어요?
questions.sample: About three years, but I still feel nervous when I speak.

questions.q: Don't worry, that's normal. What's the hardest part for you?
questions.q_ko: 걱정 마세요, 보통 그래요. 가장 어려운 부분이 뭐예요?
questions.sample: Listening is hard because people speak very fast.
questions.sample_ko: 사람들이 너무 빨리 말해서 듣기가 어려워요.

questions.q: I'll speak slowly, I promise. What kind of topics do you like to talk about?
questions.q_ko: 천천히 말할게요, 약속해요. 어떤 주제로 이야기하는 걸 좋아해요?
questions.sample: I like talking about movies, food, and travel.

questions.q: Great! How about we spend half the time in English and half in Korean?
questions.q_ko: 좋아요! 절반은 영어, 절반은 한국어로 하면 어때요?
questions.sample: That sounds perfect. Can we meet every week?

closing: Wonderful! I think we'll learn a lot from each other. See you next week!
closing_ko: 멋져요! 서로에게서 많이 배울 것 같아요. 다음 주에 봐요!

title: Dating App First Chat
situation_ko: 데이팅 앱에서 매칭된 사람과 처음 메시지를 주고받아요.
ai_role: A friendly person you matched with on a dating app

key_phrases.text: I saw that you like hiking.
Would you like to meet for coffee?

questions.q: Hi! Thanks for matching with me. How's your day going?
questions.q_ko: 안녕하세요! 매칭해 줘서 고마워요. 오늘 하루 어때요?
questions.sample: It's going well, thanks! I just finished work.
questions.sample_ko: 잘 지내고 있어요, 고마워요! 방금 퇴근했어요.

questions.q: Nice! So tell me a little about yourself. What are you into?
questions.q_ko: 좋네요! 자기소개 좀 해 주세요. 뭘 좋아하세요?
questions.sample: I'm into movies and cooking. I also like short trips.
questions.sample_ko: 영화와 요리를 좋아해요. 짧은 여행도 좋아하고요.

questions.q: Cooking is great! What's the best dish you can make?
questions.q_ko: 요리 좋네요! 제일 잘 만드는 요리가 뭐예요?
questions.sample: I make a really good kimchi stew. My friends love it.

questions.q: Yum! What do you usually do on weekends?
questions.sample: I usually meet friends or watch movies at home.
questions.sample_ko: 보통 친구를 만나거나 집에서 영화를 봐요.

questions.q: We have a lot in common. Would you like to meet for coffee sometime?
questions.sample: I'd love to. How about this Sunday afternoon?

closing: Sunday sounds great! I'll send you the details soon. Talk later!
closing_ko: 일요일 좋아요! 곧 자세한 내용 보낼게요. 나중에 얘기해요!

title: Inviting Someone to Dinner
situation_ko: 친구를 집으로 저녁 식사에 초대하고 준비를 의논해요.
ai_role: A friend you are inviting to dinner

key_phrases.text: I'd like to invite you to dinner.
Do you have any food allergies?

questions.q: Hey! What's up? You said you wanted to ask me something.
questions.q_ko: 안녕! 무슨 일이야? 뭐 물어보고 싶다고 했잖아.
questions.sample: Yes! I'd like to invite you to dinner at my place this Friday.
questions.sample_ko: 응! 이번 금요일에 우리 집에서 저녁 먹자고 초대하고 싶어.

questions.q: Oh, that sounds lovely! What are you going to cook?
questions.sample: I'm thinking of making pasta and a salad. Is that okay?

questions.q: Perfect! Should I bring anything?
questions.sample: Just bring yourself. Maybe a dessert if you want.

questions.q: Sure! Is there anything I shouldn't eat? I mean, do you want to know about my food allergies?
questions.q_ko: 좋아! 내가 못 먹는 건 없냐고? 아, 내 알레르기 같은 거 알고 싶어?
questions.sample: Yes, please tell me. I want to make food you can enjoy.
questions.sample_ko: 응, 알려 줘. 네가 맛있게 먹을 수 있는 걸 만들고 싶어.

questions.q: I'm allergic to shrimp, that's all. What time should I come?
questions.q_ko: 난 새우 알레르기만 있어. 몇 시에 가면 돼?
questions.sample: Come at seven. Dinner will be ready by seven thirty.

closing: Great, no shrimp, got it! I can't wait. See you Friday!
closing_ko: 좋아, 새우는 빼는 거 알았어! 정말 기대돼. 금요일에 봐!

title: Apologizing for Being Late
situation_ko: 중요한 모임에 한 시간 늦게 도착해서 친구에게 사과해요.
ai_role: A friend who has been waiting a long time

key_phrases.text: I'm really sorry for keeping you waiting.
Let me make it up to you.

questions.q: There you are! It's been an hour. What happened?
questions.q_ko: 드디어 왔네! 한 시간이나 됐어. 무슨 일이야?
questions.sample: I'm really sorry for keeping you waiting. I got stuck in traffic.
questions.sample_ko: 기다리게 해서 정말 미안해. 차가 막혔어.

questions.q: Why didn't you let me know earlier?
questions.sample: My phone died, and I didn't have a charger.

questions.q: Hmm, I was a little worried. Did you take a different route?
questions.q_ko: 음, 좀 걱정했어. 다른 길로 왔어?
questions.sample: No, I should have. I'll leave earlier next time.
questions.sample_ko: 아니, 그랬어야 했는데. 다음엔 더 일찍 나올게.

questions.q: Okay, I understand. How can you make it up to me?
questions.sample: Let me buy you lunch and dessert today.

questions.q: Deal! Are you hungry right now?
questions.sample: Yes, very. I skipped breakfast this morning.

closing: All is forgiven! Let's go eat. I know a great place nearby.
closing_ko: 다 용서할게! 가서 먹자. 근처에 좋은 곳 알아.

title: Advice About a Job Change
situation_ko: 직장을 옮길지 고민하는 친구에게 조언을 해 줘요.
ai_role: A friend thinking about changing jobs

key_phrases.ko: 가장 중요한 게 뭔지 생각해 보세요.

questions.q: I need your advice. I got a job offer, but I'm not sure if I should leave my current job. What do you think?
questions.q_ko: 조언이 필요해. 일자리 제안을 받았는데 지금 직장을 떠나야 할지 모르겠어. 어떻게 생각해?
questions.sample: What's good about the new job? I think you should list the pros and cons.
questions.sample_ko: 새 직장의 어떤 점이 좋은데? 장단점을 적어 보는 게 좋을 것 같아.

questions.q: The salary is higher, but the commute is longer. Is that a problem?
questions.q_ko: 월급은 더 높은데 출퇴근이 더 길어. 문제일까?
questions.sample: A long commute can be tiring. How much longer is it?
questions.sample_ko: 긴 출퇴근은 힘들 수 있어. 얼마나 더 길어?

questions.q: About one hour each way. But I would learn a lot there.
questions.q_ko: 편도 한 시간쯤이야. 근데 거기서 많이 배울 수 있어.
questions.sample: Learning is important. Maybe you could work from home sometimes?
questions.sample_ko: 배우는 건 중요하지. 가끔 재택근무가 가능할지도 몰라.

questions.q: Good point. Why don't I ask them? Do you think I'm ready for a bigger role?
questions.q_ko: 좋은 지적이야. 한번 물어볼까? 내가 더 큰 역할을 할 준비가 됐다고 생각해?
questions.sample: Yes, you work hard and learn fast. I believe you can do it.
questions.sample_ko: 응, 넌 열심히 하고 빨리 배워. 할 수 있다고 믿어.

questions.q: Thanks. If you were me, when would you decide?
questions.q_ko: 고마워. 네가 나라면 언제 결정할 거야?
questions.sample: I'd decide after asking about the schedule, maybe by next week.
questions.sample_ko: 일정을 물어본 뒤에, 아마 다음 주까지 결정할 거야.

closing: You've really helped me think clearly. Thank you, you're a great friend!
closing_ko: 덕분에 생각이 정리됐어. 고마워, 넌 정말 좋은 친구야!

title: Comforting a Sad Friend
situation_ko: 시험에 떨어져서 속상해하는 친구를 위로해요.
ai_role: A friend who failed an important exam

key_phrases.text: It's not the end of the world.

questions.q: I failed the exam. I studied for months, and I feel terrible.
questions.q_ko: 시험에 떨어졌어. 몇 달을 공부했는데 기분이 너무 안 좋아.
questions.sample: I'm so sorry. I'm here for you. You did your best.
questions.sample_ko: 정말 속상하겠다. 내가 곁에 있을게. 넌 최선을 다했어.

questions.q: Thanks. I just feel like a failure. Everyone else passed.
questions.q_ko: 고마워. 그냥 내가 실패자 같아. 다른 사람들은 다 붙었어.
questions.sample: That's not true. It's not the end of the world. You can try again.
questions.sample_ko: 그렇지 않아. 세상이 끝난 게 아니야. 다시 도전할 수 있어.

questions.q: Do you really think I can pass next time?
questions.q_ko: 정말 다음엔 붙을 수 있다고 생각해?
questions.sample: Yes, I do. You are smart and you never give up.
questions.sample_ko: 응, 그렇게 생각해. 넌 똑똑하고 포기하지 않잖아.

questions.q: I don't know what to do right now. Any ideas?
questions.q_ko: 지금 뭘 해야 할지 모르겠어. 좋은 생각 있어?
questions.sample: Let's take a walk and get something to eat. You need a break.
questions.sample_ko: 산책하고 뭐 좀 먹자. 넌 쉬어야 해.

questions.q: That actually sounds nice. Can you stay with me tonight?
questions.q_ko: 그거 좋겠다. 오늘 밤 같이 있어 줄래?
questions.sample: Of course. I'll stay as long as you want.

closing: Thank you. I already feel a bit better just talking to you.
closing_ko: 고마워. 너랑 얘기하는 것만으로도 벌써 조금 나아졌어.

title: Culture Differences Chat
situation_ko: 해외에서 온 친구와 서로의 문화 차이에 대해 이야기해요.

questions.q: I've noticed some interesting things in Korea. For example, people take off their shoes at home. Is that common?
questions.q_ko: 한국에서 흥미로운 걸 발견했어요. 예를 들어 집에서 신발을 벗잖아요. 흔한 일이에요?
questions.sample: Yes, in Korea we always take off our shoes at home. It keeps the floor clean.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 한국에서는 집에서 항상 신발을 벗어요. 바닥을 깨끗하게 유지하려고요.

questions.q: I see! Also, people here use both hands when giving something to older people. Why is that?
questions.q_ko: 그렇군요! 또 여기 사람들은 어른께 뭔가 드릴 때 두 손을 쓰던데요. 왜 그래요?
questions.sample: It's a way to show respect. Respect for elders is important here.
questions.sample_ko: 존경을 표하는 방법이에요. 여기서는 어른 공경이 중요해요.

questions.q: That's lovely. Is there anything you find different when you travel abroad?
questions.q_ko: 멋지네요. 외국에 여행 가면 다르다고 느끼는 게 있어요?
questions.sample: I was surprised that people talk to strangers easily in other countries.
questions.sample_ko: 다른 나라에서는 낯선 사람과 쉽게 이야기해서 놀랐어요.

questions.q: Yes, that's common in my country. Do you think Koreans are shy?
questions.q_ko: 네, 우리나라에선 흔해요. 한국 사람들이 수줍음이 많다고 생각해요?
questions.sample: Maybe a little, but once we become friends, we are very warm.

questions.q: I've felt that already! What's one custom from my country you'd like to try?
questions.q_ko: 이미 느꼈어요! 우리나라 풍습 중에 해 보고 싶은 게 있어요?
questions.sample: I'd like to try your holiday dinner. I love learning about new food.
questions.sample_ko: 명절 저녁 식사를 해 보고 싶어요. 새로운 음식 배우는 걸 좋아해요.

closing: I'd love to invite you someday! It's so fun to learn about each other's cultures.
closing_ko: 언젠가 꼭 초대하고 싶어요! 서로의 문화를 알아 가는 게 정말 재미있어요.

title: Chatting About Social Media
situation_ko: 친구와 SNS를 얼마나 쓰는지, 어떤 걸 보는지 이야기해요.
ai_role: A friend who uses social media a lot

key_phrases.text: I spend too much time on my phone.
I post once in a while.

questions.q: Do you use social media a lot?
questions.sample: Yes, I spend too much time on my phone, maybe two hours a day.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 휴대폰을 너무 오래 봐요. 하루 두 시간쯤요.

questions.q: Same here! What kind of accounts do you follow?
questions.sample: I follow cooking accounts and travel photographers.

questions.q: Nice! Do you post your own photos?
questions.sample: I post once in a while, usually food or places I visit.
questions.sample_ko: 가끔 올려요, 보통 음식이나 가 본 곳이에요.

questions.q: Has social media ever made you feel bad about yourself?
questions.q_ko: SNS 때문에 기분이 안 좋았던 적 있어요?
questions.sample: Sometimes. Everyone looks so happy, and I feel jealous.
questions.sample_ko: 가끔요. 모두 너무 행복해 보여서 부러워요.

questions.q: I know that feeling. Have you ever taken a break from it?
questions.q_ko: 그 기분 알아요. SNS를 쉬어 본 적 있어요?
questions.sample: Yes, I stopped for one week last year. It felt very peaceful.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 작년에 일주일 쉬었어요. 정말 평화로웠어요.

closing: Maybe I should try that too. Thanks for sharing your thoughts!
closing_ko: 저도 한번 해 봐야겠어요. 생각을 나눠 줘서 고마워요!

title: Sharing Travel Stories
situation_ko: 최근 다녀온 여행에 대해 친구에게 이야기해요.
ai_role: A friend curious about your trip
user_role: A traveler who just came back

questions.q: Welcome back! How was your trip?
questions.sample: It was amazing! I just got back from Japan.

questions.q: Lucky you! What was the best part?
questions.sample: The best part was the food. I ate so much ramen.
questions.sample_ko: 가장 좋았던 건 음식이야. 라멘을 엄청 먹었어.

questions.q: I'm jealous! Did anything go wrong on the trip?
questions.q_ko: 부럽다! 여행 중에 안 좋은 일은 없었어?
questions.sample: I got lost once, but a kind stranger helped me.
questions.sample_ko: 한 번 길을 잃었는데 친절한 낯선 사람이 도와줬어.

questions.q: That's so sweet. Who did you travel with?
questions.sample: I went with my sister. We had a lot of fun together.

questions.q: Would you recommend it to me?
questions.sample: Definitely. Go in spring if you can. The flowers are beautiful.
questions.sample_ko: 당연하지. 가능하면 봄에 가. 꽃이 아름다워.

closing: I'm adding Japan to my list! Thanks for the great stories.
closing_ko: 일본을 내 목록에 추가해야겠어! 멋진 이야기 고마워.

title: Planning a Group Trip
situation_ko: 친구와 함께 주말 여행을 계획해요.
ai_role: A friend planning a weekend trip with you

key_phrases.text: How about going to the beach?

questions.q: We should plan a weekend trip with the group. Where should we go?
questions.q_ko: 우리 그룹 주말 여행 계획하자. 어디로 갈까?
questions.sample: How about going to the beach? It's relaxing.

questions.q: Good idea! Should we drive or take a train?
questions.q_ko: 좋은 생각이야! 운전해서 갈까, 기차 탈까?
questions.sample: I think the train is better because we can chat on the way.
questions.sample_ko: 기차가 더 좋은 것 같아. 가면서 이야기할 수 있잖아.

questions.q: Okay. What's a good budget for each person?
questions.q_ko: 좋아. 한 사람당 예산이 어느 정도면 좋을까?
questions.sample: Maybe around one hundred fifty thousand won, including the hotel.
questions.sample_ko: 숙소 포함해서 15만 원 정도면 될 것 같아.

questions.q: That works. Who's going to book the hotel?
questions.sample: I'll book it tonight. Then I'll send everyone the details.
questions.sample_ko: 내가 오늘 밤에 예약할게. 그리고 모두에게 정보를 보낼게.

questions.q: Thanks! What activities do you want to do there?
questions.q_ko: 고마워! 거기서 어떤 활동을 하고 싶어?
questions.sample: I'd like to walk on the beach and eat fresh seafood.
questions.sample_ko: 해변을 걷고 신선한 해산물을 먹고 싶어.

closing: This is going to be so much fun! Let's tell the others tonight.
closing_ko: 정말 재미있겠다! 오늘 밤에 다른 친구들에게 말하자.

title: Meeting a Friend's Friend
situation_ko: 친구가 소개해 준 사람과 처음으로 이야기해요.
user_role: Someone meeting them for the first time

key_phrases.text: I've heard a lot about you.
What do you do for fun?

questions.q: Hi! You must be Soyeon's friend. I've heard a lot about you!
questions.q_ko: 안녕하세요! 소연 씨 친구분이시죠. 얘기 많이 들었어요!
questions.sample: Nice to meet you! I've heard a lot about you too. Good things only!
questions.sample_ko: 만나서 반가워요! 저도 얘기 많이 들었어요. 좋은 얘기만요!

questions.q: Ha, thanks! How did you two meet?
questions.q_ko: 하하, 고마워요! 두 분은 어떻게 만났어요?
questions.sample: We met through work a few years ago, and we became close.
questions.sample_ko: 몇 년 전에 일로 만났고, 가까워졌어요.

questions.q: That's nice. What kind of work do you do?
questions.sample: I'm a software developer. I build apps for a small company.
questions.sample_ko: 소프트웨어 개발자예요. 작은 회사에서 앱을 만들어요.

questions.q: Cool! What do you do for fun when you're not working?
questions.q_ko: 멋지네요! 일 안 할 땐 재미로 뭐 하세요?
questions.sample: I like playing badminton and trying new restaurants.
questions.sample_ko: 배드민턴 치는 거랑 새 식당 가는 걸 좋아해요.

questions.q: I love badminton too! Do you want to play together sometime?
questions.q_ko: 저도 배드민턴 좋아해요! 언제 같이 칠래요?
questions.sample: Sure! I usually play on Saturday mornings.
questions.sample_ko: 좋아요! 저는 보통 토요일 아침에 쳐요.

closing: Great, let's do it! It's so nice to make a new friend.
closing_ko: 좋아요, 해요! 새 친구를 사귀게 되어 정말 좋아요.

title: Congratulating on a Promotion
situation_ko: 승진한 동료에게 축하 인사를 건네고 이야기를 나눠요.
ai_role: A coworker who was just promoted

questions.q: I have some news. I got promoted today!
questions.sample: That's wonderful! Congratulations! You totally deserve it.
questions.sample_ko: 정말 멋져요! 축하해요! 충분히 그럴 자격 있어요.

questions.q: Thank you so much! I'm excited but also a little nervous.
questions.sample: That's natural. What will your new responsibilities be?

questions.q: I'll lead a small team and manage projects. It's new for me.
questions.q_ko: 작은 팀을 이끌고 프로젝트를 관리해요. 저한텐 처음이에요.
questions.sample: You're a great communicator, so I'm sure you'll do well.

questions.q: That means a lot. Can I ask you for advice sometimes?
questions.q_ko: 큰 힘이 돼요. 가끔 조언을 구해도 될까요?
questions.sample: Of course! I'm always happy to help.

questions.q: Thanks! How should we celebrate?
questions.sample: Let's go to dinner after work on Friday. My treat!
questions.sample_ko: 금요일 퇴근 후에 저녁 먹어요. 제가 살게요!

closing: You're the best. I'll make a reservation. Thanks for your support!
closing_ko: 최고예요. 제가 예약할게요. 응원해 줘서 고마워요!

title: Talking About Favorite Movies
situation_ko: 영화를 좋아하는 친구와 취향을 이야기해요.

key_phrases.text: I'm a big fan of comedies.

questions.q: What kind of movies do you like?
questions.sample: I'm a big fan of comedies, but I also like romance.

questions.q: Nice! What's the best movie you've seen recently?
questions.q_ko: 좋네요! 최근에 본 가장 좋은 영화가 뭐예요?
questions.sample: I saw a Korean drama movie last month. It made me cry.
questions.sample_ko: 지난달에 한국 드라마 영화를 봤어요. 보다가 울었어요.

questions.q: Oh, what was it about?
questions.sample: It was about a father and his daughter. It was very touching.

questions.q: I'll have to watch it. Do you prefer watching at the cinema or at home?
questions.q_ko: 저도 봐야겠어요. 영화관이 좋아요, 집이 좋아요?
questions.sample: I prefer home, because I can eat snacks and relax.
questions.sample_ko: 집이 좋아요. 간식 먹으면서 편하게 볼 수 있으니까요.

questions.q: Is there a movie you've watched more than once?
questions.q_ko: 두 번 이상 본 영화가 있어요?
questions.sample: Yes, I've seen one animated movie three times.
questions.sample_ko: 네, 애니메이션 영화 하나는 세 번 봤어요.

closing: Now I want a movie night! Let's pick one together this weekend.
closing_ko: 이제 영화의 밤이 하고 싶네요! 이번 주말에 같이 골라요.

title: Roommate Chat
situation_ko: 새 룸메이트와 함께 사는 규칙을 이야기해요.

key_phrases.text: I usually go to bed early.
Please let me know if it bothers you.

questions.q: Hey, since we're going to live together, can we talk about a few things? What time do you usually go to bed?
questions.q_ko: 우리 같이 살 거니까 몇 가지 이야기해도 될까요? 보통 몇 시에 자요?
questions.sample: I usually go to bed around eleven. I'm a morning person.

questions.q: Good to know. Do you mind if I have friends over sometimes?
questions.q_ko: 알겠어요. 가끔 친구들이 놀러 와도 괜찮아요?
questions.sample: That's fine, but please tell me in advance and keep it quiet.
questions.sample_ko: 괜찮은데 미리 말해 주고 조용히 해 주세요.

questions.q: Of course. How should we share the cleaning?
questions.sample: Maybe we can take turns every week. I'll start with the kitchen.
questions.sample_ko: 매주 번갈아 하면 어때요? 제가 주방부터 할게요.

questions.q: Sounds fair. Do you cook a lot?
questions.sample: Yes, I cook most nights. You're welcome to join me sometimes.
